items.statement: Management aims for consistent double-digit revenue growth in the medium term
items.quote: Our endeavor in the medium term is, you know, as I'd indicated to some other participant was that we want to get to a consistent double-digit revenue growth.

items.statement: ERP implementation went live on April 1 with zero business disruption
items.quote: In fact, kudos to the team. There has been zero disruption on that front.

items.statement: Floats reached almost mid-single-digit contribution with 16,000 pairs average weekly sales
items.quote: Floats continues to power at a very high level, and now it's reached almost mid-single-digit contribution, almost doubling for the quarter. 16,000 pairs average weekly sales

items.statement: Gross margin protected reasonably well despite tough trading conditions
items.quote: The last chart on margins, gross margin was protected reasonably well, I would say during this quarter, despite the tough trading conditions

items.statement: No price increases for almost five to six quarters since mid-second half of FY22-23
items.quote: We have refrained from price increases now for the almost five quarters or a little more, maybe six quarters now. So middle of, let's say, second half of '22, '23.

items.statement: Demand improved from January to March but sustainability unclear; optimistic medium term
items.quote: we did see an improvement during the quarter from a Jan which was actually much worse, but to March which was a little better, but still not giving us complete clarity

items.statement: Premium brands (Hush Puppies, Power, Nordstar, Comfit) contribute ~40% of turnover; premium defined as >Rs2,000 MRP
items.quote: They will cumulatively account for almost something like 40% of our turnover.

items.statement: Mass segment below Rs700 MRP remains sensitive; distribution business still a drag on growth
items.quote: the mass segment, which is an MRP, which is below INR700, consumers are extremely sensitive to it. And that did create its own, how do you say, struggle from a consumption point of view

items.statement: Marketing spend at ~260 bps for FY24; H2 run rate to continue in FY25 with potential increase
items.quote: The second half run rate. Yes, broadly ballpark, yes, we will run with that run rate. And in fact, we might want to invest a little more.

items.statement: Franchise store additions to dominate at 80-20 ratio vs COCO; target 40 doors per quarter run rate
items.quote: We will have predominant franchise store additions, which is in the ratio of 80-20. Does that answer your question?

items.statement: Industry growth estimated at GDP plus inflation (~low double-digits); aim to edge ahead of industry
items.quote: The industry growth estimates based on various inputs that we get, but I mean, nominally speaking, it should be GDP growth plus the inflation, minimal, and that works out to almost low-double digits in those lines.

items.statement: Distillery EBITDA margin for FY24 was 12%, up from 9% in FY23, but would have been 16-17% without policy change restricting ethanol diversion.
items.quote: So this impacted our overall distillery EBITDA margin on a full year basis, probably at around 12%. Wh ile this has improved from FY'23 of 9%, if there was perhaps no change in the policy framework, the EBITDA margins would have been closer to 16% and perhaps on track to move closer to 20

items.statement: Aspiration to build FMCG business with late single-digit EBITDA margin over next 5 years on substantially larger scale.
items.quote: At least towards the end of the decade, we want to have a business with the late single digit EBITA and a business which is substantially larger than what it is today.

items.statement: Value-added FMCG products target gross margins north of 35%; staples have lower gross margins but managed for contribution targets.
items.quote: So, there you will aspire for gross margins north of 35% because that would be important. On the bare bones, on the straight, which is your dal, rice, etcetera, you would have substantially lesser gross margins because these are more scale products.

items.statement: Distillery expansion of 165 KLPD at Haliyal and Nellikuppam reached greater degree of completion and will operate in full stream by Q1 FY25.
items.quote: During the year, expansion in distillery of 165 KLPD in Haliyal and Nellikuppam had reached greater degree of completion and will operate in full stream by Q1 of FY25.

items.statement: Policy uncertainty on ethanol diversion and sugar exports persists; global sugar prices in late teens per pound, well below 27 cents six to nine months ago.
items.quote: But more importantly, at least it's our view, that the sugar MSP could be certainly relooked at. The MSP has stayed at INR31 a kilo, while the FRP has moved up on a year-on-year basis for a number of years.

items.statement: Nutraceuticals division under strategic review; open to alliances for value creation; certification issues in Europe expected to resolve soon.
items.quote: As I said, nutra is under strategic review and we're always going to be open to looking at alliances which are going to create value for the business. So, I think that's kind of where we are right now.

items.statement: Standalone debt ~INR1,000 cr (INR300 cr long-term for projects, INR750 cr short-term for inventory); expected to reduce by September.
items.quote: Because if you look at the composition of the debt, out of INR1000 crores, INR300 crores is long-term in nature, which is for the projects which are underway and is getting commercialized in a quarter. So, as far as the short-term is concerned, it is about INR750 crores or so, and this majorly is on account of inventory increase, compared to the 31st March 2023. So, the debt is stretched around IN

items.statement: Retail sales 28% of sugar volume; value-added portfolio (Amrit, jaggery) growing; staples launched in TN, AP, Telangana, Karnataka; target half a million outlets in 2-3 years.
items.quote: I think in a couple of years' time, really getting closer to half a million would be the near to medium-term objectives which we have.

items.statement: Refinery turned cash profitable: Q4 revenue INR899 cr, positive EBITDA INR56 cr, PBT before exceptional INR37 cr; volume up 16%, spread improved $10 PMT, cost down $3 PMT.
items.quote: Refinery business volume has grown by 16% and the spread also has improved about $10 PMT and cost reduced by $3 PMT and this has resulted in the refinery posting a cash profit of INR12 crores.

items.statement: Brand (A&P) spend FY24 INR35-40 cr; will increase as value-added products scale with distribution.
items.quote: So, to give you perspective, it sits within the mother business right now. And brand expenditure, if you look at FY '24, is about INR35-INR40 CR in total.

items.statement: Staples sourcing initially through market; farmer network leverage possible in 4-6 years after brand stabilizes and gains volume.
items.quote: Initially, it is going to be disordered sourcing and we have to identify the right sources in the market and get the right product as per the specifications, living up to the brand standards. And what you talk about as a farmer network leveraging will happen over a period of time, say maybe the next 4-6 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 is 525-560 bps above FY24 level
items.quote: we're looking at a margin outlook for fiscal 25 guiding in the range of 525 north to 550, 560. And on that, if you look at the overall EBITDA margin, we're expecting a jump in EBITDA margin from the full year of fiscal 24.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY25 is 5-10%
items.quote: I believe our guidance going forward between 5% and 10% growth is at the back of gradually exiting but largely focusing on good quality customers going deeper but keeping our focus on EBITDA growth from where we are at this time.

items.statement: Targeting 10% operating margin over next couple of years
items.quote: Our goal is to reach about 10% operating margin, and we are clearly focused over the next couple of years to get there.

items.statement: Total order backlog is $470 million as of March 2024, down from $490 million in December 2023
items.quote: Just to highlight, on an order backlog across our various solutions and services and projects is US $470 million as on March 24 as against an order backlog of US $490 million as in December 23.

items.statement: Pipeline is close to $2 billion, strong in networking and data center solutions
items.quote: And our pipeline, of course is very strong, specifically in our networking and our data center solutions business. It's close to $2 billion at this time.

items.statement: Data center capacity expected to nearly double from 17 GW to 35 GW over next 5-7 years
items.quote: The current requirement for a data center over the next several years, 5-7 years, is for the current capacity of data center will increase from the current 17 gigawatts to about 35 gigawatts.

items.statement: Actively working with three of five major hyperscalers on data center projects
items.quote: Currently, we are working on active projects with three out of the five major hyperscalers.

items.statement: Pivoting away from long-tail customers (90% revenue from top 50) to focus on top 250-300 accounts
items.quote: We are reorganizing ourselves to be able to serve large logos, Fortune 500 customers across enterprise and across hyperscalers, data center market and so on and so forth. Now, the larger customers have a little longer lead time to work on.

items.statement: Data center revenue grew from ~$15-20M three years ago to $110-115M in FY24 (~20% YoY growth)
items.quote: About three years ago, our revenue from the data center was about $15 million or $20 million. And in fiscal '22, we did about $70 -odd million. In fiscal 23, we did about $90 -odd million. The year that we exited, we've done about $110 million-$115 million in that range.

items.statement: TPS business contributes 12-13% of revenue, expected to remain in that range
items.quote: So, the TPS business contributes currently about between 12% and 13%. We expect the contribution to remain in that range going forward.

items.statement: Center of Excellence in Bangalore matured after 2 years of investment, driving productivity gains
items.quote: The second of course, our ability now to have our Center of Excellence in India support us because it's mature now we put the investment for the last 2 years time. So, we are able to get better productivity from our Center of Excellence in India that allows us to have better margin.

items.statement: Higher US interest costs caused slight miss on FY24 profitability target
items.quote: Our strong operating performance has led to increased profitability despite higher interest costs due to the interest rate environment in US. However, these high interest costs which we have incurred in fiscal year have caused us to slightly miss our profitability target and t he guidance for

items.statement: Customer decision-making delays affected short-term revenue growth and order bookings
items.quote: There was some shrinkage when compared to December 23 order backlog due to slow decision making on project orders and consistent execution of projects at our end on a quarter -on-quarter basis led to lower than anticipated order bookings.

items.statement: No active inorganic pipeline but will pursue accretive opportunities for market depth or portfolio expansion
items.quote: We will continue to look at inorganic opportunities, but we want to be economically accretive for us and not be emotional about that. So currently, we do not have an active pipeline, but as I said, we will continue to look at if it makes sense.

items.statement: India revenue contribution expected to stay at 6-7% while exploring data center and large infrastructure opportunities
items.quote: From a percentage perspective as we grow, I do not see a massive change in terms of contribution of revenue of 6%, 7% as we scale up. But clearly, we see growth as well in that market, most specifically exploring data center or supporting other large-scale infrastructure that is getting built.

items.statement: Expect 50% to 60% growth on pharma side in current year
items.quote: we're looking at, at the moment, 50% to 60% growth on the pharma side in the current year as well.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve year-on-year over next two to three years
items.quote: yes, we expect margins to go up and in the next two to three years, you will see margins year-on-year improving

items.statement: No substantial capex planned for FY25; focus on improving utilization
items.quote: We are not looking at any substantial capex as of now as we speak. There will be some small capexes which we will be doing. But our focus is going to be on improving utilization level

items.statement: Additional capex of $15-20 million over next 6-7 years to scale from 25-30M to 60-70M devices
items.quote: I think the additional capex in the range of, I would say, somewhere in the range of between $15 and $20 million will be -- is what we're looking at additional capex

items.statement: Confirmed orders from three customers in Q4 FY24: two for Semaglutide, one for Lanreotide
items.quote: In the Healthcare division, we have received confirmed business orders from three customers, two for Semaglutide and one for Lanreotide in the last quarter.

items.statement: Total ongoing projects across all molecules: 20 to 23
items.quote: Sanjay Shah: Yes, I'd say about 20 to 23.

items.statement: Auto injector projects: 4; balance are pen injectors
items.quote: So auto injectors, we have a total of four projects and balance are on pen injectors.

items.statement: Proprietary devices share increased from 10% to 30-40% of volumes over 3 years
items.quote: contract manufacturing, for example, is 3 years ago, contract manufacturing was 90% and proprietary devices were 10%. I'd say today, the split would be somewhere 70%-30% or 60%-40%.

items.statement: Expect US/EU approvals for injection pen platforms in current financial year before end of calendar year
items.quote: We're very confident that these approvals will come in, in the current financial year before the end of this calendar year.

items.statement: Commercial supplies for Teriparatide (Axiom pen) started; Liraglutide commercial supplies expected in current year
items.quote: we started commercial supplies for Teriparatide, which is our Axiom pen. And we're starting -- we are looking at starting some commercial supplies of our Liraglutide pen as well in the current year

items.statement: Semaglutide RoW market launches targeted for calendar 2026 (FY27)
items.quote: most of our customers would be targeting '26, which is basically FY'27, but calendar '26 launch in these markets.

items.statement: Pen/device volumes: 11-12 million in FY24; expect 17-18 million in FY25 (15-16% growth)
items.quote: We're looking at -- like I said, we're looking at about 15%, 16% growth. So, I anticipate somewhere around to 17 million to 18 million pens in the clinical devices in the current year.

items.statement: No significantly adverse USFDA comments received on device-related queries
items.quote: Have we have received any significantly adverse comments? No. We have not yet received any significantly adverse comments that I'm aware of.

items.statement: GLP-1 pens give higher margins than insulin; not 3-4x difference
items.quote: GLP-1 will certainly give you higher margins than insulin. I don't think it's going to be 3, 4x.

items.statement: Carbon Steel business near EBITDA breakeven; expect breakeven in current year
items.quote: EBITDA level, I would say we have not broken even, but we are at a very borderline thing, and we should be able to breakeven in the current year.

items.statement: Expects better situation in second half of FY25 if anti-dumping duty comes into play by 1st October
items.quote: We are doing our best and in case the duty comes into play by 1st of October, which is what we are expecting, the situation in second half could be better from that perspective.

items.statement: Planning to spend over INR100 crores in FY25 on balancing equipment, captive solar-wind hybrid, and furnace rebuild preparation
items.quote: See, this year, we are planning to spend over INR100 crores in capex and this is for balancing equipment, which is required now because the type of glass, which is being demanded by the customers in order to make that to manufacture that we need to spend this capex.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR1,100-plus crores for capacity expansion put on hold pending duty structure visibility
items.quote: So we decided purposely to wait for right duty structure to be in place before we can move into this large project of say INR1,100-plus crores.

items.statement: Filing draft letter of offer to SEBI for rights issue; Board approved raising up to INR750 crores via equity, convertible securities, warrants, QIP, or preferential issue
items.quote: Finally, the company is filing around to file the draft letter of offer to SEBI to raise funds by a rights issue of equity shares. The proceeds will be utilized mainly to reduce the debt for the Indian operations as well as at the operating subsidiaries. The Board has also approved further raising of funds through the issuance of instruments of security, including equity shares or any other securi

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin declined to 12.1% from 25.7% in FY23 due to dumping and price erosion
items.quote: Consequently, the EBITDA during financial year 2024 was INR18.93 crores, corresponding to a margin of 12.1%, which was a steep decline compared to an EBITDA margin of 25.7% in the previous financial year.

items.statement: Average selling price fell 20.2% to INR109 per mm per sqm in FY24; Q4 FY24 price fell 25.6% YoY to INR98.8 per mm per sqm
items.value: INR109 per millimeter per square meter
items.quote: Average selling prices during the year were about INR109 per millimeter per square meter, a serious decline of 20.2% as compared to INR136.5 per millimeter per square meter during the previous year.

items.statement: Import freight rates from China to India rose from $700 to $3,200, improving landed cost of imports and domestic realizations
items.quote: The import freight rate into India from China has gone up from about $700 to about $3,200. And therefore, this may have a positive impact on our selling prices.

items.statement: Indian solar installations grew to 15 GW in FY24 from 12.8 GW; ALMM implementation from 1 April 2024 driving domestic module manufacturing and glass demand
items.quote: Firstly, solar installations in India last year were 15 gigawatts, an impressive growth over the previous year's insta llations of 12.8 gigawatts. Secondly, after some hesitant steps, the government has firmly implemented the ALMM mechanism on 1st April 2024, which mandates use of only ALMM -certified modules in the projects being installed in India

items.statement: 2mm glass now 20-25% of portfolio, expected to reach 60-65% by end of FY25; large-format glass now 90% of module manufacturer requirements
items.quote: This 2-millimeter glass is now almost 20% - 25% of our portfolio and which will soon become almost 60%- 65% by end of this year. So this is very much the requirement now. And also, the other thing, what we have done is to come up quickly is the large-format glass because there's a demand for larger module which started to become very popular. We have been abl e to introduce the large size of glass

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty applications accepted by DGTR; investigation ongoing, decisions expected in 5-6 months; customs duty exemption extended to 30 September 2024
items.quote: Our applications for DGTR in this regard have been prima facie accepted and already taken up for investigation. The government is now fully seized of the matter, and satisfactory decisions are expected to follow, perhaps in the next 5, 6 months.

items.statement: German subsidiary GMV resumed full production from mid-March 2024 after order cancellations in H2 FY24; export inquiries improving
items.quote: As informed in the last call, the company had temporarily slowed down production due to paucity of orders. Meanwhile, GMV has made inroads in other export markets to fill the gap created by a low domestic demand and has been able to resume full production from the middle of March this year.

items.statement: Negotiating additional solar-wind hybrid captive power plant with expected commissioning in H1 FY26
items.quote: We are negotiating an additional color placement hybrid drop at with expected commissioning during first half of financial year 2025, '26. This will not only save cost for us but will also enable us to meet a major portion of our demand for electricity from captive sources of renewable energy.

items.statement: GMV in Germany restarted second production line in late March 2024 and continues to receive enough export and domestic orders to run both lines fully
items.quote: Sometime in the last week of March, we got enough orders to start the second production line. And fortunately, we are continuing to get orders, export orders, domestic orders enough to continue to use both production lines fully.

items.statement: US demand starting in small way, expected to ramp up later in 2024 as plants start volume production, raising export demand from India
items.quote: Demand in the U.S.A. has started in a small way. We expect this to go up in the later part of this year as some of plants start volume production and ramp up operations. This will raise export demand from India.

items.statement: Company has batch house ready for 2,000 tons/day and electrical infrastructure in place, enabling faster furnace commissioning (14-24 months) if expansion approved
items.quote: We have a batch house. It's a very expensive component of the entire solar glass manufacturing plant, which is up and ready already for 2,000 tons. So if we set up another furnace, we do not need to spend any money on the batch house. We'll be saving money on the capital. The second thing, the entire electrical installation is already ready with us.

items.statement: Expect capacity utilization around 75% on 100,000-ton capacity in FY25, could reach 80% if market improves
items.quote: Yes, in the region of 75%, more like 75%. It could go to 80% if the market picks up a little bit. But at this moment, I'll probably say 75%.

items.quote: So for the anode, so at least the overall capex for the project that we are envisaging is between INR1,600 crores and INR1,800 crores depending on the final selection of technology, et cetera, how much power we need to take, how much -- we are still kind of contemplating between 48-kilometer 250 kVA line or whether we can make do with a 133 kVA line, that changes the entire dynamics. items.quote: We hope to see marginal improvement in steel production towards second half of 2024, which should result in increase in demand of electrodes. items.quote: See, if you -- in the portion of our business, it's roughly, I would say, 70% to 75% of UHP and balance of HP grade electrodes -- I mean, non-UHP electrodes.

items.statement: Next 2-3 quarters may see margins under pressure; demand recovery hoped for H2 2024 onwards
items.quote: The next 2, 3 quarters may see margins remaining under some pressure but we are hoping that the demand will come back sometime in second half of 2024 onwards and we're now fully equipped to take advantage of our expanded capacity.

items.quote: So like we mentioned earlier, around 700 -- arou nd INR80 crores of it has already been funded by HEG in terms of the land and the basic civil work that have started. items.quote: So TACC value will be around INR292 crores, as Puneet said. Puneet Anand: Riju Jhunjhunwala: For INR80 crores of money that HEG has put in today. It's a 100% subsidiary of HEG. And the new Greentech company will own 100% of TACC. It will not be 29%, it will 100% of TACC, the new Greentech company

items.quote: No. See, currently, there is no shortage. There's no problem at all. As the electrode prices have dropped in the last 6, 7 quarters, so have been needle coke prices dropped. So if you are talking about the margin being the difference of the selling price of electrode versus the buying price of needle coke, it hasn't changed much. It has kept pace with the drop in the electrode prices. And this is

items.statement: Global graphite electrode demand expected to grow 150,000-200,000 tons by 2030 (ex-China) from current 500,000-550,000 tons; no new Western capacity announced
items.quote: As we have said in our earlier calls, we expect graphite demand to increase gradually by around 150,000 to 200,000 tons by 2033 -- 2030, which is a significant increase over current demand of about 500,000 to 550,000 tons, excluding China. items.statement: HEG Graphite to retain 20MW Tawa hydro power and cash for dividend, expansion leftovers, safety capital; Greentech gets BEL 49%, TACC 100%, RePlus
items.quote: One will be the HEG Graphite company, which will have the HEG Limited, which is 100,000 tons graphite plant and the captive 20-megawatt power – Tawa hydroelectric power units and enough cash in its balance sheet to fund dividend for this year and the leftovers from the expansion and some kind of safety capital as we might call it. And the leftover company would be renamed to, let's say, HEG Greent

items.statement: Excluding smart meters, revenue growth expected at 18-23% in FY25; smart meter sales over and above that
items.quote: Excluding the smart meters, we expect to grow anywhere between 18% and 23% in the coming year. Smart meter business sales will be over and above that.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 10.5-11% for FY25, up ~100 bps from current level
items.quote: EBITDA margins, we have improved to around 70 basis points this year compared to last year. So we expect this to go up by another 1 percentage point in the coming year.

items.statement: Smart meter revenue expected at INR400-500 crore in FY25 if 50% capacity utilization achieved
items.quote: But my expectation is that I think at least 50% capacity utilization should be achieved. So I expect that we should be able to reach at least INR400 crores to INR500 crores revenue in the smart maker business if everything goes well from now.

items.statement: Industrial Switchgear growth expected at 22-23%, Wire & Cable at 18-20%, Building Products at ~40% in FY25
items.quote: industry switched gear business should be growing at around 22%- 23% this year. Copper wire and cable business should be growing b etween 18% and 20%. A building segment, we are expecting that it will grow by around 40

items.statement: Maintenance capex of INR17-20 crore for FY25; smart meter capex ~70% done, balance in FY25
items.quote: I think there's no major capex because we have done our smart meter capex almost 70% this year. So the balance will be done next year. Other than this, there is no major capex, and we will be doing the maintenance capex of approximately INR17 crores-INR20 crores.

items.statement: Smart meter plant total capex ~INR40 crore for 40 lakh capacity; doubling to 80 lakh would need another INR40 crore
items.quote: For 40 lakh units, I mean the entire plant is installed and completed our total capex will be closer around INR40 crores.

items.statement: Smart meter trial production underway; commercial production expected by June-July once orders received
items.quote: As I said, I think the trial production is underway. Commercial production, we are ready once the orders come in. So we should in my opinion, I assess that I think by June, July, we should be getting some orders and starting the commercial products.

items.statement: Smart meter EBITDA margin expected at 12-15% in first year, targeting ~15% at steady state
items.quote: But I'm optimistic, if we are able to do this first year, and the EBITDA margin is not 15 %, I think definitely, it will be between 12% and 15% for the first year.

items.statement: EV charger business targets 18-20% EBITDA margin if technology and demand materialize
items.quote: We actually projected an EBITDA margin close to 18% to 20% if everything goes well in the charger business.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on global markets; mega shift to clean energy and India infrastructure/digitalization driving growth
items.quote: We are witnessing a mega shift towards clean energy on a global scale, which is posting significant investments in renewable energy projects across the world. This persists a compelling opportunity for Salzer to leverage our expertise and offerings in the renewable energy sector, driving growth and innovation in this space.

items.statement: Single-phase smart meter BIS certified; three-phase BIS expected by end of June; factory 80% installed, trial production started
items.quote: We are right now developed Single Phase and Three-Phase. Single Phase we have got the BIS certificate already Three Phases, we will get the BIS certificate by end of June.

items.statement: EV charger failed ARAI communication test due to DIN vs ISO standard mismatch; software fix underway, retest timeline uncertain
items.quote: Out of the total of 14 different tests that the charges have to undergo at ARAI, we have passed 13 tests. However, in the one last test, which is the communication test, the chargers have failed.

items.statement: Smart meter deployment slowed by AMISP integration issues, not public resistance; 5-7 year timeline for 25 crore meter rollout
items.quote: Deployment is low at this moment is not because of the resistance from the general p ublic, but it's because of the issues that we because the MSPs have today, because of supply of metered, integrating the meters with software and ensuring that the service levels are at 99% plus

items.statement: Kaycee Industries targets 20% growth to reach INR100 crore revenue in 3 years while maintaining ~9% PAT margin
items.quote: Our target is to grow at around 20% in the c urrent year. And then reach INR 100 crores in the next at least 3 years. Yes, that's the aim and focus we are trying to get

items.statement: Promoter holding increased from 32% to 38%; target to reach close to 40% in coming years
items.quote: I think we have increased from 32% to 38% as of now. And I think this for this year, I think this is going to be the limit. However, I think as promoters, we will be comfortable and looking at see this further to c lose to 40

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle at 145-150 days (90 inventory, 90 debtor, 32 creditor); target to reduce to ~120 days
items.quote: Cash conversion cycle currently is at 145 days to 150 days with 90 inventory days and 90 debtor days and creditor days is around 32. That's our current cash conversion. We have been consistent in FY '23 is the same level and we at the same level we wanted to improve, but we couldn't. Our ultimate goal is to have cash conversion cycle of around 120 per days net working capital days.

items.statement: Target 40% VAP contribution at INR6,000 crore revenue ambition
