items.quote: The aim is to add 1,000 plus keys over the next two years, primarily as I said, driven by inorganic strategy.

items.statement: Normative capex including refurbishment is ~INR 100 crores for FY25; significant capex for 300-key expansion atop Grand Hyatt Mumbai will occur in FY26 funded by internal accruals.
items.quote: So, CAPEX, we are talking about normative CAPEX, including refurb of INR 100 crores. So, it is not significant CAPEX. Most of it is already expended last year. And fresh CAPEX is going to be roughly INR 100 crores.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion of 300 keys atop Grand Hyatt Mumbai to start in FY26 and complete in 18 months by FY27.
items.quote: So, it will start by FY '26, and it should be complete by FY '27.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margins maintained at 45.4% (Juniper) and 35.5% (Chartered) in FY24; management expects margin expansion in FY25 driven by ARR flow-through and new revenue streams.
items.quote: On the margins, as I said, ARRs are a high flow through. So, that would be a positive influencer for our operating margins.

items.statement: ARR growth outperformed micro markets: Mumbai +9% vs market +5.5%, Delhi +22% vs market +14.6% (YTD March); airline crew rates increased ~48% in Delhi and Mumbai.
items.quote: For instance, Mumbai ARR grew 5.5% and this is not just the Comp-set, this is the broader market I am talking about. And we grew at above 9% in Mumbai year-to-date. And as far as Delhi is concerned, it was a 14.6% growth and for Juniper it was (+22%).

items.statement: Management sees $100 (Rs.8,500) ARR headroom to reach $250 minimum target from current ~$150 levels.
items.quote: Even with the ARRs the way they are, we're still at about $150 . Reasonably, the $250 is the minimum that we believe that we should be able to achieve. So , there is a still $100 headroom, which is about Rs.8,500 available to us.

items.statement: Demand expected to outstrip supply in luxury/upper upscale segments for considerable future; no significant supply increases expected in key markets (Mumbai, Delhi, Ahmedabad) for 2-5 years.
items.quote: No significant supply increases are expected in our markets. So, the demand will continue to outstrip the supplies , as also confirmed by many of the hotel sector experts.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt Mumbai refurbishment of 380 rooms by end-September 2024 to target transient guests; new 49,655 sq ft 'Showroom' banquet hall operational in FY25; second banquet hall in Ahmedabad by Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Four floors that is about 380 rooms will be refurbished and ready in operation by Q2 of 2024 which is basically in three months by September, 380 rooms will be fully refurbished for this transient high paying customer.

items.statement: Weekend MICE and social event strategy at Grand Hyatt Mumbai using two banquet halls to drive occupancy above 80-82% market taper levels.
items.quote: So, if you see what will happen is , we will be able to drive additional occupancy , additional room nights over the weekend, which will add to our occupancy rate.

items.statement: Delhi Aerocity development adding 6.3M sq ft retail/commercial by 2027; next hotels in Aerocity ~2 years out, providing clear runway for Juniper's Delhi asset.
items.quote: In recent publications we have read and we have come to know that the Delhi International Airport, that Aerocity is actually going to go through a further enhancement; 6.3 million square feet of space is being added by 2027.

items.statement: IPO raised INR 1,800 crores; INR 1,400 crores used for debt repayment by March 2024, remaining INR 100 crores underway to meet INR 1,500 crores IPO object; INR 330 crores in deposits for balance debt paydown and growth capital.
items.quote: We have raised INR 1,800 crores in the IPO, pure growth capital and we have utilized 1,400 crores as of March'24 to repay debt and significantly strengthen our balance sheet and the consequent ratios.

items.statement: Inorganic acquisitions may involve some debt but management commits to not exceeding 2-2.25x debt-to-EBITDA going forward.
items.quote: But at any point in time, going forward, we believe that we will not exceed debt-to-EBITDA of 2 to 2.25.

items.statement: Net bank debt-to-EBITDA reduced to 0.7x from 5.7x; INR 160 crores annual interest savings from debt paydown; JP Morgan NCDs replaced with ICICI loan at 2% lower rate (9%).
items.quote: Net bank debt-to-EBITDA going down to 0.7 from 5.7 x and a significant saving in interest cost which is INR 160 crores which will be as a result of the debt pay down that we have actually paid out.

items.statement: Room revenue ~48-49% of total, F&B ~30% (banqueting-driven); serviced apartments benefiting from FDI/expatriate demand in Delhi and Mumbai.
items.quote: The room revenue is 48%-49% and your F&B has been maintained at around 30%.

items.statement: Firmly on track to achieve target of double-digit revenue growth with 20% EBITDA margin
items.quote: I'm happy to report that we are firmly on track to achieve our target of double-digit revenue growth with 20% margin.

items.statement: Path to achieving double-digit growth is on track with multiple drivers
items.quote: With all of these drivers moving in the right direction, the path to achieving double-digit growth is on track.

items.statement: Firmly on track to deliver 20% margin through Europe restructuring, mix improvement, price management and cost optimization
items.quote: We are firmly on track to deliver 20% margin through initiatives like Europe restructuring, mixed improvement, active price management and cost optimization.

items.statement: Europe restructuring to achieve mid-teens margins with benefits starting this year
items.quote: These efforts are geared towards achieving mid-teens margins in the near future with benefits expected to start accruing from this year itself.

items.statement: Brazil is EBITDA margin-accretive to total business in Q4
items.quote: In Q4, Brazil is EBITDA margin-accretive to the to tal business. It is margin-accretive to the total business

items.statement: Americas margins representative of steady state business and should maintain or improve
items.quote: Americas has had an organic quarter. So the margins are representative of the steady state business. We have improved our performance in Americas.

items.statement: Capex in line with amortization at Rs.374 crores; slightly higher due to Brazil spends of Rs.70-75 crores
items.quote: We have always maintained that our CAPEX will be in line with our overall amortization at about Rs. 374 crores this year. The CAPEX is slightly higher because of the Brazil spends. I think we spent about Rs. 70-75 crores additionally this year on Brazil

items.statement: Future capex in line with amortization excluding M&A or Greenfield; sufficient for growth and maintenance
items.quote: Without M&A or a Greenfield, our CAPEX will be in line with our am ortization and that are sufficient to fund our both growth as well as maintenance CAPEX

items.statement: Brazil Greenfield fulfilled 100% anchor customer demand; receiving orders from MNC and local customers
items.quote: We have now fulfilled 100% demand of our anchor customer and have received orders from both other MNC as well as local customers.

items.statement: Personal care and beyond grew 8.1% vs 5% oral care; now 47% of total business
items.quote: Personal care and beyond grew by 8.1% compared to 5% growth in oral care. Personal care and beyond now contributes to 47% of our total business.

items.statement: Sustainable sales contribution more than doubled to 21%
items.quote: In the past year, we have more than doubled our sustainable sales contribution to 21%.

items.statement: Negative pricing has begun to unwind; slight positive blip in revenue numbers
items.quote: Negative pricing has begun to unwind and therefore you begun to see a slight positive blip in terms of our revenue numbers and this will now slowly start finishing off the negative price.

items.statement: Egypt currency devaluation caused INR 465 million one-off loss; underlying business remains strong
items.quote: This resulted in the Egyptian pound depreciating by approximately 60% against the US dollar, causing, INR 465 million in one-off losses in our books on all US dollar payable.

items.statement: Europe restructuring one-time impact of INR 140 million for headcount optimization and capacity realignment
items.quote: This is leading to a one-time impact of 140 million. These efforts are geared towards achieving mid-teens margins in the near future with benefits expected to start accruing from this year itself.

items.statement: Interest cost at steady state level; similar level expected in FY25 unless M&A or Greenfield
items.quote: The current cost which is in this quarter is the steady state cost and that's the cost that is likely to continue. There would be some up and down depending upon the phasing of cash and hence that's loan debt levels but the cost is representative of the steady state business cost that we have right now.

items.statement: Expect overall margin improvement trend to continue
items.quote: And I expect that at an overall level, this trend will continue.

items.statement: Major expansions: Kashipur ethanol 400 to 500 KLPD, Gorakhpur 110 to 280 KLPD, plus NSU expansion
items.quote: One is the increase in the capacity in Kashipur from 400 KLPD to 500 KLPD, which will be ethanol manufacturing. And for Gorakhpur, we are increasing the capacity from 110 KLPD to 280 KLPD.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of INR 40-50 crore planned for FY26, no major capex firmed up
items.quote: After that, we are not planning for any major CapEx till FY25-26 except the maintenance CapEx, which will be ranging from INR40-50 crore.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 12.9% in FY24 from 11.9% in FY23
items.quote: a healthy EBITDA margin of 12.9%, which is better than before.

items.statement: Imported ethanol weighted average cost rose to 47-48 per litre recently after softening
items.quote: There was softening of imported ethanol prices, which went up to 47-48 or thereabouts in terms of the weighted average that comes to us. And then it has gone up a little bit.

items.statement: Expect full utilization of grain-based ethanol capacity in FY25 and better traction in glycols
items.quote: We expect an overall better year as far as biofuels are concerned because several of these capacities have actually come up this year, and you'll see full utilization of capacity in the current year.

items.statement: Targeting INR 200 crore revenue from new value-added products in FY25, not a formal projection
items.quote: something like in the financial year, something like INR 200 crores from new value-added product is something that we are targeting.

items.statement: RENEW green power supply delayed due to regulatory challenges; no timeline for benefits
items.quote: We've already given an update that there has been a delay as far as RENEW is concerned, and the delay has been explained on account of change of certain regulations or court directions based on which there are certain challenges.

items.statement: Ethanol supply risks include FCI rice availability hiccups and oil marketing companies' offtake
items.quote: Picking up our oil blending companies for various reasons, that could be a potential issue. But other than that, we see that by and large we will be tracking on allocation.

items.statement: No major term loan raising planned for FY25-26 as capex largely completed
items.quote: I don't foresee any major term loan raising from the bank or from the market.

items.statement: Net debt expected to reduce from INR 900 crore to INR 625-650 crore by end FY25 including EPBG repayment
items.quote: My debt is around INR 900 crores as of now, which will come down to INR 650 crores.

items.statement: Volume growth expected in line with industry at 6-7% for FY25
items.quote: Well, the volume growth will be -- should be in the line of -- in line with industry growth. Remember that, today, we are almost running at 80% plus capacity utilization. And our de -bottlenecking is not going to come in before quarter 1. So we shall be in line with the industry growth -- which should be in the region of about 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 estimated at INR100-120 crores including de-bottlenecking and maintenance
items.quote: So next year, next fiscal year, we can say that the total capex will be in the range of INR100 crores, INR120 crores.

items.statement: Clinker de-bottlenecking project to add 200,000 tons cement volume per annum by Q1 CY2025
items.quote: This de -bottlenecking shall result in an additional cement volume of 200,000 tons per annum. And the project is well on its way, and we don't anticipate any delays in this, whatsoever.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton increased 16% YoY to INR659 in FY24 driven by lower input costs
items.quote: Our EBITDA of INR659 per ton is up by 16% year-on-year.

items.statement: Cement prices dropped INR6 per bag in April-May vs Q4 average
items.quote: I think on an average, we have seen a drop of around INR6 per bag.

items.statement: Combined fuel cost at INR1.8 per kilocalorie in Q4, outlook flat
items.quote: It is around INR1.8 per kilocalorie, the combined fuel cost. And on the stepping point with respect to the current prevailing fuel cost, it's almost flat as compared to March.

items.statement: Industry saw double-digit degrowth in April-May, uptick expected in June post-elections
items.quote: So the number that you indicated is right. I think the entire industry, all the major players, the degrowth would be in that range. It will be a double -digit degrowth for April and May, but we are looking at an uptick in June post the election dates are over, because there would be a lot of pent-up demand.

items.statement: Premium cement share target 45% in next 2 years from current 34%
items.quote: So I thin k our ambition is to reach a number of -- around 45% in the next 2 years. So that's what we are gunning for.

items.statement: Power Shield sales at 8,000+ tons/month, targeting 20,000-25,000 tons/month by end of 2025
items.quote: We are about 8,000 tons right now per month. By the end of 2025, we should be clocking anywhere between 20,000 to 25,000 tons.

items.statement: Gujarat expansion delayed awaiting environmental clearance, plant would take 3 years after clearance
items.quote: Obviously, from that -- it will take 3 years' time.

items.statement: Merger with Zuari delayed due to stamp duty issues, unlikely to complete before FY26-27
items.quote: So you are right that even if you start the process in the fiscal year '25, it is not going to complete. It takes time, maybe '26 or '27.

items.statement: Green power target >40% by FY25, currently at 38% including open exchange purchases
items.quote: Our target is to reach more than 40% green power by FY '25.

items.statement: Alternative fuel rate at 8% for FY24, 10% in Q4, targeting further increase subject to availability
items.quote: So in the full year, our TSR for the authentic fuel were 8%, in the March quarter. Because gradually, we are ramping up, so our AFR consumption has been increasing. So in March quarter alone, it was 10%.

items.statement: Clinker capacity to increase from 3.1 to 3.3-3.4 million tons via de-bottlenecking
items.quote: This de-bottlenecking project will increase the clinker capacity. We are trying to get the existing clinker capacity approval from the government, and it will aid or it will increase to clinker capacity to 3.3 million tons or 3.4 million tons.

items.statement: No volume guidance given for Heidelberg specifically, only industry estimate of 6-7%
items.quote: No. At this point in time, no.

items.statement: Expects double-digit sales growth in FY25 over FY24.
items.quote: Regarding the sales outlook for 2024 -'25, we continue to expect double -digit growth over the fiscal year 2023-'24.

items.statement: Aims to hold gross margin at 33-35% despite commodity pressure.
items.quote: We will continue to aspire to hold at that kind of margin level, though it's starting to become a challenge because every major piece of commodity, whether it be copper, nickel, exotic materials used in after -treatment, platinum, silver, gold and even oi l prices are all inching upwards.

items.statement: Data centers approaching 10% of PowerGen revenue; global demand robust.
items.quote: So, yes, the answer is it's getting closer and closer to become about 10% plus of our PowerGen revenue. It is also accurate to say that we continue to see significant demand, both in India and globally for data centers.

items.statement: Exports may decline further before bottoming out due to geopolitical issues.
items.quote: So, we are not very, very optimistic that we have seen t he bottom of the market yet. So, we expect it to maybe correct a little bit more before it bottoms out and then we start to see it grow back again.

items.statement: Incremental capex for capacity; utilization at 50% installed, >90% manned.
items.quote: But when you look at the installed CAPEX, we continue to remain at roughly 50% utilization. From a manned CAPEX, we are greater than 90% of utilization.

items.statement: CPCB IV+ transition to complete next quarter; 1/3 of Q4 sales from CPCB IV+.
items.quote: Yes, I would say roughly 1/3 of our sale in the quarter was from CPCB IV+. So, it's starting to move pretty rapidly into CPCB IV+. So, we see the transition in the next quarter to happen completely.

items.statement: Commodity prices rising, pressuring material margins.
items.quote: So, there will be significant pressure on the material margin, but we wi ll continue to work with the supply base in trying to get more efficiency out of that and attempt to hold this growth.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks and conflicts pose uncertainty to global trade and supply chain.
items.quote: At the same time, internationally, geopolitical risks and conflicts continue to pose uncertainty with global trade and supply chain disruptions.

items.statement: One-time benefit of over Rs. 60 crores from management cross charges in Q4.
items.quote: One is we got a onetime true down benefit of a little over Rs. 60 crores from management cross charges.

items.statement: Industrial segment expected to grow at 20%-plus, 2x GDP for 10-15 years.
items.quote: I think it will grow at 20%-plus, but our long-term outlook when we had provided it a couple of years ago was that we see at least 2x of GDP growth of the industrial segment to continue for 10 to 15 years because we are comparing where our infrastructure is today compared to where some of the developed nations, like China and Europe and America are.

items.statement: Average lead time reduced to 30 days from 60 days due to capacity increase.
items.quote: Yes. Because capacity has increased. So, I am saying that average lead time is 30 days. The average lead time used to be 60 days.

items.statement: Majority of CPCB IV+ platforms localized >70-75%; gradual localization ongoing.
items.quote: We have over a dozen platforms. And I would say a majority of them are at high levels of localizations, and I mean high levels is greater than 70% to 75% of what we usually classify as high level because there are certain components related to electronics and certain types of parts which are not made in India, so we continue to have to import them.

items.statement: Net cash of Rs. 2,600 crores to fund future growth and returns.
items.quote: Today, we are sitting on net cash shift of almost Rs. 2,600 crores. How do you plan to utilize this for future growth?

items.statement: Royalty and support fees to be held at current percentage level.
items.quote: I think we should be able to hold it at the level we are currently. So, this quarter was an anomaly because of that onetime reversal. But overall, we should be able to hold it at the same percentage level despite the introduction of many, many new products is the way we are looking at it.

items.statement: Power Gen market to grow at 2x GDP, not 30% as last year.
items.quote: Of course, will it grow at 30% that we got last year, I don't think so. But we will continue to see at least 2x of GDP type of growth.

items.statement: Exports to remain below 20% of sales in FY25; ambition to return to 30-35%.
items.quote: So, it's very unlikely that the percentage of exports as compared to domestic is going to change very significantly for this year. And we are optimistic that this will start to pick up and as the new products start coming in and also as we start doing more and more components and other parts for export, our ambition is to get back to 30%, 35% of our sales being exports.

items.statement: Ammonia pricing expected around $400-$450 FOB ME for FY25; currently near $310
items.quote: the ammonia pricing for this year based on the forecast, which we have received from multiple agencies, that should be around $400 to $450 during the year. At this point in time, it's close to $310, which I am talking about FOB ME.

items.statement: Ammonia prices expected to reach $400+ from Q3 FY25
items.quote: From Q3 onwards, it should touch $400 plus is what we are looking at right now.

items.statement: TAN demand growth expected to continue in FY25 driven by coal, power, infra sectors growing 10-12%
items.quote: Growth in demand is expected to continue for the next fiscal, which is '24-'25 because the coal mining, power, infrastructure, all the sectors are expected to grow between 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Nitric acid prices expected to remain stable and improve over a few quarters; RGP IPA to perform better on demand and price
items.quote: Going forward, nitric acid prices are expected to remain stable and improved over a few quarters. RGP, which is propylene-based IPA, would continue to perform better from both demand and price perspective.

items.statement: Crop nutrition capacity utilization expected to rise to 60-70% in FY25 with normal monsoon
items.quote: Going forward, given that the monsoon is expected to be normal, hence, we expect the utilization should go up to around 60% to 70% depending upon which quarter you are talking about, even higher than that.

items.statement: Gopalpur TAN project capex Rs. 2,200 crore; funding tied up with bank approvals in place
items.quote: we have already tied up the funding for our Gopalpur project, which is around Rs. 2,200 crores. It's already done and dusted. We have got the approvals in place from the banks.

items.statement: Dahej nitric acid expansion capex Rs. 1,950 crore; bridge funding in place
items.quote: As far as the Dahej is concerned, which is our expansion plan, there, we are looking at to invest close to Rs. 1,950 crores. And there also the bridge funding is in place today.

items.statement: Gopalpur TAN project cash incurred ~Rs. 654 crore to date (~1/3 of total)
items.quote: So, we are close to around Rs. 654crores. That's how it is. But from a commitment perspective, we are far more higher. And till date for this year, we have actually done it. So, what we are saying is that we have actually incurred so far almost 1/3 of the amount for the project which is close to around Rs. 2,200 crores.

items.statement: TAN export quota 20,000 tons for FY25 vs domestic sales of 500,000-550,000 tons
items.quote: the quota, which we have got is around 20,000 ton for the whole year. And obviously, domestically we sell, during the year, close to almost 500,000 or 550,000 tons a year.

items.statement: TAN profitability stable within 100 bps range excluding FY23 positive aberration; expect improving trend
items.quote: TAN, except for the '22, '23, which was a positive aberration, if I were to take that away, I think from a profitability perspective, it has not impacted. There is always a variability betwe en 100 basis point plus/minus, but it has moved within that range. So, we expect to be stable and continue to be in an improving trend

items.statement: Russian FGAN imports were short-term aberration due to war-related export ban and Brazil demand shortfall; not expected to recur at same scale
items.quote: we are thinking that because of the rain effect and, obviously, the price effect, the product has come in, which in our view, will not recur year-on-year basis. And hence, we don't expect this to happen in a large sum.

items.statement: Booking value target for FY25 is INR1,000-1,200 crores, implying 25-33% growth over FY24's INR817 crores
items.quote: In general if you see, we have been growing between 25% and 33%. So it is one-fourth or one-third of new additions in booking as well as turnover. So that's how our internal targets are, that the company will keep on growing between 24% to 33%. So if we do that, it would be more than INR1,000 crores and less than INR1,200 crores.

items.statement: FY25 launch pipeline of ~12 lakh sq ft with GDV of INR1,400 crores across Monte South, Bhandup, Panvel, NeoPark, Neo Valley
items.quote: So FY'25 we will be launching in multiple areas, Monte South, Bhandup as well as Panvel. In all, we'll be launching around 12 lakh square feet and the GDV of that will be around INR14 crores to INR1500 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 40.1% in FY24 from 30.9% in FY20, with rising trajectory year-on-year
items.quote: Year-on-year if you look at FY20, we were at 30.9 and FY24, we're at 40.1 and the trajectory is rising from 30 to 41.

items.statement: Panvel project prices increased 5-6% year-on-year; Monte South prices up ~25% over 3 years and ~10% last year
items.quote: In some locations like Panvel, we have actually been able to increase our rates also by 5%-6% year-on-year. So there is no question of lull in demand.

items.statement: Monte South pricing rose from ~INR22,000 to ~INR23,500+ per sq ft (super built-up) YoY, with additional 5% GST benefit post-OC
items.quote: Last year, Monte South was selling at around 22,000 on super built up area. And this year we have sold at 23,500 plus. So that's the kind of rise that we have seen.

items.statement: No demand slack in Panvel or Bhandup; Panvel seeing robust inquiries post Atal Setu, Bhandup launches achieve 50-60% booking in launch quarter
items.quote: No, there is no drop in demand. In fact, because of this Atal Setu connectivity, Panvel has seen a robust inquiry. So at the next launch, we will have that inquiry really converted into sales and there is no lull in demand.

items.statement: Nexzone Phase 1 (Panvel) ahead of schedule by 2-3 quarters vs RERA deadline Dec 2025; Monte South Tower A OC expected this year, Tower B at 40+ floors (65 total), Tower C at foundation stage
items.quote: No, most likely it is going to be ahead of the schedule. In fact, a lot of apartments have been given possession as part occupation also. So it's most likely going to be ahead of schedule, but the RERA deadline has been December 25.

items.statement: Average cost of debt reduced from 15.5% (FY23) to 12.5% (FY24) via refinancing; FY25 interest cost projected at INR80-90 crores on INR750 crores debt; may consider equity raise for growth
items.quote: FY23 our average cost of debt was 15.5% and FY24 our average cost of debt is around 12.5%. So we have refinanced quite a lot of projects and brought down the rate of interest and we are continuously doing so.

items.statement: Monte South revenue (40% share) not recognized in top-line due to JV structure; profits recognized as line item; ~INR240 crores revenue equivalent not in top-line
items.quote: If you do want to know the effective share, that is 40% of the revenue which did not get recognized, that amount is. That amount is about INR240 crores. It is 40% of the revenue if we were to recognize.

items.statement: Balanced portfolio across three segments: South Mumbai (high value), Mulund/Bhandup/Vikhroli (mid), Dombivali/Panvel (affordable); Monte South INR6,000+ crores inventory to launch over 3-4 years
items.quote: Around INR6,000 crores – INR6000 plus inventory of Monte South is yet to be sold/launched. So that will be coming in the next three to four years as we speak in terms of launches.

items.statement: Futurex commercial OC received; most inventory to be leased/sold in FY25; OC-received unsold inventory ~225,000 sq ft valued ~INR380 crores (INR250 cr commercial, INR130 cr residential)
items.quote: Futurex has received the OC and most of the inventory should be, either leased or sold during this financial year. So that is going to be a big chunk of commercial revenue that will show up in this financial year.

items.statement: Execution capacity at ~60% utilization with 880 staff; bandwidth available for more projects pending right opportunities
items.quote: From execution perspective, if you see, you can say that we are only 60% of the bandwidth that we have, we are utilizing. Why 60%? That is always because of the want of the right opportunity and want of the acceleration in face numbers.

items.statement: Exploring SME REIT for single leased premises; not pursuing retail malls; next commercial office launch likely in 2+ years (Monte South Tower 5 or city project)
items.quote: What we are now exploring is there's a mini REIT, which is SME REIT is also permitted. So currently we are exploring that, that even single leased premises can be launched as a REIT.

items.statement: Presales growth of at least 30%-35% in FY25.
items.quote: With this momentum across projects, we are geared up to achieve a presales growth of at least 30%-35% in FY'25 and a higher growth of operating cash flow.

items.statement: Expect strong jump in profitability and margins in FY25.
items.quote: We expect to see a strong jump in profitability as well as margins in FY'25.

items.statement: Revenue recognition in FY25 to be much bigger than FY24.
items.quote: So Pritesh, again, I cannot quantify the number, but definitely can assure you that this number will be much, much bigger than the FY'24 number.

items.statement: Operating cash flow in FY25 to be much bigger than FY24.
items.quote: Also, you will see that that's why the collections in this year financial year and the net operational cash flow number will be much bigger, in fact, much, much bigger than FY'24.

items.statement: Presales growth of minimum 30% to 35% irrespective of Nepean Sea Road launch.
items.quote: And without irrespective of this project coming or not coming, we are very clear that we will make minimum 30% to 35% presales growth and plus -- and we have discussed on the revenue already.

items.statement: Presales growth of minimum 30% to 35% irrespective of Nepean Sea Road.
items.quote: But irrespective of -- let me give this at the cost of repetition. Irrespective of Nepean Sea Road, we are very confident we'll grow minimum 35% to 40% -- 30% to 35% in our presales number.

items.statement: Higher EBITDA margins in Sunteck City 4th Avenue from revenue recognition.
items.quote: We are on track to complete Sunteck City 4th Avenue project in FY'25 and due to better realizations, we expect to record higher EBITDA margins in this project from the revenue recognition.

items.statement: Better sales in FY26 than FY25.
items.quote: And we see this momentum to continue and you will see better sales, in fact, in FY'26 than what we have seen in FY'25.

items.statement: Planning for commercial portfolio at Oshiwara District Center; commencement plans to be confirmed soon.
items.quote: We have also moved ahead on planning for our commercial portfolio at Oshiwara District Center at Goregaon West. We will be able to confirm the commencement plans on this very soon.

items.statement: Roadmap to double GDV from INR30,000 crores to INR60,000 crores in coming years.
items.quote: As communicated earlier, we have embarked on the ambitious yet achievable roadmap of doubling our GDV, which is gross development value, from INR30,000 crores to INR60,000 crores in the coming years.

items.statement: GDV of Mira Road, Naigaon, Goregaon phases together more than INR4,000 crores - INR5,000 crores.
items.quote: So if you are talking about Mira Road, Naigaon, Goregaon, all put together, the GDV value of these projects, all 3 put together will be more than INR4,000 crores - INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: Inventory in ready-to-move-in projects around INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores; ongoing projects around INR1,500 crores.
items.value: INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores; INR1,500 crores
items.quote: So Vasudev, Prashant this side. So the inventory numbers, the ready -to-move-in inventory is close to around INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores and the ongoing projects have an inventory of around INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Project level margin for Naigaon at 30%.
items.quote: We have recognized approx INR284 crores from Naigaon, and the project level margin stands at 30%.

items.statement: Luxury segment sales faster than mid-income or affordable segments.
items.quote: So Prem, so what we are talking about is Luxury obviously is doing sales much better than -- and faster than the sales of any mid -segment or we are seeing all of us are observing that sales of Uber Luxury segment is faster than the mid-income segment or the affordable segment.

items.statement: Nepean Sea Road launch may slip to Q1 FY26.
items.quote: So Biplab, first thing I want to clarify that we are definitely looking to launch towards Q4. It may go to Q1 of FY'26.

items.statement: Enabling resolution for fund raise; no plans to raise equity or increase debt.
items.quote: But as a practice, we have been taking this for the years from last few years that this enabling resolution is always there. But obviously, we don't plan to raise any equity or increase the debt, we are already net debt positive.

items.statement: Single digit growth for this year, recovery starting next calendar year.
items.quote: Single digit growth for this year. And so that is how it's going to be for this year. Starting next year, right calendar year, I'm using the calendar year because in the US election will end and then recovery starts, but it may not start till probably February, March of next year is when the recovery will start.

items.statement: Expects similar margins for next year as whole year.
items.quote: Yes. Whatever we have for the whole year, we expected the similar margins for the next year, yes.

items.statement: Backlog of 8 to 9 months of revenue, about Rs. 800 crores.
items.quote: We have about 8 to 9 months’ worth of revenue that we have in backlog at this point.

items.statement: Wage inflation increased costs, not passed on to customers; bill rates same, pay rates up.
items.quote: It's about flat, Shah Nawaz. It's the inflation of the wages that we're talking about is there and the increase in costs have happened because of that and not because of anything else and we were not able to pass on that increase in cost to our customers. I guess the bill rate is still the same, but the pay rate went up for us.

items.statement: Early signs of recovery in US; Europe flat; India booming; slow growth next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: So good question, yes, we are in a similar boat as like others. And yes, there are some challenges, spending has weakened. We are seeing early signs of recovery though we are getting inquiries from our customers specifically in US markets. Europe market is pretty much flat for us. Indian market is booming, we are probably in India is the best market in the world nowadays.

items.statement: 80% of revenue from repeat customers, 20% typical.
items.quote: Around 80% of our revenue is from repeat from the same customers, right, 20% is what you will get, typical. That has been our historical numbers and that continues to be the historical thing.

items.statement: AMS is 5% to 7% of revenue.
items.quote: To answer the AMS part, it is probably 5% to 7% of our revenue. We are not doing AMS like the large, big boys. We don't do it.

items.statement: 80% of revenue from digital transformation, 7-8% SAP, balance consulting.
items.quote: For us 80% of our revenue is from digital transformation, right, it is all digital is what we call. So that is the primary side of it. And then we have about close to 7% to 8% of SAP business and the balance is what we call the me-too.

items.statement: Industry revenue breakup: BFSI 8.5%, Health 14%, Info Tech 30%, Retail 12%, Media 6.1%, Energy 7.4%.
items.quote: Now, when it comes to the industry breakup, if you are looking for an industry breakup, we have BFSI, which is about 8.5%, then Health and Life Sciences is about 14% and then we call information service and technology. These are all the new age companies, IT companies, right, IT companies, being Amazon like companies and or ISV kind of companies those is about 30% and the next largest one is, some

items.statement: AI revenue in million-dollar range, expected to grow to few million over next year.
items.quote: Let's currently answer the question on the type of work we do, but the revenue is probably in the million-dollar range at this point because since early adopters right now, people are not spending you know multi million dollars when it comes to AI based projects. People are trying out small incremental bids and we anticipate that over the next one year this will go to a few million dollars.

items.statement: Products revenue half a million, expected 20-30 million over 3-5 years.
items.quote: We have customers in India, US and European markets. We're seeing some pipeline being built up. These are early revenues, and we are probably in the half a million range of revenue. But we anticipate right over the next 3 to 5 years, 20 to 30 million revenues will be coming in from those.

items.statement: Manpower flat at 1800, hiring fluid based on demand.
items.quote: We are flat what we were last year. Ups and downs were there, there be some people left, but we were back to 1800.

items.statement: No significant R&D spend on AI, done on job with customers.
items.quote: There is no real R&D as such right. We are using internally to see our efficiencies; we can build efficiencies into our own delivery kind of stuff. So, the R&D mostly is done on the job with the customer.

items.statement: Fixed price engagements 10-20% of work, margins challenging.
items.quote: Fixed price engagements are also about 10%-20% of what we do and those are of course they tend to be based on the scope of work and whatever we estimate at that time. And those are obviously fixed price projects. There could be, obviously, there are negotiations on fixed outcomes and there we have some our margins would be a little bit more challenging there.

items.statement: 40-60% of business through outreach or other channels.
items.quote: Yes, I do not have a metrics, but in terms of basically, most of our business, I mean there is referral, so referral could be like a large part, but yes, we would get about 40%, 50%, 60% of our business which is through either our outreach or through other channels.

items.statement: Expects to double revenue to INR6,000 crores by FY27.
items.quote: So we are seeing that happening in 2027 because the situation has also to improve. See, there are still geo-political reasons for business disruptions, the Red Sea, the war, like various inputs, which are increasing in India.

items.statement: Confident to maintain EBITDA margin in guided band of 16% to 18%.
items.quote: We expect the benefits of this to play in the coming quarters and are confident to maintain the EBITDA in our guided band of 16% to 18%.

items.statement: Aims to build branded business of $100 million in next 3-4 years.
items.quote: And that's why we are quite confident that in the next 3, 4 years, we should be able to build a branded business of almost $100 million.

items.statement: Targets branded business to reach 10% plus of revenue.
items.quote: So definitely, we have set good plans to see that this becomes quite successful in our overall portfolio of revenue and slowly we will endeavour it to reach to almost 10% plus. That's where we are currently targeting.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin for branded segment at 20% to 24%.
items.quote: 20% to 24% should be considered.

items.statement: Plans to reduce debt further in next 2-3 years.
items.quote: So definitely, our philosophy is to reduce the debt and say in the next 2 to 3 years, you will see there will be a further reduction in the debt as we draw in more operating cash.

items.statement: Aims for 60% U.S. and 40% non-U.S. revenue split in mid to long-term.
items.quote: No, our overall mid to long -term strategy is to see that we have like a 60% -40% ratio, 60% in U.S. and 40% in non-U.S.

items.statement: Plans to increase India revenue share to 6% to 7%.
items.quote: Definitely, we are planning around 6% to 7% of our revenues going forward because we have various strategies under our sleeves to see that how we can expand our market share in the Indian market.

items.statement: Invested INR60 crores in fashion bedding unit last year.
items.quote: Now recently, like last year, we invested almost INR60 crores on building a world-class fashion bedding unit.

items.statement: Investing INR50 crores in zero-liquid discharge effluent water treatment plant at Bhilad.
items.quote: Right. And the zero -liquid discharge effluent water treatment plant of INR50 crores, that is at Gujarat unit, right?

items.statement: Plans to expand capacity post FY27 if utilization reaches 85%.
items.quote: That should be considered most like FY '27, I'd say, probably. But if we are lucky and if we are more successful, then definitely, we'll come forth in '26.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin impacted by 2% due to one-time promotional activities.
items.quote: EBITDA margin of 15% was on account of onetime promotional activities, which increased the other expenses and therefore, impacted EBITDA margin by around 2%.

items.statement: Endeavours to improve EBITDA margin to 18-20% then 20-22%.
items.quote: At the end of the year, we see that the EBITDA level, as I mentioned, should improve from 16%, 18% , to 18% to 20% and then 20% to 22%, that's what the endeavour is.

items.statement: Branded segment realizations are 15% to 20% higher than normal range.
items.quote: See, normally, it is like what we've just now mentioned, it is around 15% to 20% higher than the normal range, because there are expenses to be considered.

items.statement: Expects FY25 demand to be better than FY24.
items.quote: So the demand is like I can only say in one word, FY '25 is better than FY '24.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis increases freight costs and working capital by 15 days.
items.quote: And secondly, one more important thing because U.S.A. is not impacted as such with this, because it goes with Cape of Good Hope, where only you are increasing the working capital by 15 days.

items.statement: Expects PAT margin to improve next year and year after, reaching 17-18% gradually.
items.quote: I think as the cycle keeps going, we probably get to after tax profit margins and the TCI margins closer to 17%-18% gradually as we go ahead. So, this year's margin would better than FY’24, FY’26 margin should better than FY’25, and FY’27 margin should better than FY’26.

items.statement: Internal target for pre-sales in FY25 is Rs. 2,000 crores.
items.quote: This year we have a target of Rs. 2,000 crores internally to get to , again it assumes that the market will remain buoyant the way it is , and we get to launch the phases as scheduled.

items.statement: Expects to do 25-26 lakh square feet of construction this year.
items.quote: We do expect to do 25 -26 lakhs square foot of construction this year. I don't see the pace slowing down because we will continue to launch projects this year.

items.statement: Expects to hit 15% ROE in FY26 if deliveries go as planned.
items.quote: Like FY’26, we will definitely hit 15% over ROE's if things go as per plan as per deliveries.

items.statement: Aims to achieve 900-1,000 units per year in senior living, 2x-2.5x growth in 3-4 years.
items.quote: Right now, we are looking at from a medium-term view if we can get to about 900 -1,000 units a year from about 354 units a year today as compared to last year. So, percentages as we allocate, can we go about 2x-2.5x in the next 3-4 years.

items.statement: Plans to launch Ashiana Amarah Phase-4 and 5 in this financial year.
items.quote: We have Ashiana Amarah Phase-4 and 5 to launch. We are hoping to launch it in this financial year both those phases and we have another project in Sector 80 in Gurugram which is not too far away from Ashiana Amarah.

items.statement: Hoping to launch Sector 80 project in Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Also, we are hoping that we can launch that in the 4th Quarter of this year and if not 4th Quarter of this year , then the first quarter of the next year.

items.statement: Targets 27-30% gross profit margin on JV projects based on current prices and costs.
items.quote: So based on current sale prices and current cost of construction, we typically look for about 27% to 30% on JV projects. And if outright projects are there , then a commensurate increase in this GP margin to cover the cost of financing in an outright structure.

items.statement: Expects gross profit margin expansion and construction cost as percentage of sales price to come down.
items.quote: But as a percentage of sales price as I said, we are going to see gross profit margin expansion. And I think , as a percentage of sales price, construction cost to come down.

items.statement: Cost of construction will increase due to inflation and higher spec projects.
items.quote: Our cost of construction will go up for two reasons. There is inflation but in construction it is not like more than regular inflation in the economy right now.

items.statement: Expects Gurugram to contribute heavy share of pre-sales this year.
items.quote: But I said we expect Gu rugram to contribute the heavy share this year as well like last year it did. So that will continue.

items.statement: Senior living to play larger mix, allocating more capital.
items.quote: But overall, I think senior living will play a larger mix as we go forward because we see that business, relatively less competitive.

items.statement: Term sheets have 50% failure rate, some may slip.
items.quote: But these things are 50% as sometimes term sheets slip somewhere or the other during diligence or something or the other. I am hopeful that we will close but they can slip through the cracks.

items.statement: No buyback this year due to need for cash for acquisitions; buybacks every 3-5 years.
items.quote: Buybacks will not happen every year. We hope that we do buybacks every 3-5 years depending on the cash flow availability of the

items.statement: IFC has >30% share in net cash flows of Ashiana Amarah project.
items.quote: Their percentage share in the cash flows of the project would be a little bit more than 30% in the net cash flows of the project till a certain figure they have a higher share and then becomes 30 %.

items.statement: FY25 profit growth expected at least 20% over FY24's Rs 1,388 crore PAT
items.quote: This year, we did about Rs. 1,388 crores profit. I think going forward next year, we at least see if all goes well and there are not too many surprises, we should do greater than 20% growth for the year.

items.statement: FY25 top-line growth expected 15-20% and earnings growth around 20%
items.quote: I think we believe that we shall be able to grow top line wise also more than 15% to 20% and even on earnings growth, also, we are looking at about 20% comfortably.

items.statement: Annual capex of Rs 300-350 crore for maintenance and capacity expansion at existing sites
items.quote: It's nothing large, I mean we expect that we should spend about Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 350 crores a year is what we are spending in a year.

items.statement: RoW business performing well with Brazil at $25-26M, Canada at CAD 40M, and strong orders from Egypt and Saudi
items.quote: Brazil, I think direct exports and our subsidiary exports are almost $25 million to $26 million a year. Canadian sub has done nearly CAD 40 million. So, overall, our RoW business is doing well. I think this year , we have some very good orders from Egypt and Saudi.

items.statement: Margins sustainable if product mix holds; conservative 20% profit growth guidance despite stable margins and 15-20% top-line growth
items.quote: Based on the product mix holding up, yes.

items.statement: Agrochemical business internal target to triple to Rs 300 crore in next 3 years; first true year of operations
items.quote: our internal target is that this business has to triple in the next 3 years, we want to go to Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Key pipeline includes Semaglutide (FTF on strengths), Wegovy (FTF), Olaparib, Trabectedin, Carfilzomib, Imbruvica (subject to litigation)
items.quote: So, we mentioned that, Semaglutide we mentioned, Olaparib we have mentioned. Carfilzomib, we have mentioned; Trabectedin, we have mentioned. So, I think this is all there in the investor presentation.

items.statement: Promoter considering buyback if large acquisition not closed; decision pending as year unfolds
items.quote: Well, I am thinking about it, I have not made up my mind. I think if we get a large enough acquisition then I don't want to do a buyback. But if we are unable to close a large acquisition, then maybe we can consider a buyback.

items.statement: Cash and liquid assets of Rs 2,004 crore vs Rs 116 crore debt (net cash position) as of May 26
items.quote: As of May 26th, we have Rs. 2,000 crores of cash and investable liquid assets and Rs. 116 crores of debt. So, that's the actual thing to say.

items.statement: Acquisition focus on RoW/emerging markets to strengthen base business; India valuations too expensive
items.quote: I think the acquisition space is to strengthen our base business. So, we have the money to do it and primarily, we are looking at a RoW business. So, we are looking at different options.

items.statement: Domestic pharma business run-rate 95-100% of prior Rs 100 cr/qtr; one-time Rs 90 cr charge from model change
items.quote: It's a onetime charge because we just changed a few things and the way we are distributing. I think the run rate is still 95% to 100% , There's no change in that.

items.statement: Agrochemicals Rs 30 cr one-time hit from non-utilized intermediate capacity at third-party site
items.quote: So, because we are not utilizing the intermediate capability, we had to make a provision for non -utilization of that. So, we took a hit on depreciation of amo unt and certain advance we gave to that supplier. So, I think that's why we took a Rs. 30 crores hit.

items.statement: Two US-approved sites (Hyderabad, Vizag) plus CMO model for niche products; Rimegepant filed from Vizag, Semaglutide via CMO
items.quote: I mean, we have 2 sites for the U.S. So, we have Hyd erabad, and we have Vizag. So, like Rimegepant that we filed recently, we filed from Vizag. We can use these 2 sites, but sometimes we also use the CMO, because our model is doing niches, right?

items.statement: Base business PAT estimated around Rs 350-400 crore annually
items.quote: I would say, I mean, honestly,I don't have an answer to your question. It is probably around maybe Rs. 350 crores to Rs. 400 crores PAT, I would believe, yes.

items.statement: Employee count ~5,000 (ex-contractors) or 5,700-5,800 (incl. contractors); cost ratio expected to sustain
items.quote: Total, without the contractors in the part, if we remove the contractors,is what about 5,000 employees in the system and if we include the contractors and everyone, I think it's about 5,700 to 5,800.

items.statement: Management targets a CAGR of around 15%-20% per annum on a standalone basis for FY25 and is reasonably sure of achieving it.
items.quote: We definitely are looking at a CAGR of around 15 %-20% on per annum basis. So that is what we are looking at and we are reasonably sure of achieving that thing.

items.statement: Management expects standalone EBITDA margins to remain more or less the same as FY24 (around 31%) and potentially get better due to firm market conditions.
items.quote: Yes, it will be more or less the same only and maybe get better itself because as I told market is going to be firm -- remain strong. So definitely this will be the case.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin range is 40% to 45%, but with OSV additions margins will be slightly lower; 40% can be taken as current benchmark.
items.quote: Around 40% to 45% margins is the range that seems to be healthy. However, gradually, OSV business will be added to our fleet strength and there the margins will be a little lower. So you can take a 40% margin as of now.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR200-300 crores for FY26 and INR300-400 crores for FY27, totaling INR600-700 crores over next 3 years, funded majorly through internal accruals.
items.quote: so looking at the current fleet size we would definitely like to have a capex plan of about INR200 crores to INR300 crores next year w hich is 25 -26 and then 26 -27 around INR300 crores, INR400 crores. So put together about INR600 crores, INR700 crores capex will go in next 3 years

items.statement: Seamec Diamond acquired Jan 2, 2024, deployed with ONGC from Q1 FY25 for 3 years at USD8,750/day; Seamec Pearl delivery by June 22, 2024, deployed from Q2 FY25 for 3 years at USD8,750/day; NUSANTARA delivery mid-Sept 2025 with 5-year contra
items.quote: We acquired the offshore support vessel Seamec Diamond for USD7 million, completing the takeover on January 2 nd, 2024. This vessel is expected to be deployed with ONGC from the first quarter of '25 for a period of three years at a rate of USD8,750 per day.

items.statement: Charter rates have firmed up and management foresees this trend continuing for the next two to three years, supported by vessel availability for spot market.
items.quote: So over -- compared to last year we have seen prices forming up which are giving us an advantage and I foresee t his trend to continue for next two-three years definitely.

items.statement: OSV business expected payback period of 5 years with overall margins of 18%-20%; company continues to look for more OSV opportunities globally.
items.quote: In case of OSV business we are expecting a payback period of 5 years.

items.statement: Three vessels operate only in non-monsoon season; they will not operate after mid-May through Q2, causing seasonal decline in Q1/Q2 but uptrend from Q3.
items.quote: Even in Q1, since the monsoon hits around 15th of May onwards, so our three vessels which are on non -monsoon season only operate, they will not be operating after two months of Q1 and entire Q2.

items.statement: Loan of INR180 crores given to UK subsidiary for acquiring property to set up global office in London to access North Sea market.
items.quote: This loan we have given to our UK subsidiary and we are in the process of opening our global office there in London. For that we have acquired some property. For its funding we have provided that term loan.

items.statement: Consolidated losses from Seamec Nidhi (INR6 crores one-time closure hit) will cease; gap between standalone and consolidated financials will narrow from FY25 onward.
items.quote: Going forward, the difference between the standalone and consolidated will narrow as we improve our international operations. And since we have cut down heavily on this Seamec Nidhi, you will see a remarkable improvemen t in the coming years.

items.statement: Targeting 25% to 30% loan book growth for this financial year.
items.quote: So about 25% to 30% is what we are approximately targeting.

items.statement: Expects credit costs of 2.5% to 3% on average going forward.
items.quote: See as far as credit cost these things are a little difficult to predict, but on an ongoing basis, on a steady state on average we expect about 2.5% to 3% of credit costs going forward.

items.statement: Expects NIMs to be largely protected.
items.quote: NIMs would be largely protected.

items.statement: Targeting 60 to 75 new branches plus split branches in FY25.
items.quote: Yes. So we are targeting anywhere from about 60 to 75 new branches plus certain split branches as well and that will be a combination of expansions in Bihar, Jharkhand areas.

items.statement: Predicting INR6-7 crores disbursement for rural LAP this quarter.
items.quote: This quarter we are predicting about a INR6 crores or INR7 crores disbursement.

items.statement: Expects 100 bps dip in borrowing costs.
items.quote: Lower. At least we are expecting 100 bps dip as is the market interest rates.

items.statement: Targets 4.5x debt to equity, implying 22-25% capital adequacy.
items.quote: Typically, we target about 4.5x of debt to equity. That comes out to 22%-25%or so.

items.statement: Aims to build INR5,000 crores AUM, originally guided for FY26-27.
items.quote: We are confident that we are on the right path to achieve our strategic goal of building INR5,000 crores of AUM while maintaining a balanced debt-to-equity ratio.

items.statement: Borrowing costs declined 50-75 bps post QIP and rating upgrade.
items.quote: But post the QIP, we've already seen the rates coming down by about 50 bps to 75 bps in the last quarter, which is both on account of the benefits of QIP itself and the recent upgrade that we've also got with CARE.

items.statement: Lending rates are being cut due to competition and regulatory pressure.
items.quote: We are cutting our lending rates, of course, for competition and of course, through different pressure that is announced by regulato rs and other things.

items.statement: Collection pressure due to over-lending, heat, elections; expected to fix in next couple of quarters.
items.quote: So overall there is some pressure on the collections. Numerous factors at play. Of course, there is heat and there is elections, but largely speaking there's a lot of -- I mean in certain areas there has been a lot of over lending going on and that has been generating pressure for us on the repayment side.

items.statement: Microfinance sector has 2-4 years of growth before euphoria; 25-30% growth not dangerous.
items.quote: I don't think so. I mean overall, microfinance still has a good two to four years to go before it reaches that euphoric moment of growing faster than it needs to. Right now, I don't think that growing 25%, 30% is dangerous at all.

items.statement: Plans to increase retail NCD share of borrowings to 20-25%.
items.quote: And that should kind of go up from something like 12%, 13% to sizable 20%, 25% maybe.

items.statement: Over-leveraging among customers causing repayment pressure.
items.quote: But largely speaking, my guess is that most of the problems are caused due to certain customers borrowing more than they can afford.

items.statement: Pre-COVID 99% collection efficiency is behind; credit costs to be 2.5-3% over 3-4 years.
items.quote: So on a steady state over the next, let's say, 3 to 4 years, I would say that on average the credit cost should be about 2.5 % not to exceed 3%.

items.statement: Operational expenses may be marginally higher initially due to expansion, but settle by year-end.
items.quote: Yes. So to answer your second quest ion first, yes, marginally operational expense, especially salaries initially might be higher. But by the end of the year, that catches up.

items.statement: Management targets minimum 15% YoY revenue growth overall; acquired entities to focus on utilization and margins in FY25 with growth from FY26
items.quote: Our endeavor would be to grow as fast as possible. And we generally tend to focus on a 15-odd-percent Y-o-Y growth every year.

items.statement: Atraco normalized EBITDA margin 10-10.5%, Matrix ~11%; target to reach Gokaldas levels in 4-6 quarters
items.quote: In a normalized operations, Atraco should be over 10% to 10.5% EBITDA margin and Matrix should be at about 11% odd EBITDA margin on an ongoing basis.

items.statement: FY25 capex of INR100 crores: INR40 crores for Bhopal unit, INR50 crores for efficiency/profitability improvements, INR10 crores for fabric processing unit
items.quote: For the Bhopal new unit, we allocated around INR 40 crores. For the normal capex, what Mr. Siva talked about, we will be investing in improving the efficiency parameters, that is the profitability improvement capex are the key focus area. We allocate d almost INR50 crores during the year for this purpose . INR25 crores for the existing units, about INR10 crores in Matrix and INR15 crores for Atrac

items.statement: Inventory destocking ending; brands showing renewed buying appetite; US imports down 20% in FY24, EU 19%, UK 28%
items.quote: The inventory destocking cycle is now coming to an end with many fashion brands showing reduced inventory, improved financial performance and the renewed appetite to buy.

items.statement: Pricing power to return slowly over 3-4 quarters; full pricing power expected in FY26 not FY25; wage costs up 5% in April 2024
items.quote: As the situation improves going forward and the demand is coming back, the pricing power will come back. But my sense is the pricing power will take some more time before it reaches because the full demand situation has not been restored.

items.statement: FY24 shipped 29M pieces; FY25 target similar or higher pieces; outerwear share dropped due to mild winters and inventory overhang
items.quote: For FY '24, we shipped about 29 million pieces and my hope is in FY '25, even if the product mix changes to a little more outerwear, I believe we should still be able to do this or even better in terms of number of pieces shifted.

items.statement: Gokaldas standalone at 100% utilization, chock-a-block with orders; Atraco and Matrix at 80-85% utilization, targeting near 100% by H2 FY25
items.quote: Standalone entity, as we speak in the current state, we are at 100% in fact we are -- from a delivery standpoint, we have chock-a-block with orders.

items.statement: Atraco Kenya rebadging caused 2-3 weeks lost production, airfreight costs continuing into Q1; wage inflation 5% in Karnataka and other states
items.quote: We almost lost 2 to 3 weeks of production. And to make up for that, we had to incur over time, we had to incur some airing of goods, et cetera, which impacted profitability in that quarter, which some of the residual air lifting may have to happen in Q1 as well.

items.statement: Raised INR600 crores via QIP in April 2024; turned net cash positive from net debt of INR336 crores at March 31, 2024
items.quote: Subsequently, the company raised equity capital of INR600 crores through qualified institutional placement in April 2024, which has helped the company to turn net cash positive.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at more than 10%
items.quote: Going forward, whatever guidance I've given for FY '25 last time, we are confident it will be a double digit, more than 10%.

items.statement: L1 in four projects worth INR3,914.28 crores expected to be awarded in June-July
items.quote: At present, we are L1 in four projects amounting to INR3914.28 crores.

items.statement: Additional order inflow guidance of INR2,500-3,000 crores for FY25 beyond L1 projects
items.quote: Another INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of approximately INR110 crores
items.quote: This year we had basically INR110 crores.

items.statement: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus project execution of INR800 crores in FY25 and INR1,200 crores in FY26

items.statement: Consolidated operating EBITDA margin expected near 20% in next 2-3 years; hospital segment alone 23%-24%
items.quote: We can see that margins also will expand at a consolidated level, near 20% in next two to three years. And hospital segment alone, we should reach 23%-24%.

items.statement: ARPOB growth guided at 8% to 9%
items.quote: with the continuous ARPOB growth which is going to happen, which I already guided around 8% to 9%.

items.statement: MVT revenue contribution target close to 10% in next 3-4 years from current 5%
items.quote: we are confident in the next 3-4 years the MVT alone can contribute close to 10% of our revenue.

items.statement: Total project capex of INR 1,000 crores for 1,700 beds over FY25-FY27; FY25 capex INR 450 crores

items.statement: Kasargod 260-bed greenfield expected operational FY26; Aster Capital Trivandrum 460-bed greenfield expected FY27
items.quote: Kasargod is expected to operationalize in FY26 and Aster Capital is expected to operationalize sometime in FY27.

items.statement: Andhra Telangana contributes only 5% of India EBITDA; margin improvement there won't move consolidated needle significantly
items.quote: Andhra Telangana if you look at their EBITDA contribution right, it's almost 5% of your total India contribution. So even if you increase the margin, it is highly unlikely that it's going to move the needle in a very big way.

items.statement: Effective tax rate on PBT expected around 14%-15% from next year under new tax regime
items.quote: you can take an effective tax rate on the PBT of something around 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Andhra Telangana management under performance review; divestment possible if no improvement in next two quarters

items.statement: Net cash of INR 1,500 crores retained in listed entity after GCC sale proceeds and special dividend of INR 5,900 crores
items.quote: We have a cash of around INR 1,500 crores in the listed entity.

items.statement: Peak debt expected in FY25; net debt/EBITDA may slightly increase in FY25 then decline; target below 2x; debt cash by FY27-FY28
items.quote: should see the debt % coming down. That means to say net debt to EBITDA ratio today what we have around 1.1x may a little bit slightly increase in FY25 and again after that should come down in such a way that by FY27-FY28 we should go into debt cash

items.statement: Zero-to-three-year hospitals (6 units) revenue INR 275 crores, operating EBITDA loss only INR 7 crores; Whitefield broke even in month 3, full-year loss <INR 4-5 crores

items.statement: Rohtak armour factory order book INR 140 crores, Wide plate mill order book INR 250 crores

items.quote: We may be having around INR350 crores to INR400 crores. We will give you that exact figure later.

items.quote: Yes, we have communicated to investors that we have r eceived the order of around INR 130 crores, which has been already given the communication also.

items.statement: Base cost reduction of INR60-75 crores expected for FY25 vs previous year
items.quote: It should be in that INR60 crores to INR75 crores base cost reduction from the previous year.

items.quote: So, we do still have, I think, an inventory in excess of INR100 crores, but none of this inventory is at risk and we will be using all of this inventory within this financial year.

items.quote: We feel a capex of somewhere around INR120 crore, INR130 crore, INR140 crore, that's the range bound what we are looking at.

items.statement: New launches to contribute ~2.5 msf of FY25 sales; rest from sustenance sales in ongoing projects

items.statement: Free cash flow target Rs 350-400 cr over next 12-18 months; Rs 270 cr already unlocked in last 2 years
items.quote: With few monetization coming-up and few more projects coming up for closure this year, we will achieve the Rs. 350 crores of free cash flows or maybe surpass that number over the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 25% CAGR over next three to five years
items.quote: we stand with our revenue guidance of 25% CAGR over the next three to five years

items.statement: API and formulation revenue split guidance of 80%-20%

items.statement: Maintenance capex of around INR 25 crores going forward
items.quote: Now we would have some bit of maintenance capex only which will be to the tune of INR25 crores or so.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expanded 230 bps to 42.8% in FY24
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins for FY '24 stood at 42.8% as compared to 40.5%, an increase of 230 bps.

items.statement: PAT margins expanded 220 bps to 30.3% in FY24

items.statement: EBITDA to grow faster than revenue driven by operational efficiencies
items.quote: We also anticipate that our EBITDA and PAT will grow at a faster rate than revenue, driven by operational efficiencies and increased utilization across our units.

items.statement: Immunosuppressant share reduced by around 4% in FY24
items.quote: So compared to last year, the immunosuppressants have come down by around 4%, the weightage on immunosuppressants.

items.statement: Oncology and anti-infective segments growing faster than immunosuppressants
items.quote: And this is, again, mostly towards the new product launches that have happened, because of which the weightage on the immunosuppressants has come down compared to the last year.

items.statement: API revenue normalization expected in FY25 after customer site shifts
items.quote: Hence, we anticipate revenue normalization in FY'25.

items.statement: Formulation revenue grew 106% in FY24
items.quote: Our formulations revenue grew by 37% in Q4FY'24 and 106% for the full year FY'24 on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Customer site shifts impacted API growth by 6-7% in Q4
items.quote: So this was close to around -- probably around 6% to 7% or so.

items.statement: Limbasi facility capacity utilization at 35.12% in FY24
items.quote: Limbasi facility is working at around 35.12% in this financial year.

items.statement: Injectable plant commercial production expected early half of Q3 FY25

items.statement: CDMO sales minimal in FY24, not built into guidance

items.quote: To summarise, going ahead for FY '25 , the company aspires to achieve mid -teens revenue growth backed by new store openings in new and existing geographies and subject to recovery in the overall industry demand for premium and mid-premium brands.

items.statement: Targets to improve profitability through cost efficiency measures in FY25
items.quote: The company is also targeting to improve profitability through implementation of various cost efficiency measures.

items.statement: Plans to add 30 to 40 new EBO stores in FY25
items.quote: During the year, we have added 52 EBO stores and we plan to add another 30 to 40 new stores in FY '25.

items.statement: Capex for new stores and renovation of old stores; maintenance capex around INR20-25 crores annually
items.quote: So, that will be like recurring capex that will be there. So, if I were to assume a maintenance capex, it would be around that, INR20 crores to INR25 crores.

items.quote: In FY '24, the apparel market in India moderated and after an expansion during FY '23. However, at Mufti, the revenues grew by 14% to INR 567 crores with gross margins remaining stable at 57.5% for FY '24.

items.quote: The market for premium and mid -premium branded appar el continued to experience softened demand due to consumer behaviour influenced by an inflationary environment that curtailed discretionary expenditures while concurrently witnessing a surge in consumer spend towards travel and other essential purchases.

items.statement: April was a very good month compared to last year but May demand dwindled; recovery timing uncertain
items.quote: April was a very good month, so to say, as compared to last year but May somehow again has dwindled. So it's very difficult to say right now on, I immediately see recovery this and that.

items.quote: So, channel-wise for Q4 EBO was 57%, MBO was 33%.

items.quote: Our working capital days have increased to 166 days as on 31st March 2024. This is on account of two reasons. One, increased inventory due to higher goods returned.

items.statement: MBO channel degrew ~2% for FY24 primarily due to higher voluntary return provision
items.quote: MBO channel for the year has degrown by around 2%.

items.statement: Plans to spend around 5% of revenues on branding and advertising going forward
items.quote: Going ahead, we will spend on around 5% of revenues on branding and advertising.

items.statement: Intends to double business in next 4-5 years but may take 5.5 years to do so profitably
items.quote: Of course, we still intend to double the business in the next 4, 5 years. And that's what w e endeavour for even going forward. It's not like we're going to slow down our growth or progress in any way.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin is around 19% compared to 28% under Ind AS
items.quote: So, the pre-Ind AS EBITDA is around 19% compared to 28%in Ind AS.

items.quote: Today, as we speak, the EBITDA on service is about 19%, which about three or four years back, it was about nearly 12% or 13%.

items.quote: So about 5% to 6% recovery this year and going forward as such. So we're hoping that the market would be up.

items.quote: We have achieved success to some extent by bringing down our revenue from a particular state, that's Kerala, from a share of 74% in FY '21 to 60-odd percent in FY'24. And we further expect to bring this to sub-50% levels over the next two years.

items.quote: Even if you take 20% out in terms of EV 80% of 7 million is 5.6 million vehicles. items.quote: So INR3.5 crores initial capex plus INR10 crores of inventory would be about INR13.5-, 14 crores of capital employed. That's on one side. items.quote: This vertical contributes approximately 15% of our top line and in terms of EBITDA, the contribution is over 50%. In services, it's collision and repairs, that's the Bodyshop business, that contributes to a larger chunk of the margin.

items.quote: Anywhere between 70 to 75 branches a year-on-year basis is what we should be looking at in smaller towns and districts under the deeper impact strategy.

items.quote: RBI throwing out a number of INR10 crores unit shortfall on households out of which INR9.5 crores shortfall happens to be in the EWS/LIG segment which is our prime segment and prime area.

items.quote: I think we're very confident that these projects will give us an additional turnover, anything between INR2,000 to INR2,500 crores in the FY '25.

items.statement: Goal to increase D2C margins over next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Aspiration to achieve double-digit EBITDA margins over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: So, I think that over the course of the next 2 to 3 years, our aspiration would be to get to double-digit EBITDA margins.

items.statement: No further store expansions planned currently.

items.statement: No write-downs anticipated from gold business exit.

items.statement: Expects to fully exit plain gold business in next 6 months.
items.quote: So, I think that there is around INR75 crore invested in the business in terms of capital, which, over the next 6 months, we expect to be able to fully exit.

items.statement: Expects 50% increase in Irasva revenues this year with close to breakeven.
items.quote: So, I think with the introduction of lab-grown diamonds and the weighted average margins going up, the current business plan is for a 50% increase in revenues this year with expectation of close to breakeven or slight profitability based on which we will increase the store network in the following year.

items.statement: Expects high double-digit growth for U.S. brand segment in coming year.
items.quote: But our expectations would be that we would continue with high double-digit growth for the U.S. brand segment for the coming year.

items.statement: Expects return on equity in next 2 years.
items.quote: However, our expectation would be that in the next 2 years, we'd like to be in the 15% to 20% kind of return on equity rate.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to be in range going forward.

items.statement: Seeing strong green shoots of demand recovery in the U.S.
items.quote: I think with inflation coming down, we are seeing strong green shoots of demand recovery in the U.S. which is indicated by our factory order book, as of April 1 was about 25% higher than what it was 1 year ago.

items.statement: Introducing lab-grown diamonds in all Licensed Brands.
items.quote: We're also in the process of introducing lab-grown diamonds in all our Licensed Brands as well.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth, hoping closer to 15% this year.

items.statement: Will not take future orders with less than 7%-8% EBITDA margin in project business.
items.quote: We are very clear that we will not take any future order, which will give a margin of less than 7%-8% on an EBITDA basis. In the project business.

items.statement: Capital plan not affirmed, but expects around INR50 crores plus.
items.quote: So the capital plan is not yet affirmed, but we expect somewhere in the region of INR50 crores plus.

items.statement: Expects order booking much more than last year.

items.statement: Overall demand trend encouraging, inquiry position robust, export inquiries picked up.
items.quote: The overall demand trend is encouraging, and the inquiry position continues to be robust, export inquiries have also picked up.

items.statement: Adopted strategy of not going into very long-duration projects, focusing on low duration and high-technology linked projects.

items.statement: Commodity price risk mitigated to some extent due to shorter project duration and faster ordering cycle.

But because the duration of the projects is much shorter and our ordering cycle is faster now, if somebody gives us an order, we are able to order on our vendors faster.

items.statement: Aspiring for 11%-12% EBITDA margin in 3-4 years, practically possible.
items.quote: Yes, we are aspiring for that, it looks to be practically possible.

items.quote: In fact, I believe that -- by the end of this year, we will be back to our average level of margins that we have seen in the last few years, which is around INR7 per liter.

items.statement: Prestige & Above expected to reach EBITDA breakeven in 12 to 24 months.
items.quote: So over the next 12 to 24 months, we expect to be at a breakeven position net of all of this playing out.

items.statement: Annual investment in Prestige & Above business to be around INR25 crores or less.
items.quote: Having said that, we are still maintaining a view that annually, our investment in this business will be Circa INR25 crores or less. And that is what we are aiming for.

items.statement: Beer JV expects launch in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: No brewery investment planned for at least a couple of years; will stay contract brewed.
items.quote: So I don't foresee an investment in a brewery in a hurry. When we get to a certain scale, and I believe that scale is somewhere around 1 million to 2 million cases per annum of beer.

items.statement: Bengal and Jharkhand 60 KLPD plants to add INR215-230 crores revenue.
items.quote: Yes, Bengal and Jharkhand, 60 KLPD will give you an additional revenue of anything between INR215 crores to INR230 crores.

items.quote: No, we don't expect further drop in margins. We are, in fact, expecting a growth in margins on the back of maize being the new maize crop and the success of maize for production of ethanol.

items.quote: Yes. So ENA business is great in that sense, right, because you were able to pass on your costs. So ENA business has remained in that manner. On the other hand, ethanol is a fixed price business.

items.statement: 25-30 bps increase in borrowing costs can be absorbed or passed on to customers.
items.quote: And 25, 30 basis points increase. And our return on assets can easily absorb. If we want, we can pass on to the customers also.

items.statement: May pass on incremental borrowing costs to borrowers if rates rise.
