items.statement: Sees good growth in April and May despite cash limit regulation.
items.quote: And we have seen -- even after this in April, May, we have seen a good growth in these months also.

items.statement: Vehicle loan business prospects muted due to crowded sector.

items.quote: It's INR162 crores. Total INR892 crores.

items.statement: Raised INR480 crores through public issue of secured NCDs.

items.quote: As far as the book size is concerned we are expecting 8 to 10x growth in the next 3 years and we should have a very healthy increase in the PAT and the EPS in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Targets 100-120 corporate partnerships for EVA by end of FY25
items.quote: We plan to increase it to 100 this thing by end of this year. 100 to 120, you know, whatever maximum we can go.

items.statement: Expects EVA disbursements to scale 7x-8x by end of FY25 from current ~INR1 crore/month
items.quote: We are clocking close to 1 crore in disbursement in this month. And we expect to scale it to almost 7x to 8x by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin will go up driven by high-return EVA product
items.quote: Yes definitely EBITDA margin will go up.

items.statement: Plans to open offices in Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore for EVA corporate sourcing
items.quote: We are planning to open an office in Delhi, Bangalore and maybe later going to say Bombay. For sourcing more corporates for the EVA product.

items.quote: Mauritius Fund has invested about INR10 crores in our share of the warrants issue, INR2.5 crores they already put in. And I think then, say, before the end of the next, this thing, half year closing, they put the balance of INR7.5 crores.

items.statement: Main challenge is corporate onboarding taking ~1.5 months and low product awareness
items.quote: That is a major challenge. That is what onboarding an employer takes about one and a half months with currently with us.

items.statement: EVA charges 2-2.5% upfront processing fee; business loans at 17-18%
items.quote: We charge about 2%, or 2.5% processing fees is deducted upfront.

items.statement: SBI sanctioned INR15 crore limit at 10.95%; debt-to-equity target 2:1
items.quote: Last year we were sanctioned limit by State Bank of India. And they have sanctioned a INR15 crore limit. Out of that, we have just placed only INR6 crores.

items.statement: Announcing one or two new business lines in 7-10 days
items.quote: I think we should be able to tell the exchange in the next 7-10 days.

items.statement: Maintains about 20% revenue growth for FY25, with some revenue from particle board plant.
items.quote: So on the guidance, I think we still are maintaining about a 20% revenue growth with some value of revenue coming in from the particle board plant.

items.statement: Particle board unit capex expected at INR250-275 crores this year, plus INR50 crores maintenance capex.
items.quote: So this year, since the particle board unit is under implementation, so we expect around INR250 crores, INR275 crores in this year and another around INR50 crores of maintenance capex in this year.

items.statement: Peak net debt expected at INR925-950 crores this year.
items.quote: We expect it to be in the range of around INR925 crores to INR950 crores in this year. That will be the peak debt -- peak net debt, which we are hoping.

items.statement: Laminate margin to continue at current level, around 16%.
items.quote: So in the Laminate, we have already mentioned that margin, which is there, we would like to continue with this margin, what we are as of now we are having. And we believe that we will be able to maintain this margin.

items.statement: Blended margin to remain in current range or improve as new categories stabilize.
items.quote: The blended margin this year is at 12.8%, and we believe that this should be in this range, or it will go up as and when the new product category, which we are into, may stabilize and start contributing more in terms of the margin.

items.statement: Expects double-digit volume growth in laminates over next few years.
items.quote: And on the outlook, we think we should grow in double digits in volume over the next few years.

items.statement: No price hikes planned for laminates and veneer; price hikes planned for plywood.
items.quote: So no price hikes have been planned for Lam and Allied and Veneer Allied. Price hikes have been planned for plywood business.

items.statement: Particle board utilization expected at 50% in year 2 and 70-75% in year 3.
items.quote: Year 2, we are budgeting around 50%, and year 3 is around 70%, 75%.

items.statement: Particle board expected to achieve 20-24% margin in fourth year of operation.
items.quote: And again, the margin will depend upon the overall -- how the price move, both in terms of the raw material. And as you know, because right now, the timber prices are on a higher mode and how the price movement happens into the sales price also, but we are expecting this to happen, the 20%, 25% -- 20%, 24% within fourth year of operation.

items.statement: Timber prices increasing in plywood segment.
items.quote: The timber prices, yes, correct, is going up in the plywood segment. That's what the commentary from the other players also. But yes, it is going up. It has gone up in the South Zone as well as, I believe, in the North also.

items.statement: Particle board plant commercial production delayed from Q2 to Q3.
items.quote: We've extended the commencement of commercial production from Q2 to Q3. Our endeavour is to start it at the earliest.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expected to remain in 60-65 days range.
items.quote: We believe it should be in the range of 60, 65 days only what we are at present.

items.statement: Particle board plant expected to break even at 40-50% utilization.
items.quote: If it is depending upon the raw material prices, it should be within 40% to 50%.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion possible in laminate plants, 6-8 production lines.
items.quote: I think we've said this earlier; we can put up to -- anything between 6 to 8 production lines in both the plants.

items.statement: One laminate production line capex around INR40-50 crores.
items.quote: Again, normally, the 1-line capex, if it is only for the line, then it ranges in around INR40 crores, INR50 crores.

items.statement: Revenue growth to be volume-led, better than market growth rate.
items.quote: So, look, our revenue growth in last few years is primarily driven by two-third by volume growth and will continue the same trend going forward, it will be largely driven by volume.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement expected to continue due to service mix, payer mix, and operating leverage.
items.quote: EBITDA margin that we see in Q4 is on account of better service mix and a payer mix and operating leverage due to a strong revenue growth. We expect that to continue going forward.

items.statement: Maintenance capex guided at Rs 65-70 crores.
items.quote: As far as the maintenance CAPEX is concerned, we have always guided, and our maintenance CAPEX will be around 65 to 70 crores and 70 crores is the number which you saw for FY'24 as well.

items.statement: North Bangalore center total capex estimated at Rs 90 crores, spent over current and next financial year.
items.quote: North Bangalore, the total CAPEX is estimated is around 90 crores which largely would be spent in the current year and of course in the next financial year.

items.statement: Effective tax rate for FY25 expected between 35% to 39%.
items.quote: Somewhere between 35% to 39%.

items.statement: Adding 350 to 400 beds in existing hospitals over next four to five years, mostly completed in three years.
items.quote: In total, across our current hospitals, we are looking at adding about 350 to 400 beds in our existing hospitals in the next four to five years. Most of that will get completed in the next three years.

items.statement: Two new hospitals in Bangalore with total 125 beds to be operational in next 12 to 15 months.
items.quote: We are currently in the process of establishing two hospitals with total 125 beds in North Bangalore and Whitefield area , slated to be operational in the next 12 to 15 months.

items.statement: South Mumbai expected to break even in middle of the year.
items.quote: South Mumbai has reduced the losses and is expected to start breaking even sometime in the middle of the year.

items.statement: Kolkata center started contributing positive EBITDA and will continue to grow.
items.quote: Kolkata has started contributing positive EBITDA. It will continue to grow going forward.

items.statement: Rising incidence of cancer expected in coming decade due to population and lifestyle.
items.quote: Given the population of India and more recognition of cancer and lifestyle disease, there is definitely going to be a rising incidence of cancer in the coming decade.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 75% year-on-year in FY24 and will be important growth driver.
items.quote: Our digital revenue has grown 75% year-on-year in FY'24 and will continue to be an important driver of growth in future.

items.statement: Doctor attrition low at less than 5%, not expected to be an issue.
items.quote: our top doctors’ attrition is very low, less than 5%. So, we have been very proud and even today because of the way we empower the doctors, we are involved in academics and research. Our attrition has not been a major issue and we don't expect it to be an issue at all.

items.statement: Planning to introduce MR LINAC Radiation Therapy in Bangalore.
items.quote: We plan to introduce MR LINAC Radiation Therapy in Bangalore, which would be a notable addition to the vastly superior radiation treatment offering at a HCGwhich will help us revolutionize radiation therapy in the state.

items.statement: Institutional Research Committee established to fund investigator-initiated trials.
items.quote: We have established an Institutional Research Committee to fund investigator-initiated trials, which is one-of-a-kind in the Indian private health sector.

items.statement: Mortality rate now under 1%.
items.quote: We're happy to report that our mortality rate as we measure while we are one of the few measuring it has now come under 1% over the years , the feat we are immensely proud of and definitely meeting or beating the global standards.

items.statement: Management expects to consistently deliver growth, with multi-year contracts for next year higher than current numbers.
items.quote: We do believe that we should be able to consistently deliver the necessary growth. We do have multi year contracts. The contracts in the next year are much higher than, the current numbers that we have done.

items.statement: Management does not expect margins to go down year-on-year due to favorable factors.
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, we do not believe that our margins will at all go down because everything is in favor the exchange rates are in favor, the productivity is in favor, reusable components and tools are in favor.

items.statement: Capex is not a large portion of growth; investment in subsidiaries, new markets, acquisitions, and scale-up startups is planned.
items.quote: Capex does not remain a very large portion of where the growth is done but investment does happen in creating subsidiaries, reaching out to new mark ets, reaching out to creating acquisitions or investments into scale-up startups and so on and so forth which do remain as some of the immediate strategies that we'll be aligning with very soon.

items.statement: Management aims to have more signed contracts for the next year before the current financial year ends.
items.quote: So, what we continuously and consistently try and achieve is that we have more signed contracts in hand for the next year before we end the current financial year.

items.statement: Management plans to grow cybersecurity practice and set up Security Operations Centers in India and the Netherlands.
items.quote: Shortly, we'll be setting up a Securities Oper ations Center, a SOC, in both India and the Netherlands. This is where a fa ir amount of investment will also happen.

items.statement: Management identifies global market risks and mitigates with active treasury, diversification, and customer concentration limits.
items.quote: So, what do we do to mitigate these risks? Well, you do have very active treasury functions, one on your FX. So, we at least make sure that we are fairly covered for at least 3 years.

items.statement: Management sees no dearth of business if tech and talent are built, with high entry barriers in target markets.
items.quote: And if we can build more tech and talent, there is no dearth of business. So the spaces where we operate in is more dependent upon having the quality of talent and the quality of consulting capabilities and quality of innovative models and things that we take to our customers.

items.statement: Management expects onsite talent addition to increase costs and substantially increase billing rates.
items.quote: We're also adding a lot of talent onsite on global teams in local countries as well, which will increase costs, which will increase our billing rates substantially.

items.statement: Management plans to grow team size from 400 to more than double in the next 12 months.
items.quote: So, we are fairly geared at this point of time to grow from 400 to more than double in the next 12 months.

items.statement: Management expects to add 40% to 60% of team size year-on-year.
items.quote: You can see from, we do believe that on a year-on-year basis, we do add between 40%, to 60% of our team size.

items.statement: Management expects R&D spend to be 4% to 4.5% of revenue.
items.quote: So, you can say that maybe between 4% to 4.5% random numbers I'm giving you 4% to 4.5% of the revenue you can expect it to be going into training and upgradation and research and so on.

items.statement: Management expects R&D spend in FY24 to be around INR4 crores to INR5 crores.
items.quote: Around INR4 crores to INR5 crores, yes.

items.statement: Management aims for onsite team to be 20%-30% in times to come.
items.quote: No, onsite at this point of time is growing and we are consistently working towards making our onsite team to be between 20%-30% in times to come.

items.statement: Management states no short-term plans to become a product company.
items.quote: And as far as your question whether we are keen to make a product of our own at this point of time, there is no short term plans around being a product Company.

items.statement: Management expects to remain export-focused with 95% exports and 5% domestic.
items.quote: Currently, 95% of what we do is exports and 5% is domestic. And domestic is because of during the COVID time, we didn't pick up.

items.statement: Expects 6-7% growth from store expansion.
items.quote: We will be opening around 25 COCO and around 70 Franchisees. So , we expect in our value terms, around 6% to 7% growth from this expansion.

items.statement: Plans annual retail growth of 12-15% and EBITDA margin of 16-17%.
items.quote: We have an annual growth plan of around 12 %- 15% in the retail segment. And we are having an EBITDA margin of around 16% to 17%.

items.statement: Targets retail revenue of ₹650-700 crores and EBITDA margin of 17-18%.
items.quote: So with the growth coming back in the retail , we expect to be around ₹ 650 crores to ₹ 700 crores in retail and EBITDA margin of around 17% to 18%.

items.statement: Expects margin to improve with softening raw material prices.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect our margins to improve with the softening of key raw material prices.

items.statement: Margin will be more or less same as no price hikes.
items.quote: Margin will be more or less same because we're not taking any price hikes. We want to increase the volume.

items.statement: With sales growth, expects margin improvement of 100 basis points.
items.quote: So , definitely, with the sales growth coming, we'll definitely improve the margin by 100 basis points.

items.statement: No price hike taken due to muted demand.
items.quote: We have not taken any price hike because, since the demand is muted, again, taking a price hike may also impact the volume.

items.statement: Demand muted due to macro conditions, heat wave, and elections.
items.quote: In regard to demand in retail, it is muted, still , t here are 2-3 reasons for that. One is the macroeconomic conditions, other is that we are basically in the eastern part of the country, where in the month of April, the continuous period of heat wave going on, which has really restricted the footfall in the stores.

items.statement: Expects demand to improve after elections and festive season.
items.quote: I think after the election is over, I think some amount of demand will come back that is expected. And also in the fes tive season, the demand comes .

items.statement: Sports shoes category contributes 10-12% of total.
items.quote: So, when the whole sport shoes category comes, it would be around 10% to 12% of our total contribution.

items.statement: Pro brand contributes 17-20% of total.
items.quote: So , Pro as a brand would be 17% to 20% but Sport shoes would be around this 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Sub-brands increased to 59% this year from 57% last year.
items.quote: The sub-brands last year was around 57% and this year, it is around 59%.

items.statement: Plans to open 25 COCO and 70 franchisee stores.
items.quote: We will be opening around 25 COCO and around 70 Franchisees.

items.statement: Plans to refurbish 22 stores this year.
items.quote: Around 22 stores will be refurbished this year.

items.statement: BIS inventory liquidation ongoing; some stock remains.
items.quote: No. BIS inventory, there has been time given to liquidate the stock also. So , most of the stocks have been sold. Some stocks are there.

items.statement: Demerger pending NCLT approval, expected in 3-4 months.
items.quote: We have received approval from the BSE & NSE and now the matter is presently pending with NCLT. So, another 3 to 4 months it will take to get the demerger order.

items.statement: Aiming for appreciable growth in EBITDA and PAT in FY25 versus FY24; will try to defend margins near current levels
items.quote: So I think FY25, we are confident that you will see an appreciable growth in the EBITDA and the profit vis-à-vis FY24.

items.statement: Will not provide specific top-line growth numbers; focus is on bottom-line growth
items.quote: I would not like to speculate in specific numbers. It's early on, but I can say with confidence that we are a bottom line-driven company as I always have been saying in my previous interactions.

items.statement: Order book as of 31 March 2024 was INR 5,700 crore; Bangladesh order of INR 915 crore added in April
items.quote: The order book as of 31st March is INR5,700 crore. Consultancy is INR2,600 crore. Turnkey is INR2,500 crore. Export is the order of Mozambique, which is about INR300 crore, and the balance leasing and subsidiary, et cetera, is INR300 crore.

items.statement: Two export orders received: INR 300 crore Mozambique (10 locomotives) and INR 915 crore Bangladesh (200 coaches)
items.quote: The first one was to try aggressively and get at least one export order, which we had not got for the last 4 years and we got 2 orders of INR1,200 crore Mozambique plus Bangladesh.

items.statement: Capex will remain in the range of INR 100-140 crore annually
items.quote: Two, we are a low capex company. Our capex will always be in the range of INR100-odd crore, INR130 crore to INR140 crore, as you see from the trend.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin ~27% and PAT margin ~20% in Q4; consultancy margin ~45%; aim to defend margins near these levels
items.quote: As you see the trend also in Q4, we've been able to hold on to on a consolidated basis, EBITDA margins of about 27% plus; PAT margins of 20% plus. And consultancy margins have been in the range of about 45%, now on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Export margins on new global tenders will be much tighter than previous 20-25% range
items.quote: But fact that getting these orders on global tenders, the margins will be much, much tighter than the erstwhile export margins, which were in the range of 20%, 25%.

items.statement: Turnkey project margins range 3-4%
items.quote: Turnkey business by nature have a margin ranging from 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Maintaining 'one order a day' pace; 100+ orders worth INR 940 crore in Q4; healthy order inflow across sectors
items.quote: We got 100-plus orders totaling to INR940 crore. And the way the trend is, these orders both export and consultancy orders, which we have been getting across sectors, I think we are confident that the FY24, which is a year of consolidation.

items.statement: QA business client mix flipped from 2/3 IR to >50% non-IR by end of FY24; new orders from defence, power, urban infra, PM Vishwakarma (INR 67 crore), GeM (INR 14-15 crore)
items.quote: By the end of Q4, it has changed over that more than 50% to 55% is non-IR clients. We have got some interesting orders across spectrum, whether it is defence, whether it is power distribution, discoms, whether it is the sewage or urban infra or water or PM Vishwakarma quality checks order of INR 67 crore for the tool kits being supplied.

items.statement: Export revenue from Bangladesh coaches expected by Q3/Q4 FY25; locomotives by early FY26; Zimbabwe order progressing slowly
items.quote: In the most conservative scenario also at least latest by Q3, Q4, some revenue realization must start happening. In terms of locomotive, these require a longer time frame in manufacturing. So while the efforts will be on to realize some revenue by end of the FY, that's a huge challenge.

items.statement: Margins under pressure due to shift from nomination to competitive bidding in consultancy and export; competition increasing in leasing business
items.quote: In terms of project consultancy also, both in domestic and international, most of the clients are now going through EOI or tendering more. So in terms of the shift from nomination to competition, every quarter, there has been a shift in that.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio 95.2% for FY24; intend to continue high payouts as earnings grow
items.quote: Our dividend payout ratio has been 95.2% for FY24. And as we grow and as we aim to grow in both our EBITDA PAT, we will continue to give our best to our shareholders.

items.statement: REMC revenue grew 30%+, PAT grew 37%+ in FY24; paid INR 80 crore dividend (99% payout); RTC tenders progressing
items.quote: The revenue, if you look at the entire year, jumped by 30% plus it was the highest ever revenue. The PAT jumped by plus 37% plus. And we gave a huge dividend of about INR 80 crore, and RITES got about 51% of it. So dividend payout ratio was about 99%.

items.statement: Consultancy revenue (consolidated) reached all-time high of ~INR 1,300 crore in FY24, up 10% YoY
items.quote: In fact, the total consultancy revenue (consolidated) reached a figure of about INR1,300 crore, which is an all-time high, which was a huge satisfaction to us because it is moving in the right trend.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue projected at Rs. 2,000 crore in FY25, approximately 2x growth from FY24.
items.quote: In FY '25, on a consolidated basis, Gensol is projected to achieve the milestone of Rs. 2,000 crore revenue, approximately 2x growth from what we did in FY '24.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margins expected to remain at 25%-26%.
items.quote: So, I think on the bottom line, we have said that our consolidated EBITDA margins are about 25%-26% We see that we should continue to do the similar kind of numbers.

items.statement: EV manufacturing revenue expected between Rs. 50 and Rs. 100 crores in FY25.
items.quote: And in terms of revenue, we are expecting that we will have a revenue of between Rs. 50 and Rs. 100 crores from EV manufacturing in FY '25.

items.statement: Scorpius Trackers revenue expected to double between FY24 and FY25.
items.quote: The Scorpius Tracker, the revenue from there is expected to actually double between FY '24 and FY '25.

items.statement: Solar order book stands at Rs. 1,448 crores as of FY24 end.
items.quote: Our solar order book stands at Rs. 1,448 crores as on FY '24 end with a big pipeline that far surpasses the number.

items.statement: Scorpius Trackers order book approximately Rs. 100 crores out of total Rs. 1,700 crores.
items.quote: I would not have the exact number, but I can today tell you that approximately out of the Rs. 1,700 crore order books, Scorpius would have about a Rs. 100 crore-ish order book.

items.statement: EV manufacturing plant requires additional CAPEX of Rs. 75-100 crores.
items.quote: think on the EV manufacturing side, it will need between Rs. 75 and 100 crores more and if the EV leasing book will continue to grow by 100% year-on-year

items.statement: India to have over 300 GW solar power by FY30, ensuring no dearth of orders.
items.quote: I think we are seeing that India is going to have some 300 plus gigawatt of solar power by FY '30, which means that there is going to be no dearth of orders for solar, no dearth of orders for battery energy storage systems.

items.statement: EV leasing and solar businesses each expected to contribute half of EBITDA next year.
items.quote: Half of the EBITDA next year will come from the EV leasing business and half of the EBITDA will come from the solar business.

items.statement: Promoter pledges for IREDA and PFC to remain for 2-3 years; some pledges may reduce in six months.
items.quote: So, I think the pledge from IREDA, PFC will only happen at the end of the duration of the debt, which might be between two and three years from the loan that we have taken for investment into promoter, that we have taken to invest in the warrants round. I think that you could see the pledge coming down in about six months' time.

items.statement: Rs. 900 crores fund raise to open in early June; money expected from June.
items.quote: We are going to open up o ur round in the early part of June is when we are going to open up the round. So, there is, we have still not taken the equity

items.statement: EV leasing cost of funds 10%-10.5%, lease cost 14%-15%.
items.quote: One stream of income is the income that we get, which is purely what I can say is the arbitrage which we have, where our cost of funds is between 10%-10.5%, whereas the lease cost is computed at between 14% and 15%.

items.statement: EV leasing book is pristine with no payment delays.
items.quote: But as of even yesterday, I can confirm to you that not even one customer has delayed any payment by even one day on the EV leasing side.

items.statement: Monthly outgo expected to be around Rs. 150 crores this year.
items.quote: So, we are making very prudent decisions when it comes to our treasury operations and hence, you will continue to see that while we maintain our monthly outgo for this particular year is going to be in the range of Rs. 150 crores a month.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity is 2.7, expected to reduce with fund raise.
items.quote: So, our net debt-to-equity is actually 2.7, because the company had about close to Rs. 400 crores plus cash, which was there. Hence, you have to not look at the debt-to-equity, but the net debt-to-equity.

items.statement: Revenue target for excellent rating is around INR10,000-10,500 crores.
items.quote: For excellent rating, the revenue target, I expect to be something around close to INR10,000 crores-INR10,500 crores.

items.statement: Margins should remain in similar range, maybe slight increase.
items.quote: Margins should remain in the similar range, maybe slight increase the government may propose.

items.statement: Capex of INR2,500-3,000 crores over next 3-4 years.
items.quote: We expect INR3,000 crores over next 3 years to 4 years.

items.statement: Additional three submarines order likely finalized this financial year.
items.quote: Yes, we very much believe so.

items.statement: P75I project expected in FY26.
items.quote: FY’26. In the normal course, it should be in FY’26. If it goes beyond, then we feel it is delayed.

items.statement: Pending execution for destroyer project is INR11,216 crores.
items.quote: No, pending execution is INR11,216 crores. The order value was INR32,081 crores. We have already delivered three.

items.statement: Frigate pending execution approximately INR17,000 crores.
items.quote: Frigate would be approximately INR17,000 crores.

items.statement: Total order book around INR38,000 crores.
items.quote: MRLs, medium refit and life certification INR2000 crores, exports INR350 crores and others approximately INR1000 crores to INR1500 crores, total INR38,000 crores.

items.statement: Liquidated damages write-back in Q4 approximately INR141 crores.
items.quote: Approximately INR141 crores.

items.statement: Total LD write-back for FY24 approximately INR300 crores.
items.quote: Approximately INR300 crores.

items.statement: FY25 poised for highest revenue with three deliveries.
items.quote: As far as the current order book is concerned, FY25, clearly we are poised for the, maybe the highest revenue.Yeah, we will be delivering one frigate and one destroyer.Because we are targeting three deliveries during this year, one destroyer, one frigate, as well as one submarine.

items.statement: Revenue trend likely to continue increasing in FY25.
items.quote: Without assigning any figures, I can only say that by 2022, 2023, 2024, our revenues have been increasing every year. And we believe that the same trend is likely to continue for FY’25.

items.statement: Ship repair revenue expected 5-7% of total.
items.quote: Actually, in spite of repairs having a shorter cycle, primarily we are a yard for new build. So, this is -- Our focus area remains on the new build. We don't expect a revenue share of more than 5% to7% from the repair segment.

items.statement: Margins depend on contract nature and execution stage.
items.quote: Both have a totally different scenario with respect to how many players are there in competition or if the order is on nomination, then the margins are predefined. So, lot many factors would come into play when these orders actually crystallize.

items.statement: Free cash around INR4,000 crores.
items.quote: Free cash which belongs to MDL would be around INR4000 crores.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 30% to 35% for FY25 with EBITDA margins around 22%
items.quote: Based on the current estimates, we are expecting increase in revenue guidance of 30% to 35% for FY '25 and EBITDA margins of around 22%.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of minimum 30% to 35% for FY26 with EBITDA margins close to 24% plus
items.quote: We will continue to grow at a minimum of 30% to 35% for FY '26 with improved EBITDA margins close to 24% plus.

items.statement: Year-end order book closed at INR915 crores, expecting closing order book of INR1500 crores by March FY25
items.quote: We have closed the year -end order book at INR915 crores and exp ect to have a closing order book of INR1500 crores by March FY '25.

items.statement: Expecting INR650+ crores of nuclear orders from tenders 5 and 6 plus Tarapur refurbishment, INR70-80 crores from space, and substantial aerospace orders
items.quote: So, totally we are looking at about INR650 plus crores o f orders flowing in. And these orders will be executed in the subsequent financial year.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR70-75 crores for FY25 including existing POs; FY26 capex based on new programs and business case analysis
items.quote: For FY '25, we are looking for around INR70 crores to INR75 crores which includes the already existing POs which issued last year.

items.statement: MNC Aerospace margins start at 20-22% and will improve as operations streamline and cycle times reduce over next year
items.quote: To begin with, we look at margins of 20% to 22% but it would improve as we streamline the operations, as we ramp up.

items.statement: Margins to improve progressively in second half of FY25 and by 2-3% in FY26 as Bloom volumes recover and new verticals streamline
items.quote: The margins would improve over the second half of the year. We are progressively improving our margins because the operating leverage, what we had with Bloom, has reduced right now because of the lower volume.

items.statement: Bloom Energy transition to Santa Cruz model caused temporary procurement reduction; expecting bounce back to higher volumes in second half of FY25
items.quote: We have clear indications that we will bounce back to higher procurement volumes by Bloom during the second half of the year.

items.statement: Bloom forecast for FY25 at 3,300 hot boxes vs 2,752 last year; Intel contract win expected to increase requirements in second half
items.quote: So, basically if you look at our current forecast for the c urrent financial year, we have taken 3,300 units of hot boxes and last year we have done 2,752.

items.statement: MNC Aerospace revenue to grow from INR8 crores in FY24 to ~INR72 crores in FY25; signed IAI agreement worth $90-120M over 15 years
items.quote: For FY '24, we had revenues of 8 crores in MNC Aerospace Division. And for FY '25, the revenues generated will be close to about INR72 crores.

items.statement: Targeting Bloom revenue share to reduce from 70% to 35-40% over 3-4 years; FY26 Bloom revenue expected around INR450-500 crores or less
items.quote: Our aim over the next three to four years is to -- We're not worried about Bloom coming down. Bloom will do the numbers higher and higher. But our target is to bring down diversified to various customers so that the Bloom percentage would come to around 35 % to 40% or even less.

items.statement: No exclusivity with Bloom; can supply to competitors like Ceres Power/Bosch; no solvency risk seen for Bloom given Intel contract and order book
items.quote: We don't have any exclusivity contract with any customers till date. And we have the technology and we have the foundation laid to address any of these technolog ies with any company as and when we take it forward.

items.statement: South Korea localization policy limited impact; still exporting substantially to both South Korea and US
items.quote: So, not only we are supplying to South Korea directly but also to the US. So, that's really not going to change much in terms of the localization.

items.statement: Fluence Energy partnership for domestic projects first; orders tied to tender wins (3 tenders); not factored into FY25 guidance
items.quote: So, everything is tied up with MT AR, but we are just waiting for the orders from Fluence. Whenever they win the tendors they will release the orders to us that's where we are right now.

items.statement: Electrolyzer dispatch of 34 units ongoing; Bloom indicated fresh orders possible in second half; not included in business plan
items.quote: We have about 34 electrolyzers to be dispatched which we are doing part of it this quarter and next quarter, but the Bloom has indicated that once they get the fresh batch of orders for electrolyzers they definitely will move forward with us obviously.

items.statement: SSLV space program with ISRO is 4-5 year project; revenue expected around 2027-28; not entering hydrogen fuel projects directly but will benefit as contract manufacturer
items.quote: So, basically, yes, that's a project by itself which we are working on which is like a 4 to 5 years kind of a project which we are working on with a team of scientists that we are working on right now with our team and it would take that much time to develop the launch vehicle.

items.statement: Maintains 20%+ revenue growth guidance for FY25 on blended portfolio.
items.quote: So, this 20% plus guidance on the revenue growth is on the blended portfolio. This includes our current basket of APIs, some of the new products that we are launching, the CMO activities that we are doing and of course Amarnath.

items.statement: Confident of maintaining 28-30% annualized EBITDA margin.
items.quote: But 28% to 30% is a confident number that we are very assured that we will be able to maintain along with the 20%-plus revenue growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Targets INR1000 crores revenue by FY27 with 18-20% from CMO/CDMO.
items.quote: In the INR1,000 crores we anticipate about 18% to 20% coming in from CMO, CDMO.

items.statement: Plans INR100 crores capex in FY25 for Ambernath, module E, debottlenecking.
items.quote: So we are anticipating about INR100 crores of capex in FY25. This will be mainly for Ambernath as well as some part of the new module E which is coming up.

items.statement: Expects INR200 crores revenue over three years from Brazil registrations.
items.quote: Our anticipation is that in the next three years, because of this registration in Brazil, at least INR200-odd crores we will be able to add to our top line.

items.statement: Anticipates 20-25 metric tons DSM supply in FY25; peak revenue INR60-70 crores.
items.quote: Yes, we are anticipating about 20-25 metric tons of material supply to DSM in FY ‘25.

items.statement: New products to launch by Q3 FY25 in anti-diabetics, anesthetics, anti-anxiety.
items.quote: We expect most of these new products to be launched somewhere around quarter 3 of FY’25.

items.statement: US revenue expected slightly higher this financial year; Europe remains major market for next 2 years.
items.quote: Also in the next few quarters, in fact, for this financial year also, we are anticipating that the contribution from U.S. would be slightly higher than what it is today. Europe will still remain, at least for the next 2 years, Europe will still remain our major market.

items.statement: CMO/CDMO to contribute 20-25% of total revenue in next 3 years.
items.quote: But overall, the CMO, CDMO portfolio that we have in the next 3 years, we anticipate that it should contribute at least 20%, 25% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Ambernath site to be ready by Q2 FY25; commercial production start then.
items.quote: Our site in Ambernath will be ready by Q2 FY '25, where we will be further expanding our CMO and CDMO activities.

items.statement: Module E commissioning end of this month; commercial production by Q2 FY25.
items.quote: So, module E will get commissioned probably end of this month. There was a slight one month delay due to some of the other factors like the construction work getting delayed slightly because of the climatic conditions there. But it will get commissioned end of this month. So, we are anticipating that by quarter 2 of FY’25, we should start commercial production.

items.statement: Ambernath total capex about INR75 crores.
items.quote: It would be about INR75 crores.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 86% for current year; optimal limit reached.
items.quote: See for the current year we were at around 86%. With the E block coming up we believe that since like what Dr. Saloni has already told that we will be able to meet our revenue guidance for next 2 years to 3 years from the existing Lote facility.

items.statement: Oral cancer detection kit expected launch in 2 years after clinical trials.
items.quote: We anticipate that in another 2 years, we will be ready with the final product and the product can be launched in the market, because that is how much time it will take for the clinical trials and everything to be completed.

items.statement: Proposed 40% dividend for FY24 vs 30% last year.
items.quote: This year, we are very pleased to announce that we have proposed 40% dividend as against of 30% last year for all our esteemed shareholders.

items.statement: Expects H1 overall growth of 15% to 20%.
items.quote: So I wouldn't be able to give you the entire guidance for the year right now, but we're expecting H1 to be anywhere between 15% to 20% overall.

items.statement: New hard luggage plant trial runs expected in Q4 this year.
items.quote: I expect that we should be able to take our first trial runs in Q4 of this year. So JFM, Jan, Feb, March quarter is when we are looking at starting with our trial runs.

items.statement: Merger with IIF Overseas effective 1 April 2024.
items.quote: 1 April 2024, so the effective date we've already taken as 1 April.

items.statement: Plans to expand store count to 100 in next two to two and a half years.
items.period: next two to two and a half years
items.quote: I hope that in the next two to two and a half years, we want to take the store count up to, say, 100 stores, at least to begin with.

items.statement: Aims to maintain EBITDA around 11-12% and PAT around 5-6%.
items.quote: About 11%, 12% of EBITDA and 5% to 6% of PAT is something that I have always sort of committed to.

items.statement: Plans to launch own brand, currently in concept stage.
items.quote: So we are looking at launching one brand from our own stable. It is, however, still in the concept stage, product development stage, and we'll do it once I am fairly confident of the product and everything around it and in the due course of time, I will share it with everyone as well.

items.statement: B2C share of e-commerce sales increased to almost 40%.
items.quote: B2C is almost 40% of our overall e-commerce sales.

items.statement: UCB and Aeropostale contribute roughly 10-12% of overall business.
items.quote: Overall share of UCB and Aeropostale is roughly about 10%, 12% in the overall business, and lion's share of that is, again, of UCB because it's all in initial stages.

items.statement: Inventory increase mainly due to new brands, expected to settle in next couple of quarters.
items.quote: So in the next couple of quarters, I see that it should start settling down.

items.statement: Plans 15-20 stores in South India over next two years.
items.quote: I think only in south of India, we could have easily 15 to 20 stores, so very, very focused on that, sir.

items.statement: Logistics cost expected to remain 4-6% of sales.
items.quote: It's always be a percentage and that percentage would always be to the tune of 4% to 6%, whatever ; 4%, 5%, 6% , that's the expense which even today happens and it will continue to be in that zone.

items.statement: With 100 stores, COCO mix expected 40-50%, FOCO 50-60%.
items.quote: So 40% to 50% of the stores would be COCO and 50% to 60% of the stores would be FOCO.

items.statement: Tommy Hilfiger license renewed till December 2026.
items.quote: So we go t renewed till December 2026.

items.statement: Expects 30% CAGR with 15% like-to-like and 15% business development.
items.quote: The rationale was always sort of a 15% like-to-like growth, right, which is when we say like-to-like, it is same counter, same month compared one year to the other year. And another 15 odd percent would come from your business development activities with your new stores, new footprints, new shop in shops, and all of that.

items.statement: CSD channel deliveries started, but controlled due to pricing constraints.
items.quote: First set of deliveries have started, happened in Q4 and initial reports are that we're getting a fairly good response in CSD.

items.statement: FY25 will see a further step-up in performance.
items.quote: I am confident that with disciplined execution of our strategic agenda, FY25 will see a further step-up in our performance.

items.statement: Well-placed to continue to drive growth in FY25 in product and service businesses.
items.quote: If I pull back and summarize all of this, I think we are well-placed to continue to drive growth in FY 25, both in our product business and, indeed, in our service business as well.

items.statement: Expect ASPs to be a source of growth as innovation plays out.
items.quote: More specifically, as the impact of innovation plays out in the coming quarters, we expect ASPs to be a source of growth.

items.statement: Expect ESOP charges to remain stable at these levels in the coming quarter.
items.quote: Q4 employee costs include a non-cash ESOP charge of INR 9.2 crores and we expect the ESOP charges to remain stable at these levels in the coming quarter.

items.statement: No further portfolio restructuring planned; gap in H1 roughly 1.5% then tapers.
items.quote: The portfolio restructuring is over. We do not plan to do any further restructuring for the portfolio. What you have seen in FY24 are essentially remnants of the previous portfolio which has carried forward. This gap that you see would be there for H1 of the coming year but after that it will taper down and even within the H1 of the year the range will be roughly 1.5%.

items.statement: Expect no gap between volume and value growth going forward.
items.quote: We don't expect to have a gap between the volumes and the value growth. items.statement: Initial commodity headwinds seen; focus on accelerating cost reduction.

items.statement: L1 status in projects around INR11,000 crores.
items.quote: Currently, we have L1 in projects -- but exact number, will be around INR11,000 crores.

items.statement: Expects 60-70 million smart meters installed in India this financial year.
items.quote: In this financial year, I personally believe that at least 60 million to 70 million smart meters will be installed.

items.statement: Realistic assumption for 25 crore smart meters target is next four to five years.
items.quote: My realistic assumption will be it will happen in next four to five years.

items.statement: Out of INR19,000 crores platform orders, 75-80% will come back to Genus; of that, 50% supply, 20% installation, 30% O&M.
items.quote: Out of this INR19,000 crores, 80% will come to Genus. And this 80% if you form let's make this 80% at 100%. So then 50% of that 100% would be of supply around 20% will be installation and aro und 30% will be O&M, operation and maintenance

items.statement: O&M margins are comparatively better than supply and installation.
items.quote: in terms of margins definitely, O&M is comparatively better than by supply installation.

items.statement: Adding capacity at Guwahati plant to reach 1.5 crores electronic meters per year.
items.quote: we are adding up some capacity now Guwahati plant. So we will reach to a comfortable level of INR1.5 crores electronic meters every year.

items.statement: Exports expected to be at least INR150 crores this year.
items.quote: Last year also, we did exports of more than INR100 crores, and this year also, we expect to do at least INR150 crores.

items.statement: Working capital intensity to continue for next 6-12 months, then improve.
items.quote: Next 6-12 months, I continue to see that because long projects will come on the ground, FAT/SAT will open and then money will start soon. But next year onwards, I definitely see the working capital intensity getting better for Genus.

items.statement: Bank guarantee exposure more than INR600-700 crores.
items.quote: we have an exposure of more than INR600 -INR700 crores in terms of the bank guarantee.

items.statement: Gas meters opportunity 8-10 crores sold in next 7-8 years.
items.quote: we can see some 8 crores to 10 crores gas meters should be sold in like 7 to 8 years.

items.statement: Smart gas meter price around INR3,000 to INR3,500.
items.quote: And smart gas meter is around INR3,000 to INR3,500.

items.statement: Export margins are better than Indian margins for hardware.
items.quote: Export margins are comparatively better than the Indian margins for hardware.

items.statement: Management targets 30% to 40% consolidated growth for FY25.
items.quote: We are looking at around 30% to 40% growth this financial year.

items.statement: FrogData targeted to grow 100%, but 75-80% growth seen as quite possible.
items.quote: Yes, I mean, we are targeting for 100. We have hired a lot of new salespeople. We are also expanding our geographical reach in the U.S. So , we are targeting 100%, but I think that 75% to 80% growth is quite possible.

items.statement: Internal target to reach 500-crore turnover in three years.
items.quote: See, our internal projections or our internal target in the next three years is to try and reach a 500-crore turnover. It's very, very aggressive. I agree. That's our internal target.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve or remain same as costs stay flat.
items.quote: Yes, because our costs will remain quite flat. So, our margin should actually improve, if not remain the same. We don't expect much of cost expansion in the current year.

items.statement: FrogData has 30-40% margin and pricing increase to drive uptick.
items.quote: We have around 30% to 40% margin in FrogData and we have actually this year increasing pricing on that. So, we should see an uptick on the margins in FrogData business because based on the benefit the dealers are getting, we have decided to increase pricing because I think the market can bear it.

items.statement: Planning to raise funds by divesting 10-15% stake in FrogData at $60-80 million valuation.
items.quote: We are looking at between 10% to 15% and the valuation we are trying to achieve is between 60 to 80 million for the business.

items.statement: Fundraise for FrogData expected to close by end of this calendar year.
items.quote: I would say latest before December this year, definitely, worst case.

items.statement: R&D expenses to remain constant in absolute terms, but fall as percentage of revenue.
items.quote: R&D is always constant, because we keep wo rking on new products, because we are always planning what is going to be relevant five years from today or three years or even 10 years from today. Being a product company, I need to continue investing in new development.

items.statement: FrogData share of revenue increased to 26% and will contribute significantly to top and bottom line.
items.quote: See, over the last three years FrogData share has been increasing. So, in current FY, it's already 26%. Three years back it was hardly a single digit. So, it will contribute significantly to the top line and more significantly to the bottom line going forward.

items.statement: Expects $1 million+ from Stellantis Europe CRM rollout this year.
items.quote: This year, we expect a substantial bump from Stellantis because of the Europe rollout of the CRM. Earlier, they had only done France. So, the billing was less. Now they have mandated a Europe-wide rollout. So, we are expecting a million dollar plus just from this rollout itself coming in this year.

items.statement: Spain expected to generate at least couple of million euros, Germany 4-5 million euros annually once operational.
items.value: couple of million euros; 4-5 million euros
items.quote: Spain should be at least couple of million euros. Germany should be more, 4-5 million euros a year. Once they are fully operational and there is enough people know about us.

items.statement: Tax rate to remain same for two years, then normalize to 25% in FY27.
items.quote: I think it will remain the same. I think only by '26-'27, you start seeing a higher tax rate coming in, kicking in.

items.statement: VR product expected to be ready for market by end of this financial year.
items.quote: We are working on it. There is still some challenges there So, I think by end of this financial year, we should have a product ready for the market.

items.statement: Entering Germany this year, focusing on Germany and Spain for expansion.
items.quote: We are seriously entering Germany this year. We have already entered Spain. Last year, we are increasing our presence there. So, Europe will be a major thrust because there is a huge potential out there, especially for digital.

items.statement: FrogData fundraise to be used for US sales and tech team expansion.
items.quote: It will be used in the U.S. for sales expansion and expansion of the tech team.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue growth expected at 20-25%, including IAC.
items.quote: So I would say that FY '25 at a consolidated level, I would still say that the growth would be anywhere around 20% to 25%. This includes IAC.

items.statement: IAC India expected to grow 15-20% in FY25.
items.quote: Of course, the IAC growth is expected to be somewhere between 15% to 20% on the back of new model launches and cer tain other incremental organic growth of certain recently launched models.

items.statement: Stand-alone entity expected to grow 15-20% in FY25.
items.quote: And again, the stand- alone entity would probably also grow in a similar vicinity of about 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Subsidiaries expected to grow 40-50% in FY25.
items.quote: The subsidiaries will probably grow at a much faster rate. I think overall we are expecting that growth to be maybe around 40% to 50%.

items.statement: FY25 capex for Lumax Auto Technologies expected at INR150-175 crores.
items.quote: But again, to deliver the order book of almost INR 920 crores, as I mentioned, the capex outlay for FY '25 for the Lumax Auto Technologies as a whole would be anywhere between INR150 crores to INR175 crores.

items.statement: IAC India capex outlay around INR50 crores in FY25.
items.quote: I think IAC, as was mentioned earlier, that we are stretched on capacity, and there are already 2 expansions, which are underway, and there is a probably capex outlay of around INR50-odd crores for IAC India in FY '25.

items.statement: Order book of INR900 crores, with 30% maturing in FY25, 55% in FY26, 15% in FY27.
items.quote: Out of the total INR900 crores, 90% is new business. 30% of the order book value will mature in FY '25, 55% in FY '26 and the remaining 15% in FY '27.

items.statement: Stand-alone EBITDA margin expected to grow to around 13% in FY25.
items.quote: In terms of the EBITDA margins of the stand, let's say, without IAC business, we've been consistently hovering at around, a, give or take, 12% EBITDA margin, and we do expect this to grow in the current fiscal FY'25, grow in terms of expansion of margins. I would not be able to give you the exact number, but I would perceive that it should be anywhere closer to 13%.

items.statement: IAC India sustainable EBITDA margin expected at 15-16%.
items.quote: In terms of the margins on IAC, I think, again, on a sustainable basis, I still feel that anywhere between 15% to 16% should be a sustainable EBITDA margin for

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 14-15%.
items.quote: So for FY '25, as just earlier explained, even if we basically consider the one time corrections in financial year'24 due to the expansion in margins of stand- alone entity as just explained by Anmol sir, so we will be looking at a similar margin in FY'25 with respect to FY'24. It will be closer to 14% to 15%.

items.statement: Aftermarket expected to grow 20%+ in FY25.
items.quote: On the aftermarket, as I mentioned, the current year itself, we are looking at anywhere around 20% plus growth and that's largely because we do see a good uptick in the aftermarket, yes, cash flow realization still continues to be a bit of a challenge, but I think this growth is coming largely on new products, which we are going to launch in the aftermarket in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Automatic gear shifters constitute 40-45% in volume and >70% in value.
items.quote: So the penetration of automatic gear shifters has been increasing over the last 5 years. In volume terms, however, it still constitutes around 40% to 45%, but in value terms, it is contributing more than 70% right now.

items.statement: Company evaluating 2-3 acquisition opportunities.
items.quote: As we speak, again, I cannot divulge any details. But yes, the co mpany is always evaluating anywhere between 2 to 3 opportunities, which is the current state as well.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% top-line growth for FY25.
items.quote: So we are anticipating for the next financial year, maybe 20 % to 25% growth on top line. And even the revenue also growth will be probably around 25% conservatively.

items.statement: Anticipates EBITDA margin of about 20% for FY25.
items.quote: EBITDA we are anticipating it to be about 20% . We are planning to increase the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Plans capex of approximately INR150 crores for FY25.
items.quote: Now coming to the business outlook, looking ahead we are excited about our plans for FY25 which include a capex of approximately INR150 crores.

items.statement: Capex funded via internal approvals, term loans, and convertible equity warrants of INR114.3 crores.
items.quote: The capex will be funded through a combination of int ernal approvals, term loans and a recent fundraise via convertible equity warrants amounting to INR114.3 crores.

items.statement: Ibuprofen expected to reach 25-28% of total revenue in FY25.
items.quote: Definitely, I think we are anticipating to touch close to 25% to 28% in the next financial year.

items.statement: Ibuprofen sales expected to increase 30-40% in coming quarter.
items.quote: Definitely, I think there is a good possibility of increasing it by 30% to 40% in the coming quarter. And quarter over quarter, definitely, you will see a growth for this next financial year.

items.statement: Targets INR1200-1300 crores revenue in 3-4 years.
items.quote: Yes, 3, 4 years, that is the target to reach around INR1200-INR1300 crores. That is the target in the next 3-4 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected around 20% in 3-4 years.
items.quote: So yes, definitely, yes, accordingly, I think EBITDA margins will be around 20%.

items.statement: Ibuprofen prices have stabilized and are profitable.
items.quote: Yes. It has stabilized now. The prices are quite stable right now.

items.statement: Pricing is a key risk due to increasing competition and falling prices.
items.quote: Definitely, I think the pricing will be a key issue going forward always, because mar ket is becoming competitive day-by-day, each quarter, and the prices are coming down.

items.statement: ARV demand remains stable and contribution expected at pre-COVID levels.
items.quote: We anticipate maintaining the ARV segment's contribution at pre-COVID levels in the coming years. The demand for ARV products remains stable, supported by a strong market presence and strategic partnerships.

items.statement: Focus on high-margin products and therapeutic segments to improve product mix.
items.quote: Our product mix has improved due to strategic emphasis on high margin products and therapeutic segments that are in high demand in the market.

items.statement: New capex projects to contribute to revenue from FY26.
items.quote: So, we are anticipating the contribution to come in from next financial year, FY26.

items.statement: Ibuprofen capacity utilization target 65% for FY25.
items.quote: Yes. We will definitely hit 65%-70% as a target. But ye s, I think conservatively, we can take 65% as a target.

items.statement: Expects growth in coming year to be much better than last year's 2.5% revenue growth.
items.quote: We had a slightly slow year last year; 2.5% revenue growth is not spectacular, but we hope that with the scaling up of our sales engine across the t hree major geographies, our growth in the coming year will be much better than it was last year

items.statement: South Africa operations to start in Q2 or Q3 FY2024 with a center in Cape Town.
items.quote: We expect to start operations in either Q2 FY2024 or Q3 FY2024 with a center in Cape Town, and we are expecting to be able to support clients, primarily from the UK, North America, and Australia from Cape Town.

items.statement: Colombia center is almost full with about 200 people working there.
items.quote: I am happy to announce that particular center is almost full, and we have about 200 people working for us there.

items.statement: Digital services share of revenues expected to grow organically and inorganically.
items.quote: So, that is the current mix, and we expect that the digital services as a percentage of revenues, are going to grow both organically and inorganically.

items.statement: Share of labor arbitrage driven services will go down as more transformative solutions are implemented.
items.quote: You will find that our share of only labor arbitrage driven services will go down as we implement more transformative solutions around Gen AI, artificial intelligence, and the new technologies such as cybersecurity and all of that.

items.statement: Net cash and treasury surplus to be used for organic growth and strategic acquisitions.
items.quote: So, it is going to be used as a combination for organic growth as well as for acquisitions, which will be strategic in nature and add to our overall capabilities and offerings.

items.statement: Digital television subscriber base grew by just over 8% year-on-year to about 4.43 million.
items.quote: And we have seen traction on that as well, with the base growing by just over 8% year-on-year to about 4.43 million.

items.statement: Retail broadband subscriber base grew 23.8% to about 1.22 million.
items.quote: And I am talking about the retail base growing from about 1 mi llion customers last year to about 1.22 million this year, which is a humongous 23.8% growth in a year

items.statement: Digital television churn is about half of industry's double-digit annual churn.
items.quote: The industry level we know is significant double digits annually, in the low 20s or mid 20s annually, and we have been able to buck the trend and literally half that.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA grew 45.8% in FY2024.
items.quote: Coming to Slide #8, a comparison of FY 2023 with FY2024 shows a very good improvement in operating revenue and even better performance in operating EBITDA, with operating EBITDA improving by 45.8%.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin expanded from 5.4% to 7.7% in FY2024.
items.quote: Operating EBITDA has improved close to 46% on year-on-year basis and at the overall level, our Operating EBITDA margins have expanded again significantly from 5.4% (FY2023) to 7.7% (FY2024).

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin improved from 3.4% to 6% in Q4 FY2024.
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA margins are up from about 3.4% (Q4 FY2023) to 6% in Q4 FY2024.

items.statement: TekLink FY2024 revenue was US$36.6 million with EBITDA of 23.9%.
items.quote: Its revenue for FY2024 was US$36.6 million, with an EBITDA of 23.9% for the fiscal year.

items.statement: Australia acquisition revenue grew 26.3% and EBITDA grew 35.4% in FY2024.
items.quote: In FY2024, revenue grew by 26.3% on a year-on-year basis, but more spectacular was the improvement in EBITDA, which grew by about 35.4% for the year.

items.statement: Net worth is about Rs. 7,643 crore and net cash surplus about Rs. 5,013 crore.
items.quote: Our net worth is about Rs. 7,643 crore. Gross debt is about Rs. 1,306 crore, and we have a net cash and treasury surplus of about Rs. 5,013 crore.

items.statement: Profit of about Rs. 44 crore recognized from sale of optical fiber assets.
items.quote: So in last quarter, we sold optical fibre assets to the subsidiary company called IndusInd Media and Communication, and there was a profit of about Rs. 44 crore that was recognized in other income.

items.statement: Expects NSR to increase 6-7% per ton, reaching INR76,000-77,000.
items.quote: I should see an upward trend happening post september, and I think the average NSR, we should be able to achieve by about 6%- 7% increase per ton. I think the last quarter normally tends to be the best in the industry, and that trend should come back other than the hiccup that you saw in the last quarter of 23- 24.

items.statement: FY25 volume expected at 1,66,000-1,68,000 tons, up 10,000-12,000 tons.
items.quote: FY'25, we will touch about 1,65,000 tons with the implementation of the PM1 and 2 towards the latter part of the year. We should see some increased volumes coming from the commissioning and modernization of these machines.

items.statement: Capex on schedule; part machinery to be commissioned by March 2025, balance in FY26.
items.quote: And with respect to our capex, that's going on schedule. We are advancing on all our orders and discussions -- technical discussions are all over.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin in range of 28-29% going forward.
items.quote: And going forward, I would say that other than about 1% or 2% change either ways we should be able to be in the same range of about 28%, 29%.

items.statement: Specialty paper segment to increase by 5,000-6,000 tons annually, a 20% increase.
items.quote: Yes. We should see -- currently, we are operating at about 15,000 to 20,000 tons annually. We should see an increase of about 5,000 to 6,000 tons from that segment, which is a good 20% increase over the last year.

items.statement: Expects 5% volume growth from new education policy implementation.
items.quote: If they're done in a greater manner so only certain classes and not all , we should expect about a 5% increase in volume growth by the balance of the year.

items.statement: Pulp prices expected to decline to $650-700 per ton in 1-3 years.
items.quote: Future-wise, I would see them settling down around $650 to $700 level should be a decline because there are, I hear of, new capacit ies being created and that would increase the supply of global pulp, and that's why my reason of stating that pulp will normalise or trend at about $600 or $650 to $700 per ton, and will rest at that.

items.statement: Agro pulp costs favorable, expected to continue for at least three months.
items.quote: So we are seeing pretty favourable turns on our agro pulp costs, and that should continue for at least about three-odd months or until the quarter ended September at least.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA to increase by INR250 crores annually from additional capacity.
items.quote: Yes per annum we are expecting our EBITDA to increase value-wise INR250 crores annually.

items.statement: Taking additional debt of INR555 crores for capex.
items.quote: Going forward I don't see any situation or concern at all in repayment situations because even if you are taking this additional debt of INR555 crores there is going to be additional inflow, fund inflow both top line and bottom line the additional capacity that will create.

items.statement: Increased imports and Red Sea crisis impacting exports and pricing.
items.quote: I think basically, the market condition, the industry is in pattern and largely because volumes, the supply side and the demand that is there in the country has been actually accentuated by two issues. One is increased imports into our country from the -- as well as because of the Red Sea crises, our exports have come down from last year.

items.statement: Utilization at 90% of installed capacity, 100% of available machine time.
items.quote: So our utilization overall is about 90% of installed capacity. But other -- if you see differently, it's 100% of machine available time.

items.statement: Targeting capacity of 675 tons per day.
items.quote: So we are targeting reaching 675 tons per day, which will translate to about tons per annum.

items.statement: Capex of INR735 crores to increase capacity to 235,000 tons per annum.
items.quote: So, the INR735 crores is being spent on a variety of plant and machinery equipment. Part of it is going into machine upgradation.

items.statement: Targets order inflow of INR2000-3000 crores in next quarter and INR5000-6000 crores for FY25.
items.quote: The company is targeting an order inflow of INR2000-3000 crores during the next quarter s and however the total order inflow for FY24 is targeting around INR5000-6000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected to be flat, similar to last year's figure.
items.quote: So with all that, I think really if we go -- that's the last year figure that will be the greatest thing what we can do in this. We will try our best in this.

items.statement: Guidance for EBITDA margin between 15%-16% for FY25.
items.quote: but our guidance is between 15%-16% definitely we could be able to deliver.

items.statement: Expects capex of INR100-120 crores for FY25.
items.quote: but we are expecting somewhere around INR100 crores to INR120 crores will be there actually.

items.statement: Plans to infuse INR350 crores equity in FY25, INR90 crores in FY26, and INR64 crores in FY27 for HAM projects.
items.value: INR350 crores, INR90 crores, INR64 crores
items.quote: The additional equity requirement for INR504 crores to be infused as INR350 crores, INR90 crores and INR64 crores for FY25, '26 and '27 respectively.

items.statement: Total order book as of March 31, 2024 is INR5305 crores, excluding INR1200 crores from two HAM projects without appointed date.
items.quote: Now, coming to the order book position, as of March 31, 2024, the company has a total order book position of INR5305 crores.

items.statement: Plans to cut margins by 3% to 4% to win jobs due to market aggression.
items.quote: So, unless if you cut down little bit margins like 2%, 3%, 4% definitely it may not be possible for you to win the job at all, we have a taken some calls by which we were successful in that Mysuru and Ongolu bids and going forward we would like to cut down margins by 3% to 4% I think.

items.statement: Pending receivables from Telangana government amount to INR800 crores, with INR600 crores certified.
items.quote: As of now, the receivables from the Telangana government amount to roughly INR800 crores which include portion awaiting certification.

items.statement: Expects INR70 crores from Vivad Se Vishwas in first half of FY25.
items.quote: are expecting around INR70 crores out of that. So right now, one is there which we are expecting in this year and others is anyway we have gone to the court actually

items.statement: Optimistic about new project awarding after elections and new government.
items.quote: We are optimistic for new project awarding activities after the results are out and the new government takes chair.

items.statement: Exploring new sectors like irrigation, metro, tunnelling, railway, mining, solar for de-risking.
items.quote: We continue to explore new geographical and undertake unconventional projects like irrigation, metro, t unnelling, railway, mining, solar, etc.

items.quote: During Q4 FY24, the company has mad e a provision towards impairment of equity of INR55 crores and towards doubtful advance of INR32 crores and towards doubtful trade receivables of INR10 crores for one of its subsidiary companies i.e., KNR Muzaffarpur Barauni Tollway Private Limited as the toll collection of the project is not sufficient to recover the cost of the maintenance and the debt obligat

items.quote: During the year Q4 FY24, the company received a claim amount of INR135 crores towards principal and INR109 crores towards interest, which were shown in the revenue and other income respectively.

items.statement: Expects consolidated revenue to cross Rs.1200 crore in FY25.
items.quote: And we expect that we would cross at least 1200 crore in 2024-25.

items.statement: Targets consolidated EBITDA margin of 5-10% in FY25.
items.quote: And, and would try to have consolidated EBITDA of not 3%, at least between 5% to 10%.

items.statement: Expects DyStar sale process to conclude by June 2025, with funds received before December 2025.
items.quote: But as management we are expecting the sell process to get concluded well before that and the money should be coming to our account before that, yes.

items.statement: Kiri entitled to receive Rs.603.8 million as priority from DyStar en bloc sale.
items.quote: According to the order Kiri is entitled to receive Rs.603.8 million as the priority from the en block sale of entire shareholding of DyStar.

items.statement: Will pay 10% capital gains tax on DyStar proceeds without indexation.
items.quote: Based on the advice we have as we would not be taking into account the indexing. We will be paying 10% capital gain tax.

items.statement: Minimum IRR hurdle of 25% for new projects, target over 30%.
items.quote: We have minimum IRR that we are looking at is 25% for the new project for the CAPEX, but our target is to have more than 30% IRR on any new projects.

items.statement: Majority of DyStar funds to be used for future growth projects.
items.quote: So, majority of the funds would be utilized for the future , for the growth and for taking Kiri to the new levels.

items.statement: Legal costs to continue until funds are received, though lower than before.
items.quote: So, the engagement of counsel is continuing, the legal cost is incurring, we would not have probably the hearings, so per se, but some legal cost would continue to incur , it would be lesser than the earlier ones, but it would continue to incur some legal cost till the money comes to our account.

items.statement: Senda's appeal to be filed by June 20, 2024, with outcome expected by March 2025.
items.quote: So, from 20th May it would be around 20th of June, that the appeal needs to be filed. So, 30 days’ time is what is t he statutory time to file an appeal.

items.statement: Kiri to file appeal for interest component.
items.quote: We have a legal advice to strongly file an appeal for the interest part which haven’t got so, interest part is an important part and we have a very strong reasoning our belief is strong. So, we will file appeal for the interest.

items.statement: DyStar EBITDA baseline around $150 million; valuation may range 6-10x EBITDA.
items.quote: So, depending on how the buyers recognize it, the valuation may vary from seven times EBITDA to six times EBITDA to even eight, 10 times EBITDA.

items.statement: Multiple buyers interested in DyStar, including strategic and financial funds.
items.quote: So, there is enough interest in the market and there are many prospective buyers at the moment who are interested to be for the company.

items.statement: Capacity utilization: intermediates 36%, dyes <20%, basic chemicals 60%, overall 50%.
items.quote: I give you the exact number, the capacity utilization on intermediate side is 36%, dyes side is less than 20% because we have large capacities and basic chemicals is about 60 % and overall average if you look at all facilities together out of 68,725 tonne we have produced 34,388 tonne so which is about 50% of the production capacity.

items.statement: Lonsen Kiri's fluorine chemistry and Indigo account for over 60% of sales.

items.statement: Targeting mid-teens annualized growth for domestic biscuits in FY25.

items.statement: Aiming for mid-to-high teens annualized growth at company level.
items.quote: So we have been consistently saying that we want to maintain at a company level mid -to-high teens kind of growth, right? And that's what we have achieved this year also. So that's what we are striving for to achieve on a consistent basis on an annualized basis, mid-to-high teens kind of growth.

items.statement: Capex for FY24 and FY25 around INR550-570 crores.
items.quote: So as of now, around INR550 crore, INR560 crores is the capex between the last financial year and this financial year. Last financial year, what we have capex which we have spent and the balance would happen in this financial year.

items.statement: Margins may remain around same level with slight moderation in coming quarter.
items.quote: So yes. It may remain around the same level, right, at this point of time. But yes, the higher contribution of export, we don't expect to continue at the same pace. So there could be some moderation on account of that.

items.statement: Expect demand to recover from Q2 FY25 due to good monsoons and controlled inflation.
items.quote: We all know the good monsoons are projected for this year and the inflation is also coming in control. So we are also very confident that starting quarter 2 of this financial year, we should see the demand coming back and definitely post Diwali, it should be a good run.

items.statement: Competitive intensity led to consumer offers and price drops; company took action in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Premiumization reached 37% in Q4, up 20%.
items.quote: And our premiumization percentage even starting from a part of this year, to quarter 4, we have reached 37%. So there is a 20% jump in the premiumization percent.

items.statement: Red Sea issue may take 1-2 quarters to resolve, impacting working capital.

items.statement: Capex funded two-thirds by debt, one-third by own resources.

items.statement: Project Impact 1.0 cost transformation benefits to start reflecting from Q4 FY25.
items.quote: So that program has just started and it's more on a study and scoping stage. So in terms of benefits to start coming in from this program, it would start reflecting in some manner in quarter 4 of this financial year and then in the subsequent quarters of the next financial year.

items.statement: Margins impacted by change in product mix and one-off expenses.

items.statement: Inventory provision of ₹3.7 crores taken; reversal expected as sales occur.

items.statement: Expects good growth next year, more clarity by Q1-Q2.

items.statement: Does not expect large provisions in FY25; targets normalized EBITDA.

items.statement: SBI order worth INR1100 crores over seven years; execution by H1 FY25 and Q3 FY25.

items.statement: May take debt for SBI project capex and working capital.

items.quote: in Q4 of FY24, the adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 26% versus 24% in Q3 of

items.statement: Anticipates increase in revenue from existing and new customers with new contracts.

items.statement: Digital payments business contributes about 20% of payment solution segment revenue.

items.quote: We have also reduced our debt and the total net debt has come down from INR6,769 million in FY23 to INR5,707 million in FY24.
