items.quote: And our guidance for depreciation is about INR 130 odd crores.

items.statement: Expects margin expansion by about 3 percentage points in FY25 on same revenue.
items.quote: Therefore, we sec a margin expand by about 3 percentage points in FY25 even if we take the same revenue levels.

items.statement: Targets net debt to EBITDA of about 3.5 times by end of FY25.
items.quote: We have stated an objective to get to about 3.5 times Net Debt to EBITDA by end of FY25.

items.statement: Industry can sustain early teen to mid-teen RevPAR growth.
items.quote: When we look at the growth in demand coming in the key markets and we extrapolate that against these very well-known supply growth, there is no reason to believe that the industry cannot sustain. As you rightly said an carly teen to a mid-teen RevPAR growth.

items.statement: Total capex for three hotels about INR 70 crores; INR 30 crores spent, INR 40 crores to be spent next quarter.
items.quote: So only on these three hotels about INR 70 crores was the total capital expenditure. 30 spent, 40 is what we'll spend in the next quarter.

items.statement: Plans to spend INR 25 crores over next two quarters for ACIC integration.
items.quote: So we've already started that work. We believe over the next two quarters we'll spend about INR25 crores in the entire ACIC portfolio for it to be fully integrated.

items.statement: ACIC portfolio expected to deliver asset-level EBITDA of 42% and above.
items.quote: But absolutely we think ACIC portolio should deliver an asset-level EBITDA of 42% and above.

items.statement: ACIC EBITDA margin expected to touch about 41%, 42% in next few quarters.
items.quote: And as we said earlier, we are fairly confident that this number will touch about 41%, 42% in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Expects corporate expense to return to FY23 level of about INR 29 crores in FY25.
items.quote: In FY23 if you realize our corporate overhead was about INR29 crores we are fairly confident that in FY25 we expect the next corporate expense, our net corporate expense fo go back fo the FY23 level which is about INR 29 odd crores.

items.statement: April and May not double-digit RevPAR growth due to elections; good business on books from 15 June onwards.
items.quote: No, not in April and May because of the clections, but we are secing good business on books coming back for 15 June and further on.

items.statement: Bangalore and Hyderabad expected to deliver easily mid-teen RevPAR growth in next 2 years.
items.quote: In terms of absolute RevPAR, we believe Hyderabad still can catch up to Bangalore and therefore can deliver higher growth in the next 2 years, but both these markets put together shouild deliver casily mid-teen RevPAR growth.

items.statement: 300 new rooms to open by beginning of Q3 FY25.
items.quote: So we are ready to open about 300 new rooms in the next few months. This includes the first hotel in Kolkata, rebranding of our hotel in Greater Noida, an addition of 54 rooms to our existing Holiday Inn Express hotel in Bangalore.

items.statement: Expects to accumulate minimum INR 450 crores cash in next few years.
items.quote: If I take the last 6 months run rate of INR100 crores free cash, we xpect to accumulate a mininmum of INR 450 crores of cash in the next few years adding to about INR 260 crores of cash we hold with us today.

items.statement: Expects impairment reversal and deferred tax asset creation during the year.
items.quote: But we arc pretty confident that some bit of reversal will definitely hit both on the impairment reversal as well as creation of deferred tax.

items.statement: Management continues to work towards INR 20 crores profitability from Q1 onwards, may be slightly off.
items.quote: We continue to work towards that Anmol. We've seen good recovery happening in our businesses, while there is a slight impact on account of the slowdown in the capacity, capacity constraints continue to be a bit of a challenge on the B2C side.

items.statement: Expects supply-side constraints to ease starting August and 100-150 incremental aircraft by same quarter next year.
items.quote: We expect supply side constraints to start improving in the second half of the year in fact the indication we ha ve is that starting August we'll start seeing some easing of supply side constrains and by the same quarter of next year we expect almost 100 to 150 incremental aircrafts being in operation.

items.statement: Corporate travel volumes back to pre-COVID levels; IT softness offset by new customer wins.
items.quote: Travel volumes in the IT sector continue to remain soft in the fourth quarter. However, we are pleased to announce that volumes in the corporate segment overall are now back to pre-COVID levels and with IT softness being offset by our customer wins earlier in the year starting to online and picking up volume from other sectors.

items.statement: Sees recovery in most IT services customers in current quarter.
items.quote: Incidentally in the current quarter we've already begun to see recovery in most of our IT services customers as well.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 45% corporate, 55% B2C.
items.quote: In terms of your last point on the mix, our mix today from a pure revenue standpoint it will be almost about 45% coming in from corporate and 55% coming in from B2C.

items.statement: Air ticket pricing elevated due to supply constraints; expects air take rates to improve in H2.
items.quote: The supply-side constraint has also led to an increase in air ticket pricing a nd we see pricing being relatively on the higher side in the current quarter.

items.statement: Expects air take rates to improve in second half as supply constraints ease.
items.quote: With regards to the take rates on the air front, air take rates have remained a bit muted right now because of supply side constraints. We do expect that as the supply side constraints improve in the second half of the year, with more capacity being brough t back both from Indigo and incremental supply that's being added by Air India and Akasa, we do expect air take rates to improve a little bit i

items.statement: Focus on optimizing customer inducement costs on B2C to improve margins.
items.quote: So, on the B2C side, we will continue to look at optimizing our customer inducement cost going forward. We've already started doing that in the last quarter. We've further accelerated that in the current quarter and will continue to do so.

items.statement: Expects hotels growth to improve in H2 with new team and platform enhancements.
items.quote: So, we should see meaningful improvement and growth happening on hotels in the second half of this year as the teams that we've put in place start delivering the numbers that have been projected out for them.

items.statement: No negative surprises expected from one-time effects; normalized environment.
items.quote: So, as I said, now we are in a more normalized environment, and I don't see any kind of surprise coming in , in a normalized environment.

items.statement: Focus on growing corporate travel business and improving profitability.
items.quote: So, our focus is on growing and rebuilding the corporate travel business. So, in the corporate travel business, where we are the market leaders, we will continue to expand our position and focus on driving profitability.

items.statement: Expects benefits from new teams and business lines to accrue in near term.
items.quote: There are new teams that we've built out new lines of business that we have invested behind. And we should start seeing the effect of these coming in the very near term itself.

items.statement: Service cost grows in proportion to packages business; mix impacts ratio.
items.quote: But at the most fundamental level, service cost grows directly in proportion to the growth in packages business.

items.statement: No significant market share gains expected on B2C; focus on maintaining share.
items.quote: On the B2C side, I would expect us to maintain share, but I would not look at significant share gains on the B2C side.

items.statement: Expects strong growth and profitability in corporate travel in coming year.
items.quote: And we expect to see strong growth and profitability in that sector in the coming year as well.

items.statement: Aim to double inventory to 4,780 keys with around 56 hotels over five years.
items.quote: Over the next five years, we aim to double our inventory to 4,780 keys with a plan to open around 56 hotels.

items.statement: Plan to add 23 hotels with 2,385 keys over five years, total 56 hotels and 4,080 keys.
items.quote: Going forward, we plan to add 23 hotels, totalling to 2,385 keys over the next five years, taking the total number of hotels to 56, with keys of 4,080, which is double from the existing level.

items.statement: Plan to add 273 keys across six hotels this year.
items.quote: This year, we plan to add 273 keys across six hotels.

items.statement: Plan to reach 100 Flurys outlets by September and 120-125 by fiscal year end.
items.period: by September this year, end of financial year
items.quote: We plan to reach 100 outlets of Flurys by September this year and reach a target of 120-125 outlets by the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Flurys plans to add 40 to 50 outlets annually over next five years.
items.quote: Flurys plans to add every year 40 to 50 outlets over the next five years.

items.statement: Expect ARR growth in Indian hospitality sector at 12% to 14%, reflecting in results.
items.quote: The ARR growth in the Indian hospitality sector is going to continue at the rate of 12% to 14% and this will also reflect in our results.

items.statement: Expect ARR at Chettinad palace hotel in range of 12,000 to 15,000.
items.quote: We are expecting the ARR to be in the range of 12,000 to 15,000 at Chettinad.

items.statement: Expect ARR at Patiala palace hotel in range of 20,000 to 25,000.
items.quote: And as far as the Patiala hotel is concerned in the range of 20,000 to 25,000.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin for new palace hotels at 40% plus in first year, going to 50%.
items.quote: But considering that this will be the first year of operation, we are expecting the EBITDA to be in the range of 40% plus. Adhidev Chattopadhyay: Okay, thank you. Vijay Dewan: And going forward, we expect because that the EBITDA in these hotels should go to 50

items.statement: Cumulative capex for 600 keys around Rs. 600 crore, with EM bypass generating Rs. 300 crore inward cash flow.
items.quote: The cumulative number is for these 600 keys will be around Rs. 600 crore. That's the standard cumulative numbers one could see out of which EM bypass we will have a Rs. 300 crore inward cash flow also, approximate.

items.statement: Renovation capex about Rs. 45-50 crore per annum; Flurys capex Rs. 100-120 crore over period.
items.quote: And in case of renovation capex, it will be about around Rs. 45-50 crore per annum plus the Flurys will be about Rs. 100-120 crore capex over the period.

items.statement: Park Pune 200 rooms at cost of Rs. 200 crore spread over three years; Vizag 100 rooms at Rs. 100 crore.
items.quote: Three projects, as I mentioned are getting launched, the Pune Hotel, 200 rooms which will be done at a cost of Rs. 200 crore, but that is also spread over three years. Then we have Vishakhapatnam, 100 rooms at Rs. 100 crore and then EM bypass which is self-sufficient.

items.statement: Sale of apartments to add roughly Rs. 100 crore to cash flows every year for next three years.
items.quote: The sale of apartments should add roughly about Rs.100 crore to our cash flows every year for the next three years.

items.statement: Foresee persistent demand-supply imbalance, positioning for double-digit growth; hospitality super-cycle to last over a decade.
items.quote: We foresee a persistent demand-supply imbalance in the industry, especially in the key growth markets, which positions us favourably for anticipated double-digit growth. We are today in the starting phase of the hospitality super-cycle and expect the cycle to last for over a decade, if not more.

items.statement: Plan to add 383 keys on asset-light side next year, including specific hotels.
items.quote: We plan to add about 38 3 keys on the asset-light side of the model next year. FY26 includes about 43 keys in Calcutta, an additional hotel in Indore, 118 keys, Lucknow 100 keys, Alibag 50 keys and Patna 42 keys.

items.statement: Expect to remain net cash positive throughout development cycle using cash accruals and apartment sale proceeds.
items.quote: Our cash accruals rising out of operations and sale proceeds of apartments will keep us net cash positive throughout the development cycle and this is a significant part of our strategy.

items.statement: Confident of delivering 35% to 40% revenue growth in FY25 driven by organic growth of 20% and at least INR1,000 crores of distributed acquisitions.
items.quote: We are very confident of delivering 35% to 40% revenue growth in FY '25 driven by organic growth of 20% against an expected IPM growth of 8% to 10% and at least INR1,000 crores of distributed acquisitions.

items.statement: Expect 100 basis point improvement in EBITDA margins in FY25.
items.quote: This revenue expansion driving operating leverage, apart from our procurement efficiencies and product mix, can help us to deliver 100 basis point improvement in EBITDA margins in FY '25.

items.statement: Plans to acquire at least INR1,000 crores of revenue through acquisitions in FY25.
items.quote: The company plans to acquire at least INR1,000 crores of acquisition in FY’25.

items.statement: Expects INR250 crores to INR300 crores enterprise value for INR1,000 crores of revenue from acquisitions.
items.quote: So you can expect INR250 crores to INR300 crores enterprise value for a thousand crore of revenue in that ballpark range.

items.statement: Aims to reach 200,000-250,000 retail reach in next 2-3 years.
items.quote: our next 2-3 years, if we reach 200,000-250,000 retail reach that will be a substantial reach within the country.

items.statement: Acquired four entities with historical revenues of INR170 crores.
items.quote: We have acquired up to now four entities which had historical revenues of INR170 crores.

items.statement: Expects to add close to INR170 crores plus annualized revenue from four acquisitions.
items.quote: The financial impact of these four acquisitions will be noteworthy as we expect to add close to INR170 crores plus annualized revenue from these acquisitions.

items.statement: Working capital days at 67 days as of March 31, 2024.
items.quote: our working capital days as on 31 st March 2024 stood at 67 days as compared to 64 days last year.

items.statement: Normalized ROCE improved from 6.1% to 10.2%.
items.quote: normalized ROCE improving from 6.1% to 10.2%

items.statement: Normalized return on equity improved to 6% from negative last year.
items.quote: normalized return on equity improved to 6% (to be read as 5.8%) from a negative last year.

items.statement: Operating margin for FY24 at 2.9%, improvement of 91 basis points.
items.quote: Operating margin for FY '24 is at INR2.9%, which is an improvement of 91 basis points compared to last year.

items.statement: Gross margin for FY24 at 9%, improvement of 84 basis points.
items.quote: Gross profit margin stood at 9% for the year, an improvement of 84 basis points from last year.

items.statement: EBITDA for FY24 at INR112 crores, increase of 75% year-on-year.
items.quote: EBITDA for FY '24 is at INR112 crores, an increase of 75% on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: PAT for FY24 at INR40 crores as against loss of INR11 crores last year.
items.quote: PAT for FY '24 is at INR40 crores as against loss of INR11 crores corresponding last year.

items.statement: Revenue for FY24 at INR3,922 crores with growth of 19% year-on-year.
items.quote: revenue for FY '24 is at INR3,922 crores with a growth of 19% on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Engineering business growth expected at least last year's, with subdued projection of 15% to 20%.
items.quote: Yes, we should see a good growth and I am being cautious in giving out exact guidance at this point of time. As you can see that we are carrying a good order book. And I would expect that the growth should be at least what we saw last ye ar. And at the same time, I would only want to give you a subdued projection of roughly around 15% to 20

items.statement: Engineering margins expected to return to FY23 level of 9.1% in FY25.
items.quote: We do expect to improve on this significantly. On a consol basis, we saw for the full year roughly 7.7% margin. And for FY '22-'23, this number was around 9.1%. And we do expect that we will at least come back to that level.

items.statement: Engineering margin drag from unforeseen cost increases expected to continue for 1-2 quarters, then improve.
items.quote: Overall, the rest of the project margins remain healthy. This one contract where we have witnessed unforeseen price increases, we expect the drag would continue for maybe 1 to 2 quarters. And thereafter things should improve significantly.

items.statement: Engineering order book at end of March 2024 stood at Rs. 3,546 crores.
items.quote: At the end of the financial year, March 2024, the total order book for Engineering division stood at Rs. 3,546 crores.

items.statement: Significant international orders won: Saudi Arabia water treatment plant ~Rs. 120 crores, UAE order ~Rs. 250 crores.
items.quote: We've been declaring the significant orders to the Stock Exchanges,. Just to give you a couple of examples, we've got significant orders from Saudi Arabia, which is for setting up a water treatment plant, including demineralization plant. This is roughly around Rs. 120 crores. The other one, is from UAE and that value is roughly in the range of Rs. 250 crores.

items.statement: Domestic enquiry bank robust; finalization of large opportunities expected to accelerate in next few months.
items.quote: The domestic enquiry bank is robust, and we are hopeful that the finalization of some of the large value opportunities would accelerate in the next few months.

items.statement: Chemical segment volumes expected to continue improving over coming year; margins to maintain current levels if global environment and raw material prices stable.
items.quote: Overall, we do see that the volumes in the business would continue to improve over the coming year. And margins also if all things remain equal in terms of the global environment, in terms of the raw material prices, we should be able to maintain the current level and round about these levels.

items.statement: Sequential pickup in international chemical volumes anticipated to continue over coming quarters.
items.quote: There has been a sequential pickup in the volumes from the international market and we anticipate this to continue over the coming quarters also.

items.statement: Middle East situation impacted costs and increased shipping times.
items.quote: But we are seeing a bit of an impact over the last maybe few months due to the situation in the Middle East, which has impacted costs to some extent, and also the shipping times have gone up.

items.statement: UP contract execution delayed due to elections; Q1 FY25 expected to see continuing pressure.
items.quote: I would expect that during Q1 of the current financial year also, we would be seeing continuing pressure because of the elections. And while we anticipated a bit of slowdown, the slowdown was more than what we had anticipated.

items.statement: UP contract expected to be executed by end of this financial year, awaiting resumption after elections.
items.quote: We are expecting by the end of this financial year that contract should be executed, and we await the resumption of pace after the election process has been completed.

items.statement: Mapril revenue impact for full year around Rs. 92 crores; margins lower than standalone chemical segment.
items.quote: On an overall basis for the full year, the revenue impact of Mapril is in the region of around Rs. 92 crores.

items.statement: Consumer business investments to continue; significant volume growth expected, but no timeline for positive bottom line.
items.quote: The investments in ramping up this volume to a much higher level will continue. We do hope that we would be able to start seeing a positive bottom line soon. But as of today, I don't want to give you a gui dance on when exactly. But I can confirm that we will see significant volume growth

items.statement: Working capital levels expected to remain in line with FY23 and FY24 levels going forward.
items.quote: Going forward, we expect that the working capital level to be largely in line with what we have been shown at FY '23 March and also what we are showing now at FY '24.

items.statement: Receivables expected to normalize around midyear.
items.quote: The normalized level, for example, on the receivable side is what you should see around midyear because the end of the year receivables are always at its peak.

items.statement: Engineering segment expected to grow 15% to 20%.
items.quote: And given that we are carrying a very healthy order growth, 15% to 20% growth, we will certainly hope to achieve, if not more.

items.statement: Consumer segment expected to maintain similar growth momentum.
items.quote: You would have seen that we have delivered roughly around 31% growth for the current year. And we do expect that we would maintain momentum in a similar range of growth.

items.statement: Chemical segment margins expected at similar levels if stable environment.
items.quote: As far as the Chemical segment is concerned, we should be seeing margins at similar levels as of date, provided that we continue to witness stable prices and the overall dynamics on the geopolitical side do not alter significantly.

items.statement: Chemical segment margins sustainable if stable environment.
items.quote: If we are going to see a stable environment in the future also, the margin levels are sustainable.

items.statement: Total capex for current year around Rs. 115 crores.
items.quote: The total Capex, for the current year is in the region of, Rs. 115 crores.

items.statement: Roha capex for year around Rs. 50 crores, cumulative Rs. 70 crores.
items.quote: Roha, I can share that for the year, the capex is around Rs. 50 crores. And cumulatively, we have spent around Rs. 70 crores.

items.statement: Overall Roha capex just under Rs. 400 crores.
items.quote: Yes. We have indicated earlier also the overall Capex for the Roha is just under Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Roha capex this year around Rs. 250 crores to Rs. 300 crores.
items.quote: We can't be very definitive about that as of today, but it should be around that number of Rs. 250 crores to Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Roha commercialization expected in FY '25-'26.
items.quote: We have mentioned in the earlier con call that we are expecting the commercialization in FY '25-'26 of this Roha facility.

items.statement: Roha facility to be fully utilized over next 3 to 4 years.
items.quote: We expect to fully utilize that facility over the next 3 to 4 years once the commercial production commences.

items.statement: Roha project financing: 20% internal accruals, 80% debt.
items.quote: No, as regards financing of the Roha project, 20% of that will be from internal accruals and balance will be debt.

items.statement: International order book as of March '24 end around 27%.
items.quote: International order book as of March '24 end is around 27%.

items.statement: Market size in India expected Rs. 20,000-25,000 crores per year excluding municipal.
items.value: Rs. 20,000 crores to Rs. 25,000 crores per year
items.quote: So if we exclude the municipal segment and also the purely similar construction-oriented jobs coming from the government, we would expect the market size in India to be in the range of around Rs. 20,000 crores to Rs. 25,000 crores per year.

items.statement: Unforeseen cost increase in significant contract impacted Engineering margins.
items.quote: There was one significant contract where we saw an unforeseen cost increase, and we had to, therefore, take that extra cost provision in our books. That has led to an adverse impact on the margins reported by the Engineering division.

items.statement: Working capital normalized level expected 70 to 75 days.
items.quote: So the normalized level, if I understood your question correctly, should be in the region of around 70 to 75 days.

items.statement: Customer advances Rs. 180 crores, unearned revenue Rs. 224 crores as of March end.
items.quote: The customer advance as of March end was around Rs. 180 crores and the unearned revenue was around Rs. 224 crores.

items.statement: Aims 25-30% annual AUM increase, targeting over INR500 crores by FY25 and INR600 crores by FY26.
items.quote: Way forward, we aim to achieve a 25% to 30% annual increase in A UM, with targets surpassing INR500 crores by financial year 2025 and we aim to reach INR600 crores loan book by FY '26.

items.statement: Expects 20-25% growth in P&L and income in the coming year.
items.quote: We are seeing around 20% to 25% growth in the coming year as well, both on the P&L and the income.

items.statement: Total revenue expected around INR80-85 crores conservatively.
items.quote: To be honest, INR100 crores looks tough, but total revenue should be around INR80 crores-INR85 crores at a conservative approach.

items.statement: Plans fresh disbursement of around INR200 crores this year, adding INR120 crores AUM.
items.quote: AUM, yes, definitely we are targeting to add, to disburse around INR200 crores of fresh disbursement this year. And with the rundown every month that we have of principal via collections and closures, we should be adding around INR120-odd crores of fresh AUM to the existing.

items.statement: Aims to reach 75 branches by end of FY25.
items.quote: By the end of financial year '25, we aspire to establish a total of 75 branches, enhancing our market presence and accessibility.

items.statement: Plans to open 4-5 branches in Maharashtra next quarter or Q3.
items.quote: Yes, we will be opening spoke loc ations around the branches that we have already opened and we will be entering Maharashtra very soon. So, we plan to open 4 to 5 branches in Maharashtra by in next quarter if the team joins us on time. Otherwise, in Q3.

items.statement: Plans to tie up with large lenders for micro-housing products this year.
items.quote: We also plan to tie up with a couple of large lenders, large NBFCs or small fina nce banks, for micro-housing products to be added in this year.

items.statement: Cost of borrowings expected 25 basis points lower in FY25.
items.quote: While we have added new lenders this year, majority of the borrowings that have been added in the previous financial year are from very large NBFCs or scheduled banks and small finance banks, which further gives us a broader base to borrow and the cost of borrowings should be around 25 basis points lower in the current financial year now in FY25.

items.statement: NIMs stable at 10.5-11%, expected to continue with slight improvement from vehicle loans.
items.quote: NIMs are around 10.5 t o 11% which have been stable and marginally improved. We see the same kind of NIMs going forward as well. Little bit improvement could be seen if we are able to add a good amount of two -wheeler loan, three -wheeler loan, vehicle loan and electric vehicles portfolio.

items.statement: Interest rates range 16.5-24%, average yield 19.5%.
items.quote: So, our interest rat e starts from 16 .5%, but typical yield on our portfolio is close to about 19.5%. We are also going up to 23 %, 24%. It's all profile based. So, the interest rate range is 16.5%-23%, 24%, but average yield is 19.5%.

items.statement: Foresees higher employee attrition in older geographies as a risk.
items.quote: One of the risks that we foresee is higher attrition in our employees, which is in the older geographies, not in the new geographies. The team has been stable for around 15 to 18 months with us in MP and now Gujarat.

items.statement: Gross NPA 2.6%, net NPA 0.36%, expects reduction by 25-30 bps by year-end.
items.quote: And we have about 2.6% NPA, gross NPA that we have reported this year with a very comfortable provisional coverage on that. And net NPA is 0.36%. So we have done a very conservative approach there and we do n't see further slippages there. In fact, with the addition in the AUM, this number should come down by 25 to 30 basis points by end of this year.

items.statement: Plans to introduce electric vehicles and two-wheelers in vehicle loan segment.
items.quote: Furthermore, our commitment to innovation extends to introducing a new product portfolio, including electric vehicles and two -wheelers in the vehicle loan segment, to better serve our customers and drive continuous success in the evolving market landscape.

items.statement: Rights issue deferred; may consider later after AUM reaches INR500 crores.
items.quote: So we have given intimation for the rights issue, but later we deferred this agenda. The proposal was placed for the Board of Directors, but the management along with the Independent Directors of the company were in the opinion to defer the proposal of issuance of rights issue at a later date and for consideration at an appropriate time.

items.statement: Considering issuance of NCDs soon.
items.quote: Apart from that, we are also thinking of issuance of NCDs very soon. But as of now, it's completely through banks and NBFCs via the mode of term loans or small working capital limits from a couple of banks.

items.statement: Branch setup cost INR2-3 lakhs per branch, breakeven in 5-6 months.
items.quote: So, each of our branch within 6 months, 5-6 months is very given on its own. The basic infra that our branches are designed by are couple of lakhs is more than enough to get a branch ready.

items.statement: Expects to reach 100 crore capital commitment by first half of FY25.
items.quote: We are confident that by the first half of 2025, we will reach 1 00 crore capital commitment from our various partners. We have already made significant progress towards this, with almost 65 to 70 crores as of today.

items.statement: NCD of 15 crores fully committed, expected to be allocated within 30 days.
items.quote: Regarding the fundraise, I am sure some of you saw our announcement on the Bombay Stock Exchange about raising an NCD worth about 15 crores. We have been blown away by the response from subscribers.

items.statement: Expects significantly better ROEs this year versus last year.
items.quote: Obviously, compared to last year, I'm expecting this year for us to have significantly better ROEs, largely because when I compare it to last year versus this year, obviously this year we're expecting our capital to be significantly well deployed.

items.statement: ROI charged to partners typically 16.5% to 18%.
items.quote: So the capital commitment, you know, ROI that we basically typically charge could be anywhere between 16.5% to 18%. That's typically the range of ROI that a polo charges.

items.statement: NCDs raised so far below 12-13%.
items.quote: But I think today, as of now, in terms of NCDs, at least when we've raised, right? It's all been below 12-13%, right?

items.statement: Q4 90+ DPD was 2.8%, 90% from discontinued partners; expects lower going forward.
items.quote: I think in terms of NPAs, right? As you disclosed in the presentation, Q4 90 -plus DPD numbers were about 2.8%. But as we spoke about before, right? Over there also, 90% of those DPDs are actually coming from discontinued partners.

items.statement: Expects significant growth over next couple of quarters.
items.quote: We feel that moment is here, and we expect significant growth over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Majority of capital allocation now towards digital NBFCs.
items.quote: We went from primarily working with largely LSPs to, when you look at our capital allocation right now, almost the majority of our allocation being towards digital NBFCs.

items.statement: Sweet spot for loans: ticket size under a couple lakhs, duration 3-12 months.
items.value: less than a couple of lakhs; 3 to 12-month
items.quote: So we like to do loans which are probably less than a couple of lakhs in terms of ticket size, and we also like to keep the duration usually in the 3 to 12 -month range.

items.statement: Employee count may increase from 30 to 35, no significant change.
items.quote: Maybe we'll go from 30 to 35 people, but I don't foresee a significant change in terms of employees.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity currently below 0.5, headroom to go 2-3x.
items.quote: So today, very honestly, you know, our debt is insignificant, right? Like we are not even at 0.5 debt-to-equity.

items.statement: Capital commitment is total capital drawn, earning interest for 12 months.
items.quote: Yes, when I say 100 crores of capital commitment, I mean 100 crores of capital drawn. The loan book, however, can be slightly lower because the money keeps churning.

items.statement: Bulk business EBITDA margin expected to average INR7 per liter over cycle.
items.quote: Going forward, we believe that the bulk business, which is a combination of ENA and ethanol, our EBITDA margins in this business will be at around INR7 a liter. We will see periods of high margins as well as periods of low margins.

items.statement: Expects margin recovery to average INR7 per liter by end of year.
items.quote: In fact, I believe that -- by the end of this year, we will be back to our average level of margins that we have seen in the last few years, which is around INR7 per liter.

items.statement: Expects no further margin drop; expects growth on maize and other segments.
items.quote: No, we don't expect further drop in margins. We are, in fact, expecting a growth in margins on the back of maize being the new maize crop and the success of maize for production of ethanol.

items.statement: No brewery investment planned for at least a couple of years; will stay contract brewed.
items.quote: So for a couple of years at least, we're going to stay as a contract brewed operation.

items.statement: Bengal and Jharkhand 60 KLPD plants to add INR215-230 crores revenue.
items.quote: Yes, Bengal and Jharkhand, 60 KLPD will give you an additional revenue of anything between INR215 crores to INR230 crores.

items.statement: No demand concern for ethanol; can sell all surplus.
items.quote: There is no problem on the demand side for ethanol.

items.statement: Over two-thirds of ethanol production to come from maize this financial year.
items.quote: In this financial year, for ethanol, we expect over 2/3 of our ethanol production to come from maize?

items.statement: ENA business able to pass on costs; ethanol is fixed price.
items.quote: So ENA business is great in that sense, right, because you were able to pass on your costs. So ENA business has remained in that manner. On the other hand, ethanol is a fixed price business.

items.statement: Income tax demand of INR40.93 crores; no provision required per management.
items.quote: The amount of tax demand is INR40.93 crores out of which INR5.3 crores was deposited in Q3. For the balance amount, the company has deposited INR25.11 crores in protest and has gone for appeal.

items.statement: Plans to launch Carib Beer in India in Q1 FY26 via contract manufacturing.
items.quote: We plan to contract manufacture the beer in India to start with, and we expect launch in Q1 of FY'26.

items.statement: Expects Prestige & Above segment to breakeven at EBITDA level in 12-24 months.
items.quote: So over the next 12 to 24 months, we expect to be at a breakeven position net of all of this playing out.

items.statement: Annual investment in Prestige & Above business to be circa INR25 crores or less.
items.quote: Having said that, we are still maintaining a view that annually, our investment in this business will be Circa INR25 crores or less.

items.statement: Expects Regular & Others profitability to continue growing at 18-20% momentum.
items.quote: It's difficult to say right now, but we've demonstrated 18% to 20% kind of growth in profitability last 2, 3 years in Our Regular & Others brands. I hope to continue this momentum.

items.statement: Plans to expand distribution from 6 to 8 states in coming quarters.
items.quote: We are also going to be expanding our distribution presence, which currently stands at 6 states to another 2 states during the coming quarters.

items.statement: Expects strong growth in Prestige & Above segment in current financial year.
items.quote: We continue to ex pect strong growth even in the current financial year on this account, and we expect profitability to improve further as the volume growth con tinue to come in and the route -to-market efficiencies start kicking in through some of the early states

items.statement: Plans to launch Regular & Others brands in Uttar Pradesh in Q2-Q3.
items.quote: I think Q2, Q3 is when you will have the launch of Regular & Others, sometime towards the end of Q2, maybe beginning of Q3.

items.statement: Target AUM for FY25 is ₹780 crores, and for FY26 it will cross ₹1,000 crores.
items.quote: Talking about business projection s, for the financial year 2025, the target AUM is ₹780 crores, and for FY26, the target AUM will cross ₹1,000 crores.

items.statement: Plan to raise equity funds between ₹50 crores and ₹100 crores in FY25.
items.quote: In FY25, we target to raise equity funds between ₹50 crores and ₹100 crores.

items.statement: Targeted branch count for FY25 is 90 branches, and for FY26 aim to cross 100 branches.
items.quote: The targeted branch count for FY25 is 90 branches, and for FY26, we aim to cross 100 branches.

items.statement: Average monthly disbursement target for this year is between ₹30 crores to ₹35 crores.
items.quote: For this year, if we take an average of 25% for the branches, so our average monthly target will be between ₹30 crores to ₹35 crores.

items.statement: Disbursement will be around ₹400 crores, loan book increase around ₹200 crores, AUM between ₹700 crores to ₹780 crores.
items.quote: And our disbursement will be around ₹400 crores hence our loan book will increase around ₹200 crores. And the AUM will be between ₹700 crores to ₹780 crores.

items.statement: Plan to disburse 400 crores solely from existing branches, anticipating AUM of approximately 700 to 800 crores.
items.quote: Our plan is to disburse 400 crores solely from our established branches, while a nticipating an Assets Under Management (AUM) of approximately 700 to 800 crores.

items.statement: Plan to secure ₹50-100 crore in equity during this fiscal year.
items.quote: We've already obtained board approval for the equity raise. Therefore, we plan to secure ₹50-100 crore in equity during this fiscal year

items.statement: Thinking to close equity raise in one or two months as quickly as possible.
items.quote: No, no. So, we are thinking we will close it in one or two months as quickly as possible.

items.statement: If repo rate rises, slight profit decline for fiscal year; if repo rate decreases, profits likely increase.
items.quote: If the repo rate rises, we might experience a slight profit decline for the fiscal year. However, if the repo rate subsequently decreases, our profits will likely increase.

items.statement: As expand and establish 25 to 30 new branches, overall costs will eventually decrease.
items.quote: However, it's crucial to note that as we expand and establish 25 to 30 new branches, our overall costs will eventually decrease.

items.statement: Loan portfolio predominantly rural housing finance, with 94% rural and 6% urban.
items.quote: So, our loan portfolio predominantly focuses on rural housing finance, with 94% allocated to rural areas and only 6% to urban regions across our entire geographic scope.

items.statement: Approximately 74% self-employed and 25% salaried customers.
items.quote: Certainly, within this demographic breakdown, approximately 74% are self-employed individuals, while around 25% are salaried.

items.statement: Loan-to-Value ratio maximum 50%, with slight variations in larger populations.
items.quote: Our Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio stands at a maximum of 50%. In rural areas, the population varies significantly, ranging from as low as 1,000 to as high as 10,000 individuals.

items.statement: For populations below 10,000, maintain 50% LTV; for larger, allow 5% to 10% deviation.
items.quote: For populations below 10,000, we will maintain a 50% threshold. However, for areas with populations exceeding 10,000, we may allow a slight deviation of 5% to 10%.

items.statement: No immediate need for additional equity up to 1,000 to 1,500 crores AUM.
items.quote: With this, we foresee no immediate need for additional equity up to 1,000 to 1,500 crores.

items.statement: Current debt-to-equity ratio is three times.
items.quote: And now our debt-to-equity ratio is three times.

items.statement: EMOSS growth muted over coming quarters due to European economy.
items.quote: The growth at EMOSS would be muted over the coming quarters and should be taken into account considering the general economy in Europe.

items.statement: EMOSS next year or two muted growth, not 30-50% YoY.
items.quote: One is the next couple of quarters or the next year or two is going to be muted growth. I think it's clear from all the macro trends that we see in Europe that it is not going to be the 30%, 40%, 50% kind of year -on-year growth that we have seen at EMOSS in the last 3 years to 4 years.

items.statement: New EMOSS platform to start contributing in next 2 years.
items.quote: But we're developing a platform which will be extremely modular, extremely flexible. We will be working with some of the largest suppliers in the world that will allow us to be extremely competitive on cost and provide some very unique solutions in the European kind of off-highway vehicle application which should start kicking in the next 2 years or so I would say.

items.statement: OEM EV track 2-3 years away.
items.quote: And this needs to be -- this will be the basis of our development for OEM track where we will essentially be using same or similar powertrains to drive our OEM vehicles. So it is still another two to three years away I would say.

items.statement: Non-camshaft components 25% contribution not possible this FY, maybe next year.
items.quote: Yes, I don't think it would be possible in this current financial year, but perhaps a year later would be possible. So, we are still on track to -- we have the customer orders and the business to do it. I think it would be a little bit slower than expected, but it's possible.

items.statement: Domestic market expected to grow 8-10% YoY over next 3-4 years.
items.quote: The domestic market is expected to grow significantly over the next 3 years to 4 years, I would say, 8%, 9%, 10% year -on-year.

items.statement: Double-digit growth not immediate; new contracts to add significantly in 12-24 months.
items.quote: I don't think double digits would be possible immediately in the coming quarters. But I think there will be a point where we have 3 or 4 new contracts that will come into SOP , or basically start supplies all in a very short period of time in the next 12 months to 24 months, let's put it like that. And that will add significantly to top and bottom line.

items.statement: Retrofitting business target 20-25% gross margin, 10-15% operating margin.
items.value: 20%, 25% gross margin and about a 15% operating margin 10% to 15% operating margin
items.quote: At a big picture kind of long term goal if you ask me and we're talking about around a 20%, 25% gross margin and about a 15% operating margin 10% to 15% operating margin is what we hope for.

items.statement: Retrofitting margin profile requires 4,000-5,000 units per year scale.
items.quote: I would say 4,000, 5,000 plus per year.

items.statement: Setting up new assembled camshaft plant in Solapur based on strong order book.
items.quote: In addition, PCL is setting up a new assembled camshaft plant at a new location in Solapur, and these new investments are made on the basis of a strong order book for new assembled camshaft businesses that has been secured along with an addition of past camshaft business.

items.statement: MEMCO to invest in new capex for additional business in coming year.
items.quote: The company would invest in new capex for additional business in the coming year.

items.statement: May open a few retrofitment centers this financial year.
items.quote: Yes, there could be a requirement to open a few centers in this financial year.

items.statement: New business ensures complete capacity utilization for next 4-5 years.
items.quote: In the last year, PCL has been awarded new business in the foundry as well as the machine shop that will ensure complete utilization of our capacities at least for the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: EMOSS India to start commercial sales this quarter with large customers.
items.quote: Yes, we will be starting our commercial sales this quarter itself with some of the very large customers that we have on board. I mean I see a good traction. It would be hard to say how fast the numbers pick up, but we will be starting to sell to a lot of t he customers and across India within this next few months or even starting this quarter.

items.statement: EMOSS India signing commercial agreements with key customers.
items.quote: And while our trials continue, we are happy to share that EMOSS India is in the process of signing commercial agreements with several key customers, including one of India's largest service provider company for the use in waste collection application, one of India's largest biomedical waste management company and an EV -only pan-India logistics provider.

items.statement: Difficult to predict when European recession will end.
items.quote: However, it will be difficult to comment on how long the recessionary environment will last in Europe.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% top line increase for FY25.
items.quote: For the financial year 2024-'25, we would like to guide with a target of 20 to 25 percentage increase in the top line.

items.statement: Expects to sustain EBITDA at previously guided level.
items.quote: We expect to sustain the EBITDA at the level which we have previously guided.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin guidance of 17-19%.
items.quote: But going forward, the blended level, you can expect around the 17% - 19%.

items.statement: Ship repair EBITDA margin guidance of 22-23%.
items.quote: Ship repair, we would like to say 22 to 23 percentage.

items.statement: Additional depreciation from new capex to be INR125-150 crores.
items.quote: Both capacities put together is around INR2,800 crores. So the additional depreciation will be around INR125 crores to INR150 crores, not exact.

items.statement: New dry dock and ISRF to be fully commissioned by August 2024.
items.quote: We are planning to fully commission that project by August '24.

items.statement: Current unexecuted order book approximately INR22,000 crores.
items.quote: As we look towards the future, I'm pleased to inform you that our current order book position is healthy, with approximately INR22,000 crores of unexecuted orders, including the ship repair orders, which typically amounts to a little bit of higher level than earlier times at about INR1,200 crores at this given point of time.

items.statement: Ship repair order book at INR1,250 crores.
items.quote: The ship repair component of order book is about INR1,250 crores, which normally, if you have been following us earlier, we always used to guide about the order book of INR600 crores, INR700 crores.

items.statement: Expects 8-10 green tug orders over next year.
items.quote: We are expecting at least 8 to 10 vessels being ordered over the next year or so by the major ports through private entities and of course we expect to be very much actively parked in those process.

items.statement: Confident of growth for next 5-6 years.
items.quote: So we don't want to talk about peak revenue as a company. We want to continually grow both top line with a steady-state margin levels.

items.statement: PAT to be tempered due to higher depreciation from new projects.
items.quote: Our PAT level will have to be tempered due to the higher depreciation cost from the commissioning of the ISRF and the new dry dock project.

items.statement: Fixed asset turnover expected around 2 for new facilities.
items.quote: It will be around, I don't have the exact numbers right now. It will be around 2, once the operation in both new facilities get stabilised.

items.statement: IAC-2 execution timeline 8-10 years if similar to Vikrant.
items.quote: But whatever we have said on record earlier, if next carrier, when it comes, is largely based on the same or similar platform as what was Vikrant, then we have said we are somewhere around 8 to 10-ish years.

items.statement: Targets 20% consolidated EBITDA margin for FY25, or 19-20% normalized.
items.quote: So as far as financial year '25 is concerned, barring any kind of impact because of the translation, because that is something which obviously we would not be able to know, we believe that a 20% kind of EBITDA margin is what we are looking forward to at a consolidated level.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin expected at 19-20% for FY25.
items.quote: So I think coming back to your question on a normalized basis, a 19% to 20% kind of EBITDA margin is what we'll deem for financial year '25.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is CHF25-30 million.
items.quote: So FY '25 we expect that the capex should be somewhere between 25 million to 30 million.

items.statement: Maintenance capex about CHF18 million, rest for digital transformation and India capex.
items.quote: Yes. So roughly about 18 million would be more of the maintenance expenditure and rest would to complete the digital transformation project as well as I mentioned a certain amount of capex that we need to do between Bavla and Naroda in India. So close to about 25 million is what we expect should be incurred in FY '25.

items.statement: French entity has confirmed orders of EUR9.5 million and expects EUR7 million more.
items.quote: As on 31st of March, we already have confirmed orders of about EUR9.5 million for the French entity. And another EUR7 million of orders are highly expected from the requests of proposals, which have been planned for about EUR90 million.

items.statement: Expects India CRAMS revenue to increase substantially due to regulatory approvals.
items.quote: As now we have all the necessary regulatory approvals, especially from EDQM and a lot of the major market for the India business, we do expect the India CRAMS revenue to increase substantially from hereon.

items.statement: Optimistic for FY24-25 with large POs covering vast majority of business.
items.quote: But as a perspective for this year, '24, '25, we are very, very optimistic as we already have large numbers of POs that's covering the vast majority of our -- that's already in hand, and also very good perspective from the major customer that we have.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth from FY25 onwards.
items.quote: We don't see a reason why we cannot grow in double digits as far as the revenues are concerned.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA and cash flow to grow faster than revenue due to cost controls and no French losses.
items.quote: As far as the EBITDA and the cash flow is concerned that should be growing at a much faster pace largely because one we don't expect the kind of EBITDA loss that we have seen in France to be incurred in the future.

items.statement: Expects wool grease prices to decrease, positively impacting Netherlands margin.
items.quote: So over there, in the current financial year, we are expecting that the prices should come down, and that should have a major impact -- positive impact on the margin in Netherlands for the full financial year.

items.statement: Working on reducing interest cost by borrowing in Swiss francs or swapping loans.
items.quote: But we are already working on different initiatives in order to reduce the interest cost, which would be taking the borrowing in Swiss francs, which would be -- or swapping some of our loans into Swiss franc from U.S., which will help us to reduce the interest cost at a consolidated level.

items.statement: No major capex beyond routine maintenance and one water purification plant from FY25.
items.quote: So apart from the routine maintenance capex and one water purification plant that we are setting up in Bavla we don't see any major capex outlay that should happen from FY '25 onwards.

items.statement: Expects French entity to significantly contribute to consolidated performance from now on.
items.quote: There is no issue on the market side, on the demand side of the product, and we do look forward to French being -- the French entity being a significant contributor to the overall consolidated performance from here on, both in terms of revenue as well as profitability.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue to grow 10-12% in FY25.
items.quote: So FY '25 on a consolidated basis, at a minimum, we should be seeing a 10% kind of growth in the revenue, 10% to 12%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 18-20% for FY25, including French losses.
items.quote: And at an EBITDA level, as I mentioned earlier, close to about 18% to 20% is our target.

items.statement: CRAMS revenue growth of 14-15% expected.
items.quote: So yes, 15% -- 14% to 15% kind of growth in the CRAMS revenue should very much be doable.

items.statement: India CRAMS revenue to reach INR350 crores in FY25, INR400 crores in FY26, and INR450-500 crores thereafter.
items.value: INR350 crores, INR400 crores, INR450 crores to INR500 crores
items.quote: I think as far as the India CRAMS is concerned; we should be closer to about INR350 crores for the full financial year of '25. And so, yes, I mean, we can easily move to INR500 crores, but that would take about 2 years' time. FY '26 is when we can expect we will be closer to INR400 crores as far as the India CRAMS is concerned, and then it could go to INR450 crores to INR500 crores in the year aft

items.statement: UK entity expected to grow 40-50% in FY25 due to lower base.
items.quote: We do expect that the U.K. entity -- just in financial year '25, we do expect a 40% to 50% kind of growth because the base was lower in the last financial year.

items.statement: Swiss entities expected to post 8-10% revenue growth.
items.quote: we do expect that the Swiss entities will keep on posting anywhere between 8% to 10% kind of growth.as far as the revenues are concerned.

items.statement: France revenue expected at $14 million in FY25.
items.quote: France, from what it is doing right now with close to about $14 million of revenue expected in FY '25, and this should also grow substantially in the future.

items.statement: France EBITDA loss to reduce to INR35-40 crores in FY25 from INR100 crores in FY24.
items.quote: we did the INR100 crores of loss in France in FY'24, which in FY'25, we expect that it should be somewhere around INR35 crores to INR40 crores.

items.statement: France breakeven expected in FY26.
items.quote: No, it should be in FY'26.

items.statement: Free cash flow generation expected from FY25, with cash profit INR400-500 crores.
items.quote: we do expect that we should generate free cash flow from financial year '25, and the cash profit should be close to about INR500 crores as far as our cash flow from operations is concerned, INR400 crores, INR500 crores.

items.statement: Net debt expected to reduce over next 2-3 years as free cash flow is generated.
items.quote: as the free cash flow keeps on getting generated, the net debt over the next 2, 3 years should keep on reducing.

items.statement: No major capex program expected; most capex already incurred.
items.quote: So now that all of those things have been completed and most of the assets have been operationalized, we don't expect any major capex to be incurred.

items.statement: PAT to turn positive from FY26.
items.quote: as far as the profit after tax is concerned, that should come positive from FY '26.

items.statement: Development orders in excess of $140 million.
items.quote: currently we are sitting on development orders in excess of 140 million.

items.statement: Q1 and Q2 FY25 expected to be better than Q4 FY24, with stronger H2.
items.quote: Q1, Q2 should be good quarters than what we have seen in Q4 FY '25 but we will see the second half of the year posting on much, much higher growth than what we've seen in the first half.

items.statement: French facility technical issues resolved; orders in hand and $90 million of RFPs sent.
items.quote: there are already orders in hand, there are new orders that are expected, $90 million of RFP, which have gone out.

items.statement: Rate growth this year should not be less than last year.
items.quote: Well, I would say that rate growth this year should not be less than last year.

items.statement: Revenue to grow at least 15% per year for next 3 years.
items.quote: What I can say is for Lemon Tree certainly, we will see at least a 15% increase in revenue every year for the next 3 years.

items.statement: Operational inventory to reach 120+ hotels with over 11,000 rooms by end of FY25.
items.quote: We expect our operational inventory to be about 120 + hotels with over 11,000 rooms by end of FY25.

items.statement: Will spend Rs. 100 crores on renovation this year and next year.
items.quote: But bottom line is that this year, I have said this earlier, we will spend Rs. 100 crores on renovation and next year too.

items.statement: Confident to have 2,000-3,000 more rooms in pipeline this year.
items.quote: I do not think this is guidance when I say that we are very confident that we have 2,000-3,000 more rooms on our pipeline this year.

items.statement: Expect to open 1,200-2,000 rooms this year.
items.quote: And our endeavour is very simple, I can say it will be between from 1,200 - 2,000. Those are the rooms we should open this year.

items.statement: Target EBITDA for Keys is Rs. 60 crore a year minimum, by next October.
items.quote: Our target EBITDA for Keys would be Rs. 60 crore a year, minimum. And I think we will be getting there certainly by next October.

items.statement: Industry price hikes expected 5% to 12% depending on market and hotel quality.
items.quote: Otherwise, typically, the hikes you will see will be depending on the market and depending on the quality of hotel, it could be anywhere from 5% to 12%.

items.statement: Keys average rate to move to Rs. 4,500 by October next year.
items.quote: So , within the next 2 rate cycles, that is by October next year, you will see Keys gradually moving up to Rs. 4,500.

items.statement: Red Fox rate to move north of Rs. 5,000; Lemon Tree and Premier north of Rs. 7,000.
items.quote: Red Fox in my opinion, will move to north of Rs. 5,000 and Lemon Tree and Lemon Tree Premier and all, each of them will be north of Rs. 7,000.

items.statement: Expects structural shift in demand, mid-market to grow, not at cost of luxury.
items.quote: I do think that there will be a big growth in mid-market, but that w ill not necessarily be at the cost of luxury because both these consuming segments or cohorts of Indian customers are going to increase in the next 5 years.

items.statement: Q1 will be much better than Q1 last year for owned company.
items.quote: As far as for the owned company goes, I think Q1 will certainly be much better than Q1 last year.

items.statement: IT hiring slowdown impacts Bangalore and Hyderabad occupancy; expects hiring to start Q3 onwards.
items.quote: Nothing to worry about because we have been giving early indications that IT hiring should start in Q3 onwards. I guess we are quite dependent on that.

items.statement: Debt to be zero within next 4 years; may list Fleur earlier to be debt free sooner.
items.quote: We are very confident that our debt will be 0 within the next 4 years, we will be net debt 0 but should we list Fleur before that, which is something we're thinking about then obviously we will be debt free much earlier because Fleur has roughly 75% of the total debt of the company and while it is consolidated, we own 60% of that company.

items.statement: Renovation expenditure to be recovered in 2 years through incremental EBITDA.
items.quote: I'm giving you a number , that if we have spent Rs. 250 crores in 3 years, then in the following 2 years, we expect to recover it in incremental EBITDA beyond what we would have otherwise achieved.

items.statement: Overall growth expected in the range of 10% to 20%.
items.quote: Yes, there would be -- it would be in the range of 10% to 20% growth.

items.statement: Bidding INR1,000 to INR1,200 crores this year; with 20-30% success, order book could double.
items.quote: So the order book that we are submitting right now is INR1,000 crores. So the bidding happening for this year is INR1,000 to INR1,200 crores.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of INR350 crores to be executed over 2.5 to 3 years.
items.quote: So the INR350 crores unexecuted order book is to be executed in the next 3 years.

items.statement: Office establishment in U.K. planned this year.
items.quote: Definitely, there will be an office establishment in U.K. this year.

items.statement: Expecting work orders from Tanzania, Ghana, and Mozambique; turnaround time 8-9 months.
items.quote: So we are just expecting a few orders from Tanzania, then Ghana and Mozambique, where we are already shortlisted. And since the turnaround time is 8 to 9 months, it takes time to give us the work order.

items.statement: Shortlisted in over 20 bids; another 120 bids yet to be evaluated.
items.quote: In over 20 bids, we have been shortlisted, another 120 bids are yet to be evaluated.

items.statement: Hoping EBITDA margin to grow more due to adding clients and larger projects.
items.quote: Yes. That is why, in fact, we are hoping for this to grow more because we are adding in a lot of clients this time.

items.statement: Targeting large ticket size projects of INR20 crores to INR50 crores.
items.quote: We are not just in international but in domestic market also we are now targeting a large ticket size projects wherein right now, we were getting orders of INR5 crores, INR10 crores, INR15 crores, we will now be getting orders of INR20 crores and above -- INR20 crores to INR50 crores is what we are bidding right now.

items.statement: Working capital cycle: NHAI 45-60 days, MoRTH 90-120 days.
items.quote: So NHAI/MoRTH it is in the range of -- at NHAI it is 45 to 60 days. And for MoRTH, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, it is 90 to 120 days.

items.statement: ECL provision in Q4 approximately INR1.8 crores.
items.quote: It will be approx. INR1.8 crores.

items.statement: Top line would have been INR90 crores to INR95 crores if no elections.
items.quote: INR90 crores to INR95 crores.

items.statement: Expecting work order for Tanzania project around INR50 crores.
items.quote: One is the Tanzania, it is around INR50 crores assignment.

items.statement: Dhaka project value above INR20 crores; financial proposal yet to be submitted.
items.quote: And the -- it is definitely above INR20 crores, but we are yet to submit our financial proposal for this.

items.statement: Expects 40-50% year-on-year growth for next couple of years.
items.quote: So growth, we are looking to continue the current growth trend of 40% to 50% year-on-year for the next couple of years. I mean, 40% on a conservative level, we are hoping to grow for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin of 8.5-9.5% for current financial year.
items.quote: And, as far as EBITDA is concerned, we are expecting EBITDA to be in the range of 8.5% to 9%, 9.5% for the current financial year.

items.statement: Plans to increase ODU capacity by 20% in coming year due to demand.
items.quote: We are also looking at increasing our capacity by about 20% in ODU in the coming year, because of increased demand.

items.statement: Expects 50-70% capacity utilisation in commercial refrigeration next year.
